thread.label: Genesis 3:1-6
thread.text: Now the serpent was more subtil than any beast of the field which the Lord God had made. And he said unto the woman, Yea, hath God said, Ye shall not eat of every tree of the garden?

classes.title: Popular Persuasions: Fighting Against Heaven Defending Earth

precepts.label: Ecclesiastes 3:18
precepts.why:
“Now the serpent was more subtil than any beast of the field which the Lord God had made.” The serpent is counted among the beasts, and in the scriptures the Most High compares men to beasts. Solomon wrote, “I said in mine heart concerning the estate of the sons of men, that God might manifest them, and that they might see that they themselves are beasts.” So the serpent in Genesis 3 is a representation of a man.

He was more subtle than any beast: more crafty, better with his lies, better with his persuasion. Satan’s first weapon was persuasion. Eve was not subdued physically; he did not grab her. He came to her with words. “Yea, hath God said, Ye shall not eat of every tree of the garden?” Notice what he brings: doubt and fear. Eve answered correctly, that God had said “Ye shall not eat of it, neither shall ye touch it, lest ye die.” Then came the doubt: “Ye shall not surely die,” and “ye shall be as gods, knowing good and evil.” She was already meant to be eternal, but he threw doubt in to persuade her to eat.

“she took of the fruit thereof, and did eat, and gave also unto her husband with her; and he did eat.” She was persuaded by the serpent, and then she defiled Adam as well. The serpent used no force; he used words to sway Eve’s perception of reality, and then she went into sin. He went to the woman first, which is why the woman is to learn from her husband at home.

That same serpent spirit is still speaking. Christ told the Pharisees, “Ye are of your father the devil,” “a liar, and the father of it.” The serpent seed came through Cain, and it lives on in Esau, the so-called white man, the pioneer of lying, who persuades the world today through his media and his religion. It is a battle for the minds of the people, and the answer is to stay in the word.

thread.label: Genesis 3:15
thread.text: And I will put enmity between thee and the woman, and between thy seed and her seed; it shall bruise thy head, and thou shalt bruise his heel.

classes.title: Edom's Achilles' Heel

precepts.label: Genesis 4:6-7
precepts.why:
In the garden, before Adam and Eve were put out, God said, “I will put enmity between thee and the woman, and between thy seed and her seed”. Enmity is hatred. Satan has seed on this earth, and the woman’s seed, the descendants who would come through her, is Israel. When that was spoken, Cain was not yet born. The seed of Satan was Cain.

Genesis 4 shows how. “And the Lord said unto Cain, Why art thou wroth? and why is thy countenance fallen? If thou doest well, shalt thou not be accepted?” If you obey me, will you not be accepted by me? But “and if thou doest not well”, if you choose to break my commandments, “sin lieth at the door. And unto thee shall be his desire, and thou shalt rule over him.” The one spoken of there is Satan: Satan would be Cain’s desire, and would rule over him. Satan would be Cain’s god and Cain’s father.

Cain chose not to obey, and he killed Abel. From that moment the enmity of Genesis 3:15 was at work in the earth: the seed of the serpent against the seed of the woman.

It did not end with Cain. His line died in the flood, but all spirits return. Cain came back as Esau, the one who “came out red, all over like an hairy garment”, and Abel, or Seth, came back as Jacob, whose hand took hold on Esau’s heel. So Genesis 3:15 and Genesis 4:7 explain the hatred Edom has for Israel to this day: it is the enmity God put between the two seeds in the beginning.

precepts.label: Genesis 5:3
precepts.why:
“And Adam lived an hundred and thirty years, and begat a son in his own likeness, after his image; and called his name Seth”. Don’t you see something wrong there? Abel was already dead, and Cain was still alive. So why does it never say that Cain was in Adam’s image?

Go back to the making of Adam: “And God said, Let us make man in our image, after our likeness: and let them have dominion over the fish of the sea, and over the fowl of the air, and over the cattle”. Adam, the black man, was made in the image of God. Adam and Eve had Cain and Abel; Cain killed Abel, because God had told him that if he did not do well, sin lay at the door and Satan would rule over him.

Then, when it names the son born “in his own likeness, after his image”, it names Seth, not Cain. People say everybody is in the image of God. No: Cain was not in the image of God, and he is never said to be in Adam’s image.

So whose image was Cain in? John answers it: Cain “was of that wicked one”. Seth was of Adam; Cain was of Satan. That is why the seed of the woman and the seed of the serpent are two different seeds, and why Seth’s line, the line that returns as Jacob, is the one that carries Adam’s image.

precepts.label: 1 John 3:10-12
precepts.why:
“In this the children of God are manifest, and the children of the devil”. There are children of God on the planet, and there are children of the devil on the planet. And “whosoever doeth not righteousness is not of God, neither he that loveth not his brother. For this is the message that ye heard from the beginning, that we should love one another”.

“Not as Cain, who was of that wicked one, and slew his brother.” Wait: we thought Cain was of Adam. It says no. Seth was of Adam; Cain was of that wicked one, of Satan. That is exactly what God told Cain in Genesis 4: unto thee shall be his desire, and he shall rule over thee. “And wherefore slew he him? Because his own works were evil, and his brother’s righteous.”

This is the enmity of Genesis 3:15 made plain: “between thy seed and her seed”. Satan’s seed is Cain, the children of the devil, and her seed is Israel, the children of God.

Cain’s line died in the flood, but all spirits return. Cain came back as Esau, and Abel, or Seth, came back as Jacob. Esau “came out red, all over like an hairy garment”, and Idumea, the Greek and Roman name for Edom, is that same Esau. So when we ask who the children of the devil are in the earth today and why they hate us, John has already told us: not as Cain, who was of that wicked one.

precepts.label: 2 Thessalonians 2:9
precepts.why:
Paul speaks of the man of sin: “Even him, whose coming is after the working of Satan with all power and signs and lying wonders”. His coming is after the working of Satan, meaning Satan is his father, as he was Cain’s. That is Esau, Cain come again.

Genesis 3:15 ends, “it shall bruise thy head, and thou shalt bruise his heel.” Christ is our head, smitten so that the sheep were scattered. But the heel is Edom’s Achilles heel. Jacob took hold of Esau’s heel at birth, and in Daniel 2 “a stone was cut out without hands, which smote the image upon his feet that were of iron and clay, and brake them to pieces.”

The image is the empires. The head of gold is Nebuchadnezzar and Babylon; the silver is Persia and Media; the brass is Greece, “which shall bear rule over all the earth.” That was Alexander, “son of Philip, the Macedonian”, who “slew the kings of the earth” until “the earth was quiet before him; whereupon he was exalted and his heart was lifted up”: the beginning of white supremacy in the earth. His kingdom was parted among his generals, “and evils were multiplied in the earth.” Their own books, The Chronology of Ancient Nations and The Rise of Christendom, trace Philip back to Esau. The iron is Rome, and we are still in it: America and NATO, a kingdom “partly strong, and partly broken”, strong in military, with the toes as the European nations. The miry clay is the melting pot: “they shall mingle themselves with the seed of men: but they shall not cleave one to another”.

The stone is Christ, “Jesus Christ himself being the chief corner stone”. He strikes the image on its feet, its heel, and “the stone that smote the image became a great mountain, and filled the whole earth.” And “in the days of these kings shall the God of heaven set up a kingdom, which shall never be destroyed: and the kingdom shall not be left to other people”. We are living in the days of these kings. What we teach is the beginning of that kingdom, and it cannot be stopped; it will consume all these kingdoms with the word of God.

thread.label: Genesis 4:1-8
thread.text: And Adam knew Eve his wife; and she conceived, and bare Cain, and said, I have gotten a man from the Lord.

classes.title: Bitterness: The Hidden Leaven From Cain To Esau

precepts.label: Proverbs 15:10
precepts.why:
Cain was born first, just like Esau. “Abel was a keeper of sheep, but Cain was a tiller of the ground”, a man of the field, which already tells you what is going on. “And in process of time it came to pass, that Cain brought of the fruit of the ground an offering unto the Lord.” Cain already knew right from wrong, because his father taught him animal sacrifice, but over a process of time Cain turned evil and did not do what the Lord commanded.

Abel brought “of the firstlings of his flock and of the fat thereof. And the Lord had respect unto Abel and to his offering:” “But unto Cain and to his offering he had not respect. And Cain was very wroth, and his countenance fell.” His countenance fell because he was corrected. What really started all of this? Correction.

Solomon says, “Correction is grievous unto him that forsaketh the way”. Cain had forsaken the way over a process of time, so the correction was grievous to him. That grievous spirit nourished bitterness, and the bitterness grew until he murdered his brother. That is the spirit you are rolling in when you move with a bitter spirit.

Then: “and he that hateth reproof shall die”, because the wages of sin is death. Paul says, “For if we would judge ourselves, we should not be judged.” If we judged ourselves we would not have to be told about the bitterness, envy, hatred and malice inside us; when we refuse, the Lord has to bring the chastening. Cain refused to get himself right, and he became the father of wickedness.

precepts.label: Proverbs 13:10
precepts.why:
Bitterness does not travel alone. Envy, pride, hatred and evil suspicion come bundled together like a cable TV package. Solomon names one: “Only by pride cometh contention”.

Cain was contending because pride was on him. Cain's attitude was: I am not going to make it right with my brother; my brother is the one who is off; in fact, I have to put him to death, because he is making me look bad. That is pride. Cain did not want to take the correction.

Then: “but with the well advised is wisdom.” The well advised are the ones who do well, like Abel. Wisdom says, let me get my spirit right; I cannot have an evil eye toward my brother. When correction comes, pride contends with it, while wisdom takes it and makes things right with the brother.

precepts.label: James 3:16
precepts.why:
“For where envying and strife is, there is confusion and every evil work.” Genesis 4 is an account of envying and strife. Cain was not doing right, he saw Abel doing right, and that built envy, the same spirit that shows up later between Esau and Jacob. It was there from the beginning.

Then comes confusion. All of a sudden Cain did not know right from wrong, and every evil work followed: he slew his brother. When you are confused, saying, I do not know where this is coming from, every evil work will be the result.

Confusion is Satan's playground. Satan loves us operating in confusion. That is why his children throw every kind of confusion into the media and everywhere they go, and why leaders of other nations have said they do not want that American media in their countries. They know every evil work hides behind that cloud of confusion.

precepts.label: Galatians 5:26
precepts.why:
“Let us not be desirous of vain glory, provoking one another, envying one another.” Cain wanted to be the man; that is vain glory.

Provoking one another means agitating a brother to play him out of position, because you are envious of him. You do something to provoke him to evil so you can justify your position against him.

We see this even in marriage. A brother provokes his wife, she leaves the house and does something foolish, and he sits back saying, I told you the sister was off, I told you she was evil. No, brother: you are the evil one, you provoked your wife. We are not going for that foolishness here. Envy provokes, and provoking is how the bitter spirit sets up its victim.

precepts.label: Romans 7:11
precepts.why:
What is bitterness? It is sin. “For sin, taking occasion by the commandment, deceived me, and by it slew me.” Taking occasion by the commandment means you can only recognize sin through the commandments of God. How do you know you are in the middle of sin? The law says you shall not hate your brother in your heart, and when you meditate on it you realize, I have an evil spirit toward that brother. The law brings it to the surface.

Sin “deceived me”: you did not know bitterness was a sin, because you were deceived. But the law gives clarity. Like fog lights, it pierces the cloud of confusion. That is why the law is called a light: so you can see through the nonsense your mind was thinking.

Then sin “by it slew me.” When the scripture comes out, you feel cut, because you are no longer deceived and can see clearly. What you see on the other side of the fog is yourself in the mirror of the Bible, realizing how evil you were. Some people do not like the light and love to walk in darkness, saying, do not call that out, that is not me; brothers wearing purple and gold, a ribbon of blue and fringes, who are only blue ribbon Christians. We do not want to be those night walkers.

precepts.label: Psalms 37:8
precepts.why:
“Cease from anger, and forsake wrath: fret not thyself in any wise to do evil.” That bitterness is the spirit of Cain, and in that wrath you might slay a brother, or in that bitterness you might betray one. None of us is above this. Do not sit in the congregation thinking so-and-so is getting cut with the scriptures; brother, that is you. Every lesson the leadership brings out is for us. The moment you think, I am not dealing with that, Satan already has you lined up and counts you on his team.

Go back to Genesis 4:8: “And Cain talked with Abel his brother”. This is the deception. Cain acted like his friend, talking with him over time about his flocks, until he could lure him out to the field: “when they were in the field, that Cain rose up against Abel his brother, and slew him.” Solomon describes that man: “He that hateth dissembleth with his lips, and layeth up deceit within him;” “When he speaketh fair, believe him not: for there are seven abominations in his heart.” Murder, envy, pride and covetousness are all in there. “Whose hatred is covered by deceit, his wickedness shall be shewed before the whole congregation.” That is why it is called a root of bitterness: roots are covered by soil where nobody can see them, but the Lord always brings it to the surface. “Whoso diggeth a pit shall fall therein”, and “a flattering mouth worketh ruin.”

John names the spirit: “Not as Cain, who was of that wicked one, and slew his brother.” Cain was the first recorded hater in the scriptures, and he came back as Esau. The scribes and Pharisees were bitter toward Christ and wanted him dead; carry an evil eye toward your brother and you are in the same spirit. “We know that we have passed from death unto life, because we love the brethren. He that loveth not his brother abideth in death.” “Whosoever hateth his brother is a murderer”. And Sirach warns, “When the ungodly curseth Satan, he curseth his own soul.” Brothers say, the white man is the devil, they are going to be destroyed, they are going into captivity, and then carry hatred toward their own brother, moving in the same spirit.

“Be not hasty in thy spirit to be angry: for anger resteth in the bosom of fools.” Bitterness is a progression: it starts with a correction or an offense, then pride comes in and you will not speak to the brother, then when you do speak it is in deceit, masking envy, anger and hatred, and in the end it destroys you and those around you. “A little leaven leaveneth the whole lump”: a little bitterness defiles the whole soul. Christ said, “Beware ye of the leaven of the Pharisees, which is hypocrisy.” “For there is nothing covered, that shall not be revealed”. Leaven looks flat at first and grows as it bakes, so do not let the hate bake. Deal with your brother and sister uprightly according to the laws of God before it festers and overcomes you.

classes.title: Raising Cain: The Son of Perdition, Merchants, and Captive Nations

precepts.label: Romans 9:13
precepts.why:
Cain “brought of the fruit of the ground an offering unto the Lord”, and Abel brought “of the firstlings of his flock and of the fat thereof.” “And the Lord had respect unto Abel and to his offering: But unto Cain and to his offering he had not respect.” What happened to Cain and Abel physically is a foreshadowing of Jacob and Esau spiritually: one is chosen and one is not.

Paul explains it with Rebecca’s twins: “For the children being not yet born, neither having done any good or evil, that the purpose of God according to election might stand, not of works, but of him that calleth”. Then: “As it is written, Jacob have I loved, but Esau have I hated.” Cain was not rejected because he was wroth; that was ordained from the beginning. It is about election, the purpose God makes. He can make one vessel for one use and another vessel of wrath fitted for destruction.

Christians take “not of works” to mean the law need not be kept. What it tells us is that from the foundation God chose his elect. He still requires the works of the law, not the sacrificial law, but being clean and repented, to obtain the kingdom of heaven. When the first world was formed every nation was supposed to follow the laws, and judgment followed whoever did not. Cain’s rebellious nature showed itself, and it continues to this day in Esau.

People say God doesn’t hate, and they isolate “God is love.” But notice it says “as it is written”: it is in the Bible. It was written first in Malachi: “Was not Esau Jacob’s brother? saith the Lord: yet I loved Jacob, And I hated Esau, and laid his mountains and his heritage waste for the dragons of the wilderness.” Edom says, “We are impoverished, but we will return and build the desolate places”, and he did, in the Renaissance. But the Lord says, “They shall build, but I will throw down; and they shall call them, The border of wickedness, and, The people against whom the Lord hath indignation for ever.” God lets him rise to power so that he can take him down.

And the Lord asked Cain, “Why art thou wroth? and why is thy countenance fallen?” Remember that, because the same reason Cain hated Abel is the reason Esau hates Jacob today. It is the same spirit; only the name changes. “Satan” simply means adversary, one who obstructs and opposes. That is why everything they do is about us: they were made for that purpose, to obstruct and oppose us, because God purposed it from the beginning.

thread.label: Genesis 4:9
thread.text: And the Lord said unto Cain, Where is Abel thy brother? And he said, I know not: Am I my brother’s keeper?

classes.title: Raising Cain: The Son of Perdition, Merchants, and Captive Nations

precepts.label: Job 10:14
precepts.why:
The Lord asked Cain, “Where is Abel thy brother?”, and he answered, “I know not: Am I my brother’s keeper?” But “the voice of thy brother’s blood crieth unto me from the ground. And now art thou cursed from the earth”. That curse is layered, but the ultimate curse is the utter destruction of Cain and his seed, and it has not yet been fulfilled. It is a deferred judgment, held “until the times of the Gentiles be fulfilled”: a set time that has to be fulfilled of these heathen nations, starting with Esau as the top one. It is the same spirit of Cain today. Unless we accept who this man is, the son of perdition, nothing else about the last days will make sense.

The Lord told him, “a fugitive and a vagabond shalt thou be in the earth”. Apart from the little land he had in the kingdom of Esau, he takes up the identity of others: he calls himself the Greeks, when the real Greeks were black, of the Japhetic seed; the Romans; the last samurai; the Israelites and the Egyptians in The Ten Commandments. The confusion of faces was supposed to be his curse, and he flipped it onto us, until we became the astonishment, the proverb and the byword.

Cain feared that “every one that findeth me shall slay me”, and “the Lord set a mark upon Cain, lest any finding him should kill him.” Why not judge him right then? Because God had a purpose for him, as he raised up Pharaoh so that his power would be magnified when he comes to redeem his people and the earth.

Job tells us what the mark is: “If I sin, then thou markest me, and thou wilt not acquit me from mine iniquity.” The mark is sin. And sin preserves him, because sin is witchcraft: by it he seduces the nations that might stand against him into the confederacy of Psalm 83. They all know what he is, but lust, the love of money and power, make them put that aside and ally with him, the way criminals make alliances knowing one day someone will stab them in the back. Under Trump that confederacy is starting to crack.

So Cain is protected only for a time. The judgment was promised through Esau: “I hated Esau, and laid his mountains and his heritage waste”, and they shall call them “The border of wickedness, and, The people against whom the Lord hath indignation for ever.” That border of wickedness is the mark. “The earth is given into the hand of the wicked: he covereth the faces of the judges thereof; if not, where, and who is he?” If not Esau, the United States of America, who is he? And “evil shall hunt the violent man to overthrow him”: his demise will come the same way he ruled.

precepts.label: Wisdom of Solomon 4:12
precepts.why:
Why would a mark of sin protect Cain? Solomon answers: “For the bewitching of naughtiness doth obscure things that are honest; and the wandering of concupiscence doth undermine the simple mind.” Sin is bewitching. It is seductive. It hides what is honest, so that, as the scripture says, if it were possible even the elect would be deceived.

That is how the mark works. Cain’s line would have rulership for a time, and he would rule the earth with darkness, with sin and with evil, and people would be enticed by it, Israelites included. Our northern kingdom, the majority of it, fell for it, and now they are getting their wake-up call, though there was always a remnant that rebelled against the colonialism they saw in Latin America.

The bewitching is also how the confederacy holds together. The other nations know what he stands for; it is common knowledge. But the love of money, power and rulership says, put that aside, this is the one it was given to, nobody else could get me these things. So they ally with him, and there is no honor among thieves with this man. We watch him boast of taking Venezuela’s president in an operation so fast and violent, threaten the vice president with worse, and name Colombia and Mexico next.

But the spell does not last. “The pride of thine heart hath deceived thee, thou that dwellest in the clefts of the rock, whose habitation is high; that saith in his heart, Who shall bring me down to the ground?” We know who brings him down: first those he dealt with turn against him, and then Christ and his elect have the glory and honor of taking him down. The wicked are revealed and restrained for a time, a hedge around them until they fulfill what the Lord wants, and then comes their final judgment.

thread.label: Genesis 4:22
thread.text: And Zillah, she also bare Tubal–cain, an instructer of every artificer in brass and iron: and the sister of Tubal–cain was Naamah.

classes.title: Raising Cain: The Son of Perdition, Merchants, and Captive Nations

precepts.label: Genesis 27:38
precepts.why:
Tubal-cain was “an instructer of every artificer in brass and iron”. He worked metal, and at that time metal meant tools of war; he was not making decorations for your house. The mark followed Cain’s lineage: sin, violence and hatred were in his spirit. Where an artist sees art in raw material, his mind saw weapons. Weaponry came into the earth, or at least advanced, through Cain’s line. Murder led to industry, hatred led to technology, and violence led to institutional power, the hegemony that controls everything.

Then that spirit comes through Esau. “Hast thou but one blessing, my father? bless me, even me also, O my father. And Esau lifted up his voice, and wept.” Isaac answered, “Behold, thy dwelling shall be the fatness of the earth, and of the dew of heaven from above”: he would have rulership and authority. And the connection to Tubal-cain: “And by thy sword shalt thou live”. The fatness of the earth, everything he has, he gets by violence.

Then: “and shalt serve thy brother; and it shall come to pass when thou shalt have the dominion, that thou shalt break his yoke from off thy neck”. That happened once our kingdom passed. We had a kingdom for a little while, and since then we have never been in any kind of power up to this day, while he increased through the process of time.

We see it in the graphic of Trump straddling the Western Hemisphere, the Monroe Doctrine renamed the Donroe Doctrine: this is mine. That is the one that sits upon many waters. The wicked are revealed, restrained for a time with a hedge around them to fulfill what the Lord wants, and then comes their final judgment.

precepts.label: Isaiah 54:16
precepts.why:
“Behold, I have created the smith that bloweth the coals in the fire, and that bringeth forth an instrument for his work”. The Lord is over all of it. He puts it on Satan, his emissary, and Satan passes it around. It is twofold: it speaks of the brass and iron of Tubal-cain, and then it names something more.

Notice “an instrument”: not all weaponry, one in particular. Then he names it: “and I have created the waster to destroy”. What weapon at that time could have been called the waster? Nothing. Zechariah describes it: “Their flesh shall consume away while they stand upon their feet, and their eyes shall consume away in their holes, and their tongue shall consume away in their mouth.” Nobody could have imagined such a weapon then. They had no word for nuclear weapons or atoms, so they saw visions and explained them the best they could: it is the waster.

Malachi says, “behold, the day cometh, that shall burn as an oven; and all the proud, yea, and all that do wickedly, shall be stubble”: Esau, the other nations, and rebellious Israel that does not repent. The day that cometh burns them so “it shall leave them neither root nor branch”. A fire leaves ash; this leaves nothing. Peter says “the elements shall melt with fervent heat”. The nations know it: their treaties against nuclear proliferation show the Lord staying their hand, because whoever uses one ends the world as they know it. Isaiah 29 says the strangers “shall be like small dust” and it shall be “at an instant suddenly”, not like regular fire, and all the nations that fight against Ariel, the lion of God, “even all that fight against her and her munition”, her weapons, “shall be as a dream of a night vision”, gone that quick. They filled their bellies and lived deliciously, and in an instant it is all gone. God put it in their spirit to make that thing, and he will use their own weapon, the thing that gave them their power and respect, to end them.

This should move us. The Lord “is longsuffering to us-ward”; the day waits until the set number is sealed, and it comes “as a thief in the night.” “Seeing then that all these things shall be dissolved, what manner of persons ought ye to be in all holy conversation and godliness”? Paul says the same: “let us watch and be sober”: do not drink of her wine, do not sleep thinking you are an American and nothing can touch you. “For God hath not appointed us to wrath, but to obtain salvation by our Lord Jesus Christ”. So “comfort yourselves together, and edify one another”: this is the time to be more united, not divided over simple issues. We look boldly for that day, because “we, according to his promise, look for new heavens and a new earth, wherein dwelleth righteousness”: a baptism by fire that cleanses the evil and makes the earth fit for the kingdom.

thread.label: Genesis 4:23
thread.text: And Lamech said unto his wives, Adah and Zillah, Hear my voice; ye wives of Lamech, hearken unto my speech: for I have slain a man to my wounding, and a young man to my hurt.

classes.title: Raising Cain: The Son of Perdition, Merchants, and Captive Nations

precepts.label: Genesis 27:41
precepts.why:
Lamech told his wives, “I have slain a man to my wounding, and a young man to my hurt. If Cain shall be avenged sevenfold, truly Lamech seventy and sevenfold.” That was cold-blooded murder, killing with no anger behind it, for the thrill of it. Cain killed in anger; if he is judged, how much more Lamech, who just had violence in him. He boasted in it. It went beyond Cain; it increased. That is when murder was normalized and celebrated in that line.

That is why Esau has the same spirit: “And Esau hated Jacob because of the blessing wherewith his father blessed him: and Esau said in his heart, The days of mourning for my father are at hand; then will I slay my brother Jacob.” It is in his spirit till this day. Rebekah was told, “Behold, thy brother Esau, as touching thee, doth comfort himself, purposing to kill thee.” Killing is a comfort to him. Trump boasted that the Venezuela raid was very violent, and said of the boats, we are just going to kill them.

“Now therefore, my son, obey my voice; and arise, flee thou to Laban my brother to Haran”. The only thing Jacob could do was flee; he could not stand against that bloodthirsty violence. It is the same spirit as Cain: patient, vengeful and calculated. Cain lured his brother into the field; Esau said, I will wait until the days of mourning are done, and get him when he least suspects it.

That spirit is the son of perdition. “Let no man deceive you by any means: for that day shall not come, except there come a falling away first, and that man of sin be revealed, the son of perdition; Who opposeth and exalteth himself above all that is called God”. It says revealed, not elected: he was ordained from the beginning. Ezra was told, “Jacob’s hand held first the heel of Esau. For Esau is the end of the world, and Jacob is the beginning of it that followeth.” People blame Jacob for grabbing the heel, but none of them had done good or evil in the womb; it was a sign, and Jacob was always supposed to be in rulership. Christ said, “those that thou gavest me I have kept, and none of them is lost, but the son of perdition; that the scripture might be fulfilled.” He is not kept; he is ordained for destruction.

The Lord “shall destroy with the brightness of his coming” him “whose coming is after the working of Satan with all power and signs and lying wonders”: the bomb, the weapons, the industrial complex and the economics. So it runs like a ring: Cain murdered his brother Abel, his line built weapons, Esau plotted to murder his brother Jacob, Isaiah 14 reveals the oppressor of the nations, and 2 Thessalonians shows the man of sin fully manifested in these last days. The spirit did not disappear; it evolved from individual murder, to weapon maker, to institutional violence, to global domination, a man who says nothing can stop him but his own morality. But “The whole earth is at rest, and is quiet” once he is laid down.

precepts.label: 1 John 3:1
precepts.why:
Genesis 5 traces the lineage from Adam down to Noah, who “begat Shem, Ham, and Japheth.” Then Genesis 6 says “the sons of God saw the daughters of men that they were fair.” The sons of God are that lineage just named; the daughters of men are the daughters of the other nations that were created. These are not literal angels. The chapter before gives the understanding, and the scriptures that follow prove who the sons of God are.

John writes it in the New Testament: “Behold, what manner of love the Father hath bestowed upon us, that we should be called the sons of God.” That is what God calls us. Brothers, you are walking gods, whoever gets upset about it, the apologists included.

“therefore the world knoweth us not, because it knew him not.” The world looks at our people, calls us Negroes, and refuses to believe these could be the people of the book, the sons of God. And it knew him not: to this day they refuse to say Christ was a black man. They put the image of Cesare Borgia in every church, comic book and piece of media, while the Bible says he is black, of the tribe of Judah.

So when Genesis 6 speaks of “the sons of God” going in to the daughters of men, it is speaking of the same people John calls the sons of God: Adam’s line, our forefathers.

precepts.label: Psalms 82:6
precepts.why:
“the sons of God saw the daughters of men” in Genesis 6 is about men, not spirits; God says “My spirit shall not always strive with man, for that he also is flesh.” Psalms 82:6 shows who these sons of God are and what God calls them: “I have said, Ye are gods; and all of you are children of the most High.”

We are gods, and we are children of the Most High. That is why the sons of God in Genesis 6 are called by that name: they carried that DNA, made in the image of God.

It is also why their sin was so serious. Back in Genesis 6:4, “There were giants in the earth in those days; and also after that, when the sons of God came in unto the daughters of men.” The sons of God, the children of the Most High, took wives of the other nations, which was forbidden. The children born to them “became mighty men which were of old, men of renown,” and “God saw that the wickedness of man was great in the earth, and that every imagination of the thoughts of his heart was only evil continually.” So the Most High brought destruction, and later we had to pay for what we did as the sons of God; he told Abraham his seed would be afflicted in a land not theirs for four hundred years.

precepts.label: Deuteronomy 14:1
precepts.why:
The sons of God in Genesis 6 are Adam’s line, the lineage traced in Genesis 5. Did that name change later, after the flood and after Egypt? No. Deuteronomy 14:1, spoken after the Exodus, says to Israel: “Ye are the children of the Lord your God.”

We are the children of the Lord our God because we are the sons of God. The same people carried the same title from Adam through Noah, through the fathers, out of Egypt, and into the law.

This matters for reading Genesis 6 rightly. The sons of God who went in to the daughters of men were not angels coming down from the sky; they were men of that same chosen line, God’s own children, who mixed with the other nations when it was forbidden. That sin brought the flood, and later the affliction of our people. The scriptures do not change the name: from Genesis, to Deuteronomy, to the prophets, to the New Testament, it is our people who are called the children and the sons of God.

precepts.label: Hosea 1:10
precepts.why:
The title “sons of God” runs through the whole book. After Deuteronomy called Israel “the children of the Lord your God,” did anything change in the prophets? No. Hosea 1:10: “Yet the number of the children of Israel shall be as the sand of the sea, which cannot be measured nor numbered.”

“And it shall come to pass, that in the place where it was said unto them, Ye are not my people.” That place is where our people are today: America and the diaspora, Jamaica, Haiti, Africa, Europe. Everywhere we were told we are not God’s people. “there it shall be said unto them, Ye are the sons of the living God.”

God calls us the sons of the living God. That is who we are. So the sons of God of Genesis 6 are the same nation the prophet speaks of: the children of Israel, scattered and counted as nothing, yet still his sons. The world does not know us, but God does, and in the very place where we were called not his people, he will call us his sons again.

precepts.label: Judith 16:7
precepts.why:
Genesis 6:4 says the children of the sons of God and the daughters of men “became mighty men which were of old, men of renown,” and that “There were giants in the earth in those days.” Judith’s song names that kind of people: “For the mighty one did not fall by the young men, neither did the sons of the Titans smite him, nor high giants set upon him: but Judith the daughter of Merari weakened him with the beauty of her countenance.”

The sons of the Titans and the high giants are those giants, the men of renown of Genesis 6, the offspring of the sons of God.

That is where Esau gets his Titan movies, and his Greek mythology of Hercules and the half-gods. He always mixes some lies in with the truth. He tells those stories because he looks at us as gods: because of our DNA, our physical prowess, our melanin. We are the sons of God, demigods on the earth, and that is why when our people are put into sports or anything physical, we dominate. Everybody wants our rhythm, but nobody wants our blues.

So the Titans of the Greek stories are not fallen angels or gods of another people. They are a twisted memory of the mighty men born when the sons of God went in to the daughters of men.

precepts.label: Baruch 3:26-28
precepts.why:
Baruch says the same thing as Genesis 6: “There were the giants famous from the beginning, that were of so great stature, and so expert in war.” Those giants were the offspring of the sons of God, the mighty men of renown, and they were expert in war as well.

“Those did not the Lord choose, neither gave he the way of knowledge unto them.” God did not choose them; they were wicked. “But they were destroyed, because they had no wisdom, and perished through their own foolishness.” How were they destroyed? The flood. God saw that “every imagination of the thoughts of his heart was only evil continually,” and he wiped it out.

But those same spirits came right back, by way of the three sons of Noah, Shem, Ham and Japheth. There is no new thing under the sun. Jude speaks of “certain men crept in unawares, who were before of old ordained to this condemnation,” the same words, “of old,” that Genesis 6 uses of the men of renown. The same kind of wickedness is still here, reserved “unto the judgment of the great day,” which has not yet come.

So the giants are not a fantasy of fallen angels, the Nephilim Esau talks about. They were men, the offspring of the sons of God, who had no wisdom, and whose spirit lives on until the judgment.

precepts.label: 2 Esdras 6:7-10
precepts.why:
When the twins were born, Jacob came out and “his hand took hold on Esau’s heel.” That is very important, because there is a lot of symbolism behind it, and 2 Esdras 6 explains it.

Ezra asks, “What shall be the parting asunder of the times? or when shall be the end of the first, and the beginning of it that followeth?” In other words, when shall this world end, and when shall the new world come in? The answer goes straight to Rebekah's womb: “From Abraham unto Isaac, when Jacob and Esau were born of him, Jacob’s hand held first the heel of Esau. For Esau is the end of the world, and Jacob is the beginning of it that followeth.”

That is what the hand on the heel means. Esau's world is the one that ends, and Jacob's is the one that follows. It matches what the Lord told Rebekah: “Two nations are in thy womb”, “the one people shall be stronger than the other people; and the elder shall serve the younger.” The word Genesis means beginning, and this is the beginning of those two nations.

“The hand of man is betwixt the heel and the hand”: all the other nations sit between those two. They are like extras in the movie. Moab is an extra; Ishmael is an extra. The story is Jacob and Esau. Christians do not know what that means at all.

precepts.label: Genesis 2:7
precepts.why:
Rebekah bore twins, but they were not identical, because the Lord said “two manner of people shall be separated from thy bowels.” They looked different. “And the first came out red, all over like an hairy garment; and they called his name Esau.” Esau means wasted away: his melanin was wasted away. Look at them in a heat wave in France: when they are in the sun they get red. Down south they are called rednecks, but it is not just their necks. Don't call them white; they are Esau, and these are his children.

The scripture never mentions Jacob's color, because Jacob looked just like his mother and father. In fact, Jacob looked like everybody from the time of Adam. Genesis 2:7 shows what that was: “the Lord God formed man of the dust of the ground.” The dust of the ground is different shades of brown, and the deeper you dig, the darker it gets. That is what Adam looked like, and Eve, and everyone who came from them.

The only one who differed was Esau, and that is why the scribes had to write down his color: he was starkly different. In the old world, Cain's line was cursed with a lack of melanin. The flood came and killed them all off, and God brought them all back through Noah's three sons.

So when you move up the generations to Isaac and Rebekah, the two lines return in one womb. Esau is the return of Cain's lineage, and Jacob is the return of Seth. That is why the two boys were two manner of people from birth: Esau the cunning hunter, a man of the field who liked the rush of the hunt, and Jacob a plain man, dwelling in tents, herding the sheep and the goats.

precepts.why:
When Rebekah’s twins were born, “the first came out red, all over like an hairy garment; and they called his name Esau.” It was important for that to be written down, because everybody was of the same complexion before. Genesis 2:7 shows why: “the Lord God formed man of the dust of the ground.” Man was made from the earth, and the deeper you dig, the darker the earth gets.

Even the ground people call red earth is not red. In Oklahoma City the clay-looking dirt is a bright, vivid brown; put your hand next to it and you see it. The old Indian red crayon was brown too, because the natives were not red. That is another way to show that the natives were black, and the book Black Indians shows it.

Then the verse goes on: he “breathed into his nostrils the breath of life; and man became a living soul.” The breath of life is the Lord’s statutes and commandments, the same laws the Christian pastor tells you that you do not have to keep. Back in Genesis 25, notice that when Jacob came out, “his hand took hold on Esau’s heel,” and nothing is said about his color. It did not need to be said: everybody was brown, different shades of brown, as the dust they were made from. Esau came out red and hairy, and that was different enough that it had to be documented. He is the one whose name was changed to Edom, which means red, and from him came a different manner of people.

precepts.label: Proverbs 7:2

Proverbs 7:2 finishes what Genesis 2:7 opened. God “breathed into his nostrils the breath of life; and man became a living soul,” and that breath of life is his statutes and commandments. Solomon says it plainly: “Keep my commandments, and live; and my law as the apple of thine eye.”

If you want to have life, you must keep God’s laws; there are no two ways about it. The man who is not keeping the Lord’s statutes and commandments is dead, no matter what the Christian pastor tells him about not having to keep them.

The way back to life is to keep his commandments and hold his law as the apple of our eye.

precepts.label: Genesis 33:4
precepts.why:
“And Esau hated Jacob because of the blessing wherewith his father blessed him: and Esau said in his heart, The days of mourning for my father are at hand; then will I slay my brother Jacob.” That is the bitterness, and it plans over a process of time. It is the same thing we read in Genesis 4: Cain slew Abel, and Esau wanted to kill Jacob. Cain was the firstborn and Esau was the firstborn. Same spirit.

To see how someone can hold bitterness, hatred and malice toward you and hide it completely, look at Genesis 33, long after Esau said he hated his brother: “And Esau ran to meet him, and embraced him, and fell on his neck, and kissed him: and they wept.” Someone who hates you can play the long game. He can pretend to be your friend and on your side while he waits for the moment to hit you at your worst. They call them liberals today. That's the liberal for you: oh, we love you niggers, I mean black people. Jacob knew Esau's heart. That is why he sent the gifts ahead: he thought Esau might be coming to kill him.

Hebrews explains what was working in Esau: “Looking diligently lest any man fail of the grace of God; lest any root of bitterness springing up trouble you, and thereby many be defiled”. Looking diligently means looking within yourself. The root of bitterness is a hidden sin under the ground that nobody sees, but over time it springs up and troubles you. It distorts your thoughts and your perception, so that things you once saw clearly, with eyes anointed with eye salve, are no longer pure to you.

“Lest there be any fornicator, or profane person, as Esau, who for one morsel of meat sold his birthright.” Profane means devoted to what is not sacred, secular rather than religious: Esau was a carnal man, a man of the field, whose religion is sin. When we follow the carnal ways of Esau, we throw away our birthright, the kingdom of heaven. Hebrews says “for he found no place of repentance, though he sought it carefully with tears.” Hold on to a bitter spirit and you are a spiritual Edomite, and you will find the same place of no repentance on that day.

An officer drew the parallel: “He that committeth sin is of the devil; for the devil sinneth from the beginning.” Christ came “that he might destroy the works of the devil”, so we cannot move in the devil's spirit and think we move in Christ's. Whoever does not love his brother is not of God. If there is an offense, deal with it by Matthew 18:15, not by sowing discord in the congregation. “For to be carnally minded is death; but to be spiritually minded is life and peace.” The spiritually minded man seeks to gain his brother, not keep him as a rival to get back at, “Because the carnal mind is enmity against God: for it is not subject to the law of God”.

precepts.label: Psalms 50:19-20
precepts.why:
Esau cried, “Is not he rightly named Jacob? for he hath supplanted me these two times: he took away my birthright; and, behold, now he hath taken away my blessing.” Is that true? Go back to Genesis 25. Esau came from the field faint and said, “Feed me, I pray thee, with that same red pottage”. “And Jacob said, Sell me this day thy birthright.” There was no trickery. Jacob asked him straight, and it was up to Esau to say no. Esau said, “what profit shall this birthright do to me?” Jacob made him swear, because the word of that man is no good, just as with the four hundred and some treaties they broke. Scripture sums it up: “thus Esau despised his birthright.”

So Esau was lying and playing the victim. The Psalm describes it: “Thou givest thy mouth to evil, and thy tongue frameth deceit.” “Thou sittest and speakest against thy brother; thou slanderest thine own mother’s son.” Did we not just read the slander? He tricked me two times. Nowhere does scripture show Jacob dealing with deceit over the birthright. They were liars from the beginning, because they moved in the same spirit as their father Cain, who was of the wicked one.

It is how they do today: throw the rock, hide the hand, and as soon as the other side hits back, run to the UN as the victim. Now all of a sudden he cares about the birthright, just as his children want to stand in our place claiming to be the Jews and the people of the book. Where was that energy when he threw it away for something to eat, or today for money and fame?

You got the children of God and you got the children of the devil; there is no in between. You either got the godly mind or the Edomite mind. The same Psalm says to the wicked, the white man, “What hast thou to do to declare my statutes, or that thou shouldest take my covenant in thy mouth?” “Seeing thou hatest instruction, and castest my words behind thee.” They say in God we trust and swear on the Bible while doing nothing the scripture says.

Esau “lifted up his voice, and wept”, but that was worldly sorrow. “For godly sorrow worketh repentance to salvation not to be repented of: but the sorrow of the world worketh death.” We must come to the Lord sincerely, because of those who wait, God says, “Then shall they call upon me, but I will not answer; they shall seek me early, but they shall not find me:” “For that they hated knowledge, and did not choose the fear of the Lord”. “Therefore shall they eat of the fruit of their own way”. We all have to examine ourselves so we are not moving in that same spirit.

precepts.label: 2 Kings 8:20
precepts.why:
Isaac told Esau, “Behold, I have made him thy lord, and all his brethren have I given to him for servants.” Jacob was made Esau’s lord; the elder would serve the younger. Everybody on this planet was meant to be our servants. It is our birthright; we are the rulers of this earth. But the only way to get it back is to remember where we fell off and what we did wrong, and Christianity will not teach us that. It keeps us in the wrong, and keeps us divided into Adventist, Protestant, Pentecostal, Mormon and Jehovah’s Witness, with none of them telling us who we are.

Esau “lifted up his voice, and wept,” and he still got a blessing: “thy dwelling shall be the fatness of the earth, and of the dew of heaven from above.” The best portions of the earth, and the dew that falls on the whole earth. But the whole earth was already given to Jacob. How the hell is Esau going to get the best part of the earth? The next words answer it: “by thy sword shalt thou live.” He would take it by the sword. He is a killer, yet wherever he goes he says he comes in peace, that he only wants to liberate the people and bring them freedom, while it is missiles after missiles, rape after rape, nothing but atrocities once he is let in. That's what democracy is about: now you could be a homo, nobody can judge you; now you could be a transgender, nobody can judge you. The book of Maccabees shows evil multiplying on the earth when they took control.

The blessing ends, “and shalt serve thy brother; and it shall come to pass when thou shalt have the dominion, that thou shalt break his yoke from off thy neck.” 2 Kings 8:20 shows that yoke breaking: “In his days Edom revolted from under the hand of Judah, and made a king over themselves.” Edom had served Judah, and in the days of the kings he threw it off.

From there it went back and forth. There was dominion again in 193 AD under Septimius Severus, wicked as hell as it was, and it was lost again around the Renaissance. So Isaac’s words have come to pass: Esau has possession of the earth, and he killed to get it.

precepts.label: 2 Kings 8:16-20
precepts.why:
Esau cried, “Hast thou but one blessing, my father? bless me, even me also, O my father.” Jacob had already received the major blessing. Rebekah sent him in, dressed in goats' hair so he would feel hairy like his brother, because she remembered what God told her at the birth: the elder shall serve the younger. When Jacob feared a curse, she said let it fall on her. The white man's the devil, and when you ask the Christians about those two boys, they say Jacob was the evil son and Esau the good one, and black people in church echo those same sentiments. No: Jacob was the good one. Esau was the profane one, the fornicator, the one who despised his birthright, and Rebekah was being obedient to God.

Isaac answered Esau: “thy dwelling shall be the fatness of the earth, and of the dew of heaven from above.” Dew falls everywhere, and wherever it falls, Esau would live; he would have the best places on the planet. How would he get them? “And by thy sword shalt thou live”: by war. God through Isaac blessed Esau with the art of war, the same blessing Cain's line had when Tubal-cain made all kinds of weapons.

Then: “and shalt serve thy brother; and it shall come to pass when thou shalt have the dominion, that thou shalt break his yoke from off thy neck.” When did that first happen? 2 Kings 8 answers. “Jehoram the son of Jehoshaphat king of Judah began to reign”, and “he walked in the way of the kings of Israel, as did the house of Ahab: for the daughter of Ahab was his wife: and he did evil in the sight of the Lord.” Yet the Lord would not destroy Judah for David's sake. “In his days Edom revolted from under the hand of Judah, and made a king over themselves.” That is the first time Esau broke the yoke from off his neck, just as Genesis 27:40 prophesied.

After that, Edom turned on his brother outright. When the Babylonians destroyed the first temple in 586 BCE, Edom helped them instead of helping Judah: rejoicing, looting the city, blocking the survivors who fled. Obadiah, “concerning Edom”, says, “even thou wast as one of them”, and “Neither shouldest thou have stood in the crossway, to cut off those of his that did escape.” 1 Esdras names who set the fire: “the temple, which the Edomites burned when Judea was made desolate by the Chaldees.”

precepts.label: Deuteronomy 2:12
precepts.why:
Esau left Canaan because his riches and cattle were too great for him and Jacob to dwell together, and the land did not belong to him. “Thus dwelt Esau in mount Seir: Esau is Edom.” But Genesis 14:6 had already shown that the Horites dwelt in Mount Seir. So what became of them?

Genesis 36 lists the dukes of Esau's sons, the high titles: Teman, Omar, Zepho, Kenaz, Korah, Gatam and Amalek, all of Eliphaz, Esau's firstborn by Adah. Remember these dukes, because they are all around today under various names like German, Israeli and Polish. Then comes a surprise: “These are the sons of Seir the Horite, who inhabited the land; Lotan, and Shobal, and Zibeon, and Anah,” “And Dishon, and Ezer, and Dishan: these are the dukes of the Horites, the children of Seir in the land of Edom.” Seir the Horite was a Hamite, and the Horites had dukes first. That is where Esau learned about dukes: he got among them, took their title and took their land.

Deuteronomy tells how: “The Horims also dwelt in Seir beforetime; but the children of Esau succeeded them, when they had destroyed them from before them, and dwelt in their stead”. The Horims are the Horites, the same Hamite people. The children of Esau intermingled with them, then conquered them by the sword and dwelt in their place. So when you read about Seir it means Edom, but originally it was the land of the Horites, the children of Ham.

Moses adds, “as Israel did unto the land of his possession, which the Lord gave unto them.” Israel did the same in Canaan, but we did not kill off all the Canaanites; they kept living there. Esau did not waste any time. He killed them all out of there. That is the robber nature of Edom from the beginning: take the land, take the title, and destroy the people who were there.

precepts.label: Deuteronomy 2:22
precepts.why:
Moses says it a second time: “As he did to the children of Esau, which dwelt in Seir, when he destroyed the Horims from before them; and they succeeded them, and dwelt in their stead even unto this day”. Esau destroyed the Horims and lived in their stead, and he is still there unto this day.

The name tells the rest. The Horims, or Horites, get their name from the Hebrew word for a cave or a hole, which shows they were known as cave dwellers, troglodytes, living in the mountains of Seir. These Hamites lived in the caves first. Esau went in, conquered the cave dwellers and became a cave dweller himself. And what does Caucasian mean? Cave dweller. Edom became a cave dweller. People say the white man is not Esau. Well, then who is he? Japheth? The hell he is. He is far from Japheth.

Malachi shows God's view of it: “yet I loved Jacob,” “And I hated Esau, and laid his mountains and his heritage waste for the dragons of the wilderness.” Christian theologians say hated means preferred less, but that sounds just as bad; it means hate. The dragons of the wilderness are the Arabs, the Nabataeans, who later pushed much of Esau out of that land or intermarried with him. Mount Seir is called Petra today, meaning rock. Edom, rich in Canaan, became a poor cave dweller in Seir, saying, “We are impoverished,” but vowing to return and build the desolate places, and God calls them the border of wickedness, the people against whom he has indignation forever.

Obadiah describes the same people in the last days: “thou that dwellest in the clefts of the rock, whose habitation is high”, the cave dweller, “Though thou exalt thyself as the eagle, and though thou set thy nest among the stars, thence will I bring thee down, saith the Lord.” The Greeks, the Romans, Spain, France, Russia, Britain and America all exalt the eagle, and all are Caucasian. Show us a powerful black nation today that came out of caves and exalts itself as the eagle. It fits one people: the Europeans, who took Seir from the Horites and dwell in their stead unto this day.

precepts.label: Deuteronomy 25:5-6
precepts.why:
About three months after Judah went in to Tamar, she began to show, and word came to Judah that his daughter-in-law had played the harlot and was with child by whoredom. Her husband was dead and she was living in her father's house, so Judah said, “Bring her forth, and let her be burnt”: that was the law for a harlot. But she sent him his own signet, bracelets and staff, and “Judah acknowledged them, and said, She hath been more righteous than I; because that I gave her not to Shelah my son.” The child was his, and he was the one in the wrong.

Deuteronomy 25 shows what Judah and Onan owed her. Moses recites this law later, but our forefathers already had knowledge of it through oral tradition passed down from Adam. “If brethren dwell together, and one of them die, and have no child, the wife of the dead shall not marry without unto a stranger: her husband’s brother shall go in unto her.” That is why it was wrong when Onan spilled his seed on the ground.

“the firstborn which she beareth shall succeed in the name of his brother which is dead, that his name be not put out of Israel.” To succeed in the name of the dead brother does not mean the child takes his actual name. It means the child inherits the dead man's possession, his land and his things, because he left no seed to inherit for him. The brother raises up a surrogate seed in honor of his dead brother, so the land stays in his brother's name and is not lost.

A brother who refuses is brought before the elders. His brother's wife shall “loose his shoe from off his foot, and spit in his face”, saying, “So shall it be done unto that man that will not build up his brother’s house.” And “his name shall be called in Israel, The house of him that hath his shoe loosed.” He carries that humiliation forever, because he would not love his neighbor as himself. That is why the history of Ruth is so important. It is not about Ruth, the Moabite heathen woman; y'all make it about her because y'all love heathens.

So Tamar was more righteous than Judah: she kept her dead husband's name alive when Judah withheld Shelah. From her came twins. Zarah put out his hand first and the midwife bound a scarlet thread on it, but he drew it back and his brother broke forth: “this breach be upon thee: therefore his name was called Pharez.” Pharez means a breach, and the line of the kings runs through him.

precepts.label: 1 Corinthians 3:16-17
precepts.why:
Exodus 12:15 says, “even the first day ye shall put away leaven out of your houses”. That is purging the old leaven. We had to do it physically, but it is something spiritual today. So what is your house today? “Know ye not that ye are the temple of God, and that the Spirit of God dwelleth in you?” You, me, we are the temple of God, and the Spirit of God is to dwell in us because our temple was destroyed.

Look at how we purge leaven from the house. Brothers dump out the toaster, sweep underneath the floor mats and in the corners where stuff builds up. There is not one grain of yeast in the house. Meanwhile the brother has an evil eye toward another brother, or is bitter toward his wife, or vice versa. We sweep our houses with diligence; we must do the same with our spirit, because we are the temple of God.

“If any man defile the temple of God, him shall God destroy; for the temple of God is holy, which temple ye are.” You will pull this out on a brother in the street: brother, you got tattoos, you got the devil on you, you are defiling your temple. We know tattoos are wrong. But meanwhile you have a whole yeast factory in your spirit. If you are out there with the leaven of bitterness in your spirit, you are out of order too, and you will be destroyed just like that brother if he and you do not repent.

precepts.label: Romans 6:23
precepts.why:
Exodus 12:15 says, “whosoever eateth leavened bread from the first day until the seventh day, that soul shall be cut off from Israel.” What is that really saying? How do we eat the leaven today? A dumb thought jumps into your mind and you say, damn, I don't like that brother. You are spiritually consuming it, entertaining sin and not purging the leaven from your house. That is how you get cut off from your people, and this is a serious thing.

How you get cut off: “For the wages of sin is death; but the gift of God is eternal life through Jesus Christ our Lord.” Christ is our Passover, who set the example. That is the gift, the promise made to Abraham, for us to get repentance for sins, because we are in a wicked place.

And Exodus 13:7 says “there shall no leavened bread be seen with thee, neither shall there be leaven seen with thee in all thy quarters.” We do not want to be seen in the midst of sin, Passover or not. Don't be the brother who does not throw the bread out but puts it in his storage closet and brings it back when Passover is over: laying the bitterness aside for the season and picking right back up hating the brother. That is not the spirit. Throw it out. Let it go.

precepts.label: 1 Corinthians 6:19-20
precepts.why:
Some brothers say, I am going to tuck mine in, tuck away my hatred and my bitterness and save it for later. Paul answers that: “What? know ye not that your body is the temple of the Holy Ghost which is in you, which ye have of God, and ye are not your own?”

We are not our own. So when we hide hatred, bitterness, malice, whatever sins we deal with, we are throwing that back in Christ's face. He is our Passover, our sacrifice; he bought us back, twice he bought us back. So we do not own our bodies to even have the angle to defile our temple. When a brother lends you something, you are supposed to take extra care of it. Christ gave us our bodies and bought us back again, and we need to keep them like brand new.

“For ye are bought with a price”: with Christ's blood. Then, “therefore glorify God in your body, and in your spirit, which are God’s.” We have to use our bodies to glorify him in every way possible, and our spirit too, because both belong to God. When we hold back malice, hatred for our brothers or hatred for our wife, we put that on Christ, and it is not of the Lord. We have to let go of that spirit.

That is the leaven Exodus 12:15 says to put out of your house: not only the yeast on the box, but the bitterness tucked in when Bishop comes around and let out again when he leaves.

precepts.label: Deuteronomy 28:48
precepts.why:
“Thou shalt not abhor an Edomite; for he is thy brother”. Use this verse to your advantage; don't run from it. In Romans 9:13 Paul speaks on behalf of God, and that is what God says about Esau. But God's law to us is: thou shalt not abhor an Edomite, for he is thy brother, a wicked brother.

And look at our condition: “Therefore shalt thou serve thine enemies which the Lord shall send against thee, in hunger, and in thirst, and in nakedness, and in want of all things”. If you know you have to serve this man for food, water and clothing, you can't go around saying I hate your guts, I just want to harm you. You think you're going to have a job? You're going to lose everything.

There was a brother at camp on Eastern Parkway, on medication, who said he couldn't work because he gets violent: I hate white people; when I sit in the office or do construction, I look at them and I just want to harm them. And there was a martial artist, a black belt, who drew young Haitian brothers to him, skinny at first and diesel two or three months later, calling themselves the barbershop crew in Brooklyn. One night a brother called to be gotten out of jail: they were getting diesel and learning to fight to do home invasions and burglaries.

The bottom line is, professing yourself to be an Israelite is not on the premise of wanting to harm white people. A lot of Israelite camps teach that, and the leaders of those camps are bums: either they are bums or they live off the congregation, and they can talk that way without repercussions because they have no boss to answer to. We serve our enemies under the curse, so we keep the law: we do not abhor the Edomite.

precepts.label: Ephesians 4:26
precepts.why:
In an interview with Soft White Underbelly came the question: when you're teaching this, doesn't it cause people to be angry? Yes, they get angry. The Bible says anger is okay: “Be ye angry, and sin not: let not the sun go down upon your wrath”.

The sin would be if you start murdering people; the sin would be if you start stealing. Remember the series American Gods: Anansi was on a slave ship and asked, are you angry? That's good; anger gets stuff done. Surely oppression makes a wise man mad. Not I'm going to go kill everybody, but let's organize, let's do better. And you know who got that actor fired? Black people, who said what he was saying would make white people mad. The whole show was cancelled, and all those black people lost their jobs.

So “Thou shalt not abhor an Edomite; for he is thy brother” does not mean you can't be angry at what was done. Be angry and sin not: let the anger drive you to organize and build, not to harm, steal or kill.

precepts.label: Romans 12:18
precepts.why:
“If it be possible, as much as lieth in you, live peaceably with all men.” That's if possible. As much as lies in you, you live peaceably, and that includes the Edomite the law says you shall not abhor, for he is thy brother.

But we've seen some instances on the news where it was impossible; you had to throw hands with some people, because some people are irate and some people are unreasonable. Paul did not say peace at any cost; he said as much as lieth in you.

So the law of Deuteronomy 23:7 is not a command to be harmless. It is a command not to carry hatred and seek harm. We live peaceably as far as it depends on us, and we are not the ones who start it.

precepts.label: Matthew 5:22
precepts.why:
“But I say unto you, That whosoever is angry with his brother without a cause shall be in danger of the judgment”. The key is without a cause. If I'm mad with you and I have no reason to be mad with you, I'm in danger of judgment.

But now somebody does something to your daughter, your wife, your loved one: do you have a reason? Yes. At one of the schools a sister's phone kept going ding, somebody sending her indecent pictures on Instagram. It went on for a while until the heads of the school had everybody bring their phones up and closed the doors. One brother said his phone was dead; they said don't worry, we got a charger. Sure enough, it was him. They told everybody to move back, and the husband said, move out my way. That is anger with a cause.

As the saying goes, in order to be a man of peace you must be capable of great violence; if you're not capable of violence, you're just harmless. So “Thou shalt not abhor an Edomite; for he is thy brother” forbids hatred without a cause, not the defense of your own.

“Because thou servedst not the Lord thy God with joyfulness, and with gladness of heart, for the abundance of all things”. We had the whole earth, the whole thing belonged to us, and we were ungrateful children. We murmured and murmured and murmured. Even today it is like pulling teeth to get many of us to be happy and joyous on a feast day. We have to change that, because we did not have gladness before, and that is why we went into captivity. So now, coming back to serve the Lord, if you want your strength, you had better apply Nehemiah: “the joy of the Lord is your strength.” There are no two ways about it.

The blueprint is already set. The Bible tells you exactly what you need to do and how you need to go about living; we just do not want to listen. The curse of serving our enemies came because we would not serve the Lord with gladness, and the way back is to serve him with the joy that is our strength.

precepts.label: 2 Corinthians 11:4
precepts.why:
“Therefore shalt thou serve thine enemies”, “in want of all things”. We serve for food, for water, for clothes, for all kinds of paperwork, because nothing is real in your life until the so-called white man says it is real. You are not even dead until the white man says you are dead; without a paper stamped by Esau Edom you cannot even get the money your daddy left behind.

So even the understanding you have of the Bible was taught to you by Esau, and that is why you do not have the right spirit on you. When you read 2 Corinthians 11:4, once you serve “another Jesus”, you get “another gospel”, and once you get the other gospel, you get “another spirit”. That is the spirit in these churches; that is why those little boys are twitching in the church.

The enemy did not only put the yoke on our necks; he set up shop in our heads using Christianity, and you have to be dumb to believe Jesus is white with no Bible proof while you carry the biggest Bible under your arm. The only way for us to deal right is to come out of these churches and join this movement. No weapons, no guns, no physical fight will save us; the only thing that will save us is this book.

precepts.label: Romans 1:26
precepts.why:
Look at the Christian church: gangsters, homos and lesbians coming out of that church. It has mutated to a whole different level. Why? Because once you serve another God, according to the book of Romans, the Lord gives you up unto “vile affections”.

So if you keep staying in that Christianity, serving the false deity, or keep being a Muslim, serving a rock, do not be mad when the evil spirit jumps on you and you start defiling your body, changing kind and doing all kinds of nonsense. That is what is going to happen. Your choir master is making all those songs dedicated to another deity, and the Lord is unhappy with that. He says, you want to devote all your time to serving another god? I am going to remove myself from here, and watch what happens to you.

That is the curse of Deuteronomy 28:47-48 working in the spirit: because we did not serve the Lord with gladness, he sent our enemies against us, and when we took up their gods, he gave us up. Thank the Lord for saving a remnant, because we all would have been as Sodom and Gomorrah.

precepts.label: Deuteronomy 33:25
precepts.why:
Moses blessed the tribes “before his death”, and of Asher he said “Let Asher be blessed with children; let him be acceptable to his brethren, and let him dip his foot in oil.” Asher is Venezuela, Colombia, Peru, Brazil, from Colombia down to Uruguay. When the conquistadors came to conquer, rob and pillage, many fled into the jungles of the Amazon and grew up without fathers, so they must be made acceptable to their brethren, and we have to go there and save our people in the jungles. And the oil: a brother in Venezuela, asked how Venezuelans and Colombians can benefit from their precious resource, stood right on the oil. The oil is the precious commodity the red man covets so earnestly.

Then verse 25: “Thy shoes shall be iron and brass.” Look up the name Brazil: it is associated with the Hebrew word barzel, meaning iron. It is not a coincidence that the name Brazil means iron in Hebrew; these people know where our people are. Brazil is full of iron, Colombia is full of iron, Venezuela is full of iron, Ecuador is full of iron. Mexico has iron too, but not the same abundance as South America.

“and as thy days, so shall thy strength be.” That is the inheritance of our people in these lands. It is not a coincidence, the names these countries get, for those who do not believe that the northern kingdom is the northern kingdom.

The elders in the 60s and 70s deciphered this without Google or the internet; all they had were the scriptures and history books. Now, in the information age, it is so much plainer. Asher's blessing, children, oil, iron and brass, sits right where the Bible said it would.

classes.title: The Iranians & The Ephesians

precepts.label: Hosea 2:8
precepts.why:
Judges says Israel “served Baalim” and “forsook the Lord God of their fathers, which brought them out of the land of Egypt”. Hosea shows how ungrateful that was: “For she did not know that I gave her corn, and wine, and oil, and multiplied her silver and gold, which they prepared for Baal.”

That is what the Lord did for Israel. He clothed us, gave us land, gave us food and possessions, all of that. And we turned around and prepared it for Baal; we started serving the devil with what God gave us. Baal, Baalim, it is the same thing: the Canaanite god of fertility, storms, thunder and lightning, worshipped in horrible ways, whose name means lord or master. He sounds like Thor. Baal and Ashtaroth have taken on so many names over the ages, which is why we rarely hear of them, but the worship is coming back to light.

Even now it goes on. Just days before this class, thousands of Afro-Brazilians gathered on a Rio beach to offer gifts to a sea goddess, Yemanja, revered in the Yoruba religion as the mother of all orishas and humanity. Brazil is the tribe of Asher. It is the same deity all throughout: “the women knead their dough, to make cakes to the queen of heaven”. Ashtaroth, the queen of heaven, Yemanja, whatever the name. Our people carried that witchcraft with them and kept doing it, even in Africa.

That's our history, and that is why we are in captivity today, catching hell. The Lord clothed us and named us, yet even in 2026 our people are still worshipping the devil, and we wonder why America goes down there stealing presidents, starving people out and destabilizing countries.

precepts.label: Leviticus 18:21
precepts.why:
“And thou shalt not let any of thy seed pass through the fire to Molech, neither shalt thou profane the name of thy God: I am the Lord.” Molech worship went along with the fertility gods: it dealt with children, with the womb. That is what we were doing, and it is exactly what God told us not to do. We became bullheaded and stubborn and started worshipping the devil. That is how Israel “forsook the Lord, and served Baal and Ashtaroth.”

Stubbornness runs through this whole history. “A stubborn heart shall fare evil at the last; and he that loveth danger shall perish therein.” So we have to prophesy against the idolatry and come up out of this foolishness: Christmas, Valentine's Day, which a lot of our people celebrated. It has nothing to do with us. God did not give it to us.

“Bow down his neck while he is young, and beat him on the sides while he is a child, lest he wax stubborn”. That is why God's laws are taught without going to the left or the right: we know how we got over here, through stubbornness. If we want to be delivered, we have to wake up.

It is how Israel gets down: “when the judge was dead, that they returned, and corrupted themselves more than their fathers, in following other gods to serve them, and to bow down unto them; they ceased not from their own doings, nor from their stubborn way.” When there is no judge, no leader, in place, they go back to their lonesome: the officer's not here, the captain's not here, the Deacon's not here, the Bishop ain't here. If you can't uphold righteousness when nobody is looking, the same judgment is your future. Stubborn goes back to bullheaded, and bullheaded goes back to Baal.

“For rebellion is as the sin of witchcraft, and stubbornness is as iniquity and idolatry.” Stubbornness is idolatry; it is satanic worship. So many think they are not dabbling in the mystic arts, but when you are stubborn and rebellious, you are: “sorcerers, and idolaters, and all liars, shall have their part in the lake which burneth with fire and brimstone”.

precepts.label: 1 Samuel 15:23
precepts.why:
Judges 2:19 ends: “they ceased not from their own doings, nor from their stubborn way.” Stubborn goes back to bullheaded, and bullheaded goes back to Baal. 1 Samuel 15:23 says what stubbornness really is.

“For rebellion is as the sin of witchcraft, and stubbornness is as iniquity and idolatry.” Bullheaded, stubborn, is idolatry. It is satanic worship.

That is how Israel gets down: “when the judge was dead, that they returned, and corrupted themselves more than their fathers.” Whenever there is not a judge, a leader, in place, they go to their lonesome. They get relaxed: the officer is not here, the captain is not here, the deacon is not here, the bishop ain’t here, let’s go back to our lonesome. If that is your spirit, you are going to get the same judgment. If you can’t uphold righteousness when nobody is looking, that is your future: damnation, judgment, destruction.

Ecclesiasticus 30:12, read just before, gives the remedy: “Bow down his neck while he is young, and beat him on the sides while he is a child, lest he wax stubborn.” That is why God’s laws are taught without going to the left or to the right, and without playing games. We know how we got over here: through stubbornness. So if we want to get delivered, we have to wake the hell up.

precepts.label: Revelation 21:8
precepts.why:
1 Samuel 15:23 said rebellion is as witchcraft and stubbornness is as idolatry. Revelation 21:8 shows where the witches and the idolaters end up.

“But the fearful, and unbelieving, and the abominable, and murderers, and whoremongers, and sorcerers, and idolaters, and all liars, shall have their part in the lake which burneth with fire and brimstone.”

A lot of y’all think, I’m not dabbling in the mystic arts. Yes, you are. When you are stubborn and rebellious, yes, you are. It says sorcerers and idolaters. The one who in Judges 2:19 would not cease “from their stubborn way” is standing with the sorcerers and the idolaters, and their part is the lake of fire.

Psalms 78:8 makes the connection plain: “a stubborn and rebellious generation; a generation that set not their heart aright.” “The children of Ephraim, being armed, and carrying bows, turned back in the day of battle. They kept not the covenant of God, and refused to walk in his law.” That is the northern kingdom, though Judah did the same thing. Even when they got over here to the Americas they still did not keep the covenant, and that is why Assyria took the northern kingdom and why Columbus and Cortez came: because of the idolatry. The Lord was sick of it and still is, and this is the last time.
