precepts.label: Judges 21:25
precepts.why:
Naomi told Ruth, “Behold, thy sister in law is gone back unto her people, and unto her gods”. Orpah went back to Moab, to her people and her gods. These were not Israelite women; this was a heathen woman of another nation. That is important, because there are doctrines out there teaching that Ruth was an Israelite. No, she was not. She was a heathen. Was it right for Boaz to deal with a heathen? No, but it happened.

Just in case there is any confusion, the last verse of Judges, right above Ruth, shows why it happened: “In those days there was no king in Israel: every man did that which was right in his own eyes.” During the judges, we did what we wanted to do.

And Ruth opens in that very time: “Now it came to pass in the days when the judges ruled”. There was no king. It was the time when Israel did what they wanted, and that included taking heathen women.

So Ruth's story does not make her an Israelite, and it does not make it right to take a heathen wife. It shows what Israel was doing when every man did what was right in his own eyes. The scripture keeps calling her what she is: “Ruth the Moabitess”. That is clear.

precepts.label: Zechariah 8:23
precepts.why:
Ruth said, “thy people shall be my people, and thy God my God”. She is a heathen saying, if I go with you, I will be as if I am an Israelite, and I will serve your God too. She is cleaving to an Israelite woman, that's all; there were no promises made to her. “Where thou diest, will I die, and there will I be buried”: I'm not leaving you.

The nations are going to be the same way in the kingdom. Zechariah shows it: “Thus saith the Lord of hosts; In those days it shall come to pass, that ten men shall take hold out of all languages of the nations, even shall take hold of the skirt of him that is a Jew, saying, We will go with you: for we have heard that God is with you.”

We will go with you, just like Ruth said. For we have heard that God is with you: your God is a real God, and ours is garbage. They are going to cleave to Israel the way Ruth cleaved to Naomi, and they will cleave as servants.

So Ruth is the picture of the nations in the kingdom: not Israelites, but holding on to Israel because the God of Israel is the true God.

precepts.label: John 4:3-5
precepts.why:
Ruth 4 is a trial at the gate before ten elders over land. Elimelech had land; he died, and his two sons, Mahlon and Chilion, died too, leaving no man to take it. So the land had to be taken up by the next of kin. Boaz told the nearer kinsman that Naomi “selleth a parcel of land, which was our brother Elimelech’s.” A parcel of land: that phrase opens the whole chapter.

John 4 uses the same wording. Christ “must needs go through Samaria. Then cometh he to a city of Samaria, which is called Sychar, near to the parcel of ground that Jacob gave to his son Joseph.” Jacob gave Joseph that parcel of ground; he bought his son that land.

A parcel of land, a parcel of ground, a parcel of a field: they are all the same thing, and a parcel of land and an inheritance are one and the same. So when Boaz bought the parcel that was Elimelech's, he was not making an ordinary purchase. He was taking up an inheritance in Israel, one that had to stay in the family of the dead.

precepts.label: Genesis 33:18-20
precepts.why:
Genesis 33 gives the history behind the “parcel of ground that Jacob gave to his son Joseph” in John 4. “Jacob came to Shalem, a city of Shechem, which is in the land of Canaan, when he came from Padan–aram; and pitched his tent before the city. And he bought a parcel of a field, where he had spread his tent, at the hand of the children of Hamor, Shechem’s father, for an hundred pieces of money.”

Jacob bought that land from the Hamites for a hundred pieces of money, and “he erected there an altar, and called it El–elohe–Israel.” A parcel of a field is again the same thing as a parcel of land: an inheritance.

Later, as he was dying, Israel told Joseph, “Moreover I have given to thee one portion above thy brethren, which I took out of the hand of the Amorite with my sword and with my bow.” His sons did take the land by the sword; Simeon and Levi went crazy and killed the men of that city. But the field was bought first, before his sons ever took it. So the inheritance at Shechem stood on a lawful purchase, the same way Boaz bought Elimelech's parcel before the elders at the gate.

precepts.label: Joshua 24:32
precepts.why:
“And the bones of Joseph, which the children of Israel brought up out of Egypt, buried they in Shechem, in a parcel of ground which Jacob bought of the sons of Hamor the father of Shechem for an hundred pieces of silver: and it became the inheritance of the children of Joseph.” The parcel of ground, the parcel of land, the parcel of a field is the land of inheritance, and this one was given to Ephraim.

That is what Boaz was protecting in Ruth 4. The nearer kinsman would not redeem it, “lest I mar mine own inheritance”, and plucked off his shoe; here the shoe is passed without shame, because he is yielding the right to someone else, not refusing his brother. Boaz bought all that was Elimelech's, Chilion's and Mahlon's, and took Ruth, the wife of Mahlon, “to raise up the name of the dead upon his inheritance, that the name of the dead be not cut off from among his brethren.” The son he raised up would inherit that land, because it belonged to Mahlon. Boaz is still the father; Boaz begat Obed, and the line goes through Boaz. There are no two fathers. The land falls under the dead man's line; the lineage goes back to Boaz. That is love your neighbor as yourself.

So Elimelech did not lose his land. We kept our land in house. Land is very important: if you have it, keep it and give it to your children; don't sell it off. Our people once had millions of acres in America, and Esau made laws, eminent domain among them, and found a distant kin to pay off with a little money, and so stole millions of acres, beaches included, from Judah.

The allotment still stands. When we came out of Egypt, every family was allotted land, and Judges says “the children of Israel went every man unto his inheritance to possess the land.” Those families are here today. The Lord says he “will bring them again, every man to his heritage, and every man to his land.” Whoever is left after the destruction, those who repent, will be given back the land and inheritance that was given to us back then.

precepts.label: Jeremiah 12:15
precepts.why:
“And Salmon begat Boaz, and Boaz begat Obed”. Boaz raised up seed in the name of Mahlon, but the record says Boaz begat Obed, not Mahlon, because Mahlon was dead. The genealogy goes under Boaz; the land falls under the dead man's line. Obed takes on the land of Elimelech even though that is not his father's line. That is the inheritance: the parcel of land, the parcel of field, the parcel of ground. You don't inherit a tribe; you inherit the land. And they were both of the same tribe anyway.

That is why the scripture says this in Jeremiah: “And it shall come to pass, after that I have plucked them out I will return, and have compassion on them, and will bring them again, every man to his heritage, and every man to his land.” It literally means what it says. In the beginning God allotted every family land.

The line of David had an inheritance given to it; the families of Judah each had land appointed to them. Guess what? Those families are here today. When the Lord returns, those that make it, that repented, are going back to that land, every man to his heritage.

That is why Boaz raised up seed for Elimelech's family: so the land would stay within that family's inheritance. That is loving your neighbor as yourself. We kept our land in house. So land is very important: if you have it, keep it and give it to your kids; don't just sell it off. A lot of Judah had millions of acres here in America, and Esau stole them, creating laws like eminent domain and finding some distant kin to pay a little money and take the land. There are beaches that belong to us. But the Lord will bring every man again to his heritage and to his land.

precepts.label: Judges 2:6
precepts.why:
Judges shows how the land was first given: “And when Joshua had let the people go, the children of Israel went every man unto his inheritance to possess the land.” We all had land and an inheritance. When we came out of Egypt, every family was allotted land. Whoever of those same families is left after the destruction takes place will be given back the land and inheritance that was given to us back then.

Notice it says every man unto his inheritance. Sisters, you're divorcing us and taking half our stuff, but it says every man. Our wives benefit from our inheritance; it belongs to the men, but it is theirs too because they are married to us. According to God, the inheritance belongs to the men, just as the earth belonged to Adam, and Eve benefitted from it because she was helping him.

And the land we inherit is not an acre or something. 1 Chronicles 2 shows Jair “who had three and twenty cities in the land of Gilead”, “even threescore cities”. We owned cities. Somebody literally owned the Bronx, Manhattan, Brooklyn, Queens. We had castles on those cities, winter houses and summer houses.

That is why the land in Ruth had to stay with Elimelech's family. Boaz begat Obed, and the genealogy goes through Boaz down to Jesse and David, but the inheritance, every man's portion from the time of Joshua, stayed with the dead man's line through the seed raised up to him.

precepts.label: Ecclesiasticus 12:10-11
precepts.why:
Agag was not supposed to be kept alive in the first place. King Saul trusted the enemy; Samuel did not. “Then said Samuel, Bring ye hither to me Agag the king of the Amalekites. And Agag came unto him delicately.” He came crouching and speaking softly: “Surely the bitterness of death is past.” And Samuel still carried out the word of the Lord: “Samuel hewed Agag in pieces before the Lord in Gilgal.”

This is the wisdom Samuel applied, and the wisdom we have to learn to apply: “Never trust thine enemy: for like as iron rusteth, so is his wickedness.”

“Though he humble himself, and go crouching”: is that not exactly what Agag did, coming delicately? “Yet take good heed and beware of him, and thou shalt be unto him as if thou hadst wiped a lookingglass, and thou shalt know that his rust hath not been altogether wiped away.”

The things that were written aforetime were written for our learning. Esau does not forget, but we do, because we are not tapped into the scriptures. When we apply what the scriptures show us, we learn that our enemies have been the same from day one, and they are not going to change. That is the perpetual hatred we never learned.

precepts.label: 2 Kings 25:27-28
precepts.why:
Zedekiah rebelled like his brother and his nephew did. He tried to run away and got caught in the plains of Jericho, and they killed his kids in front of him first, then took his eyes out, bound him and locked him up in Babylon. At this point there are no more kings of Judah; Zedekiah was the last one. His sons are gone, his heirs are gone. So who's left?

Read on: “in the seven and thirtieth year of the captivity of Jehoiachin king of Judah”, “Evil–merodach king of Babylon in the year that he began to reign did lift up the head of Jehoiachin king of Judah out of prison; And he spake kindly to him, and set his throne above the throne of the kings that were with him in Babylon”. Jehoiachin had been locked up between 36 and 37 years. Then he “changed his prison garments: and he did eat bread continually before him all the days of his life.” His allowance was a continual allowance, a daily rate for every day: Babylon gave him a job and status.

Jehoiachin is Jeconiah, and he is the Jechonias of Matthew 1:11. He got some mercy in captivity, but was he a king anymore at this point? No. He was a king, but now he was a captive in Babylon, receiving wages and some status.

And in Babylon he had children: “the sons of Jeconiah; Assir, Salathiel his son”. Salathiel is Shealtiel, the father of Zerubbabel, whose name means born in Babylon. That is where the line of the kings of Judah went on after Zedekiah's sons were slain: through a captive king in Babylon.

precepts.label: 1 Kings 4:31
precepts.why:
Judah had five sons: Er, Onan and Shelah by the daughter of Shua the Canaanitess, and the twins Pharez and Zerah by Tamar. “The sons of Pharez; Hezron, and Hamul. And the sons of Zerah; Zimri, and Ethan, and Heman, and Calcol, and Dara: five of them in all.” Ethan, Heman, Calcol and Dara became very famous. They were very wise.

How wise? Solomon’s wisdom is measured against them: “For he was wiser than all men; than Ethan the Ezrahite, and Heman, and Chalcol, and Darda, the sons of Mahol: and his fame was in all nations round about.”

Those same sons of Judah were so wise that many men were named after them, and Solomon surpassed even them. He was wiser than the wise men of his own tribe.

That is the house this genealogy runs through. Hezron, the oldest son of Pharez, begat Ram, and from Ram comes Amminadab, Nahshon, Salma, Boaz, Obed and Jesse: a tribe of wise men, princes and kings.

precepts.label: Numbers 2:3
precepts.why:
“And Ram begat Amminadab; and Amminadab begat Nahshon, prince of the children of Judah”. Nahshon was of the elite princes of Judah, a prince family, a royal family. The census confirms the same man: “Of Judah; Nahshon the son of Amminadab.”

And in the camp: “And on the east side toward the rising of the sun shall they of the standard of the camp of Judah pitch throughout their armies: and Nahshon the son of Amminadab shall be captain of the children of Judah.”

So Nahshon was a captain. These men had serious status: princes and captains, leaders. They were warriors; they were not regular men.

“And Nahshon begat Salma, and Salma begat Boaz, And Boaz begat Obed, and Obed begat Jesse”. Boaz came from that line, the line of Pharez, the twin that breached, not the one whose hand came out first with the scarlet thread. And Jesse had eight sons, and one of those sons is David.

precepts.label: Exodus 6:23
precepts.why:
Now a tie-in regarding family ties: “And Aaron took him Elisheba, daughter of Amminadab, sister of Naashon, to wife; and she bare him Nadab, and Abihu, Eleazar, and Ithamar.”

Aaron is Moses’ brother, of Levi. He took Elisheba, Amminadab’s daughter and Nahshon’s sister, to wife. Aaron’s wife was of the tribe of Judah. Those families intermarried, priests and kings marrying together. It is no coincidence; that is why John the Baptist and Christ are cousins.

Nadab and Abihu were the two who offered strange fire and were killed; Eleazar and Ithamar were spared. Eleazar became the high priest in the days of Joshua, the mediator before the Lord. So Eleazar’s mama was Judah. That is why some Levites don’t have the big heads; their mama is Judah. And don’t forget the big nose, too.

So Amminadab begat Nahshon and a daughter Elisheba. Aaron married Elisheba and had the four sons, the high priests, which makes Nahshon Aaron’s brother-in-law. And from Nahshon came Salma, Boaz, Obed and Jesse: the priesthood and the royal line of Judah bound together in one family.

thread.label: 1 Chronicles 2:34-35
thread.text: Now Sheshan had no sons, but daughters. And Sheshan had a servant, an Egyptian, whose name was Jarha.

classes.title: The Nativity: the Bloodline, Birthright, & the Messiah

precepts.label: Genesis 15:3-4
precepts.why:
Abram, childless, was going to leave his house to Eliezer of Damascus, the eldest servant born in his house: “Behold, to me thou hast given no seed: and, lo, one born in my house is mine heir.” The Lord said no: “This shall not be thine heir; but he that shall come forth out of thine own bowels shall be thine heir.” Not a heathen servant, but his own seed. An heir and an inheritance are the same word, like a family heirloom passed down the line.

That is the key to 1 Chronicles 2: “Now Sheshan had no sons, but daughters. And Sheshan had a servant, an Egyptian, whose name was Jarha. And Sheshan gave his daughter to Jarha his servant to wife.” This was while Israel was in Egypt, when we had no land of inheritance allotted to us. People read it and say the Egyptian married into the tribe and became Judah. No.

The record follows that line for generation after generation so that it is known. When Israel came out of Egypt and inherited the land, that line could not receive land, because the land passes by the paternal bloodline and that line goes back to an Egyptian servant. They were among us in the land, but they did not inherit. It is written there to exclude, not to include. Sheshan's brothers had sons and received land; his line did not. It does not mean the Egyptian became a Jew. When we came back under the Persians and the Medes, a man who could not show from his father's house who he came from was given no inheritance, and a Levite could not serve in his office. Zerubbabel could show he came from King David's line.

The daughters of Zelophehad show the law when a man has only daughters. They asked, “Why should the name of our father be done away from among his family, because he hath no son?” The Lord said, “If a man die, and have no son, then ye shall cause his inheritance to pass unto his daughter”, then to his brother, then his father's brethren, then the next kinsman: the law Boaz was fulfilling. But those daughters had to marry “only to the family of the tribe of their father”, “So shall not the inheritance of the children of Israel remove from tribe to tribe.” The inheritance of Israel is paternal. There is no sin in marrying a woman of another tribe; Aaron did it. The command there was only to keep the land in the tribe. We have no land in captivity now, so marry within your nation and stay with your people.

precepts.label: 1 Chronicles 28:19
precepts.why:
David, chosen out of Judah and out of his father’s house, hands the building of the house to the son the Lord chose to sit on the throne: “Solomon thy son, he shall build my house and my courts: for I have chosen him to be my son, and I will be his father.” “Moreover I will establish his kingdom for ever”. Solomon’s kingdom, not Solomon and his brethren’s. Then David charges him: “Take heed now; for the Lord hath chosen thee to build an house for the sanctuary: be strong, and do it.”

“Then David gave to Solomon his son the pattern of the porch”. The blueprints to the temple: guess who gave them to Solomon? David. Solomon did not come up with the design; David came up with it, and Solomon fulfilled his father’s wishes. That porch is why the feast of dedication is kept at Solomon’s porch. It took Solomon seven years to build the temple and thirteen years to build his own house, so the temple was done before his house was finished.

David gave him the pattern “of the houses thereof, and of the treasuries thereof, and of the upper chambers thereof”, the floors and levels, “and of the inner parlours thereof, and of the place of the mercy seat”, the holy of holies. “And the pattern of all that he had by the spirit”: the spirit moved David to design the temple. The courses of the priests, which priest for burning incense and which for each service, David was behind all of that too. Gold by weight for the things of gold, “refined gold by weight” for the altar of incense, everything gold, “and gold for the pattern of the chariot of the cherubims, that spread out their wings, and covered the ark of the covenant of the Lord.”

“All this, said David, the Lord made me understand in writing by his hand upon me, even all the works of this pattern.” David did not write it off the top of his head. The Lord moved his hand on what to write, and David drew out the temple through his hands. So the house Solomon built on the throne of the kingdom of the Lord was the Lord’s own pattern, given through David to the son chosen to sit on David’s throne.

precepts.label: Isaiah 44:28
precepts.why:
Cyrus the Great founded the Achaemenid Empire, the old Persian kingdom, in 550 BC, and it was an ancient Iranian empire. That makes this very significant for what is going on today. “the Lord stirred up the spirit of Cyrus king of Persia”, and Cyrus proclaimed, “The Lord God of heaven hath given me all the kingdoms of the earth; and he hath charged me to build him an house at Jerusalem”.

The Lord was working through King Cyrus. The Lord did speak to him, and he listened. Isaiah had already named him: “That saith of Cyrus, He is my shepherd, and shall perform all my pleasure: even saying to Jerusalem, Thou shalt be built; and to the temple, Thy foundation shall be laid.”

So the word of the Lord by the mouth of Jeremiah was fulfilled through a Persian, an Iranian king, called by God his shepherd, who performed all his pleasure: Jerusalem built again and the foundation of the temple laid.

precepts.label: Isaiah 45:1
precepts.why:
Isaiah goes on: “Thus saith the Lord to his anointed, to Cyrus, whose right hand I have holden, to subdue nations before him; and I will loose the loins of kings, to open before him the two leaved gates; and the gates shall not be shut”.

That is why Cyrus could say, “The Lord God of heaven hath given me all the kingdoms of the earth”. The Lord held his right hand and subdued nations before him. The Lord used King Cyrus, who was a Persian, to allow us to go back and build the temple.

Cyrus is also the one who gave that decree. And the kingdom he ruled, Persia and Media, is Iran today, which is why his story is very significant for what is going on now.

precepts.label: 1 Samuel 9:1-2
precepts.why:
Esther 2:5 gives Mordecai’s line: “a certain Jew, whose name was Mordecai, the son of Jair, the son of Shimei, the son of Kish, a Benjamite.” Mordecai, and Esther with him, were of the tribe of Benjamin. Go back to 1 Samuel 9 and see who Kish is.

“Now there was a man of Benjamin, whose name was Kish, the son of Abiel, the son of Zeror, the son of Bechorath, the son of Aphiah, a Benjamite, a mighty man of power.” Kish was a mighty man of power.

“And he had a son, whose name was Saul, a choice young man, and a goodly: and there was not among the children of Israel a goodlier person than he: from his shoulders and upward he was higher than any of the people.”

So Saul and Mordecai come out of the same line, the line of Kish. This was not a regular line; this was a mighty Benjamite line. Keep that in mind for what follows, because the enemy Saul was sent against in his day, the Amalekites and their king Agag, shows up again in Mordecai’s day. The hatred is perpetual, and it runs down the same lines.

thread.label: Esther 3:1
thread.text: After these things did king Ahasuerus promote Haman the son of Hammedatha the Agagite, and advanced him, and set his seat above all the princes that were with him.

classes.title: Edom: The Robbers of thy people revealed past and present

precepts.label: Esther (Greek) 12:6
precepts.why:
“After these things did king Ahasuerus promote Haman the son of Hammedatha the Agagite”. Ahasuerus is Artaxerxes. Haman was the enemy in the book of Esther, the one who sought to kill all the Jews out of existence. And he is called the Agagite: in 1 Samuel 15, Agag was the king of the Amalekites, an Edomite king. Haman was a descendant of the survivors when King Saul went in and slaughtered them.

The Apocrypha tells the same man's story: “Howbeit Aman the son of Amadathus the Agagite, who was in great honour with the king, sought to molest Mardocheus and his people because of the two eunuchs of the king.” When you read Esther, Haman hired two assassins to kill the king and take over the throne. The Greeks infiltrated the Persian Empire and tried to conquer it from the inside.

And when Haman found out that Mordecai was of the same line as King Saul, he said, that's Saul's line, kill them all; they tried to kill us off. They were going to go to war with them from generation to generation. We will never get along, from the womb to the tomb. This is war.

precepts.label: Esther (Greek) 16:10
precepts.why:
Esther 3:1 calls Haman the Agagite. Chapter 16 tells you what he was: “For Aman, a Macedonian, the son of Amadatha, being indeed a stranger from the Persian blood”. Haman was a Macedonian.

Now read 1 Maccabees 1:1: “Alexander son of Philip, the Macedonian”. Alexander the Great's father was Philip the Macedonian, who came out of the land of Chettiim and whose son smote Darius king of the Persians and Medes and reigned in his stead, the first over Greece. That is when the Greeks began to conquer the dark nations.

So Haman was called a Macedonian, and Philip was called the Macedonian: Edomites and Macedonians are the same people. Haman was not a Persian; he was “a stranger from the Persian blood”. He was an Edomite, the Agagite, a descendant of Amalek, the enemy of Jacob from generation to generation.

thread.label: Job 1:1-12
thread.text: There was a man in the land of Uz, whose name was Job; and that man was perfect and upright, and one that feared God, and eschewed evil.

classes.title: Popular Persuasions: Fighting Against Heaven Defending Earth

precepts.label: 1 Kings 22:19-23
precepts.why:
In Job, “the sons of God came to present themselves before the Lord, and Satan came also among them. And the Lord said unto Satan, Whence comest thou?” But I thought he got kicked out of heaven and was one of the fallen ones? No. He is there because he works for God. God created good angels and bad angels, and Satan’s job is to tempt us; he is only allowed to do what God allows. The prophet Micaiah saw the same court of heaven.

“I saw the Lord sitting on his throne, and all the host of heaven standing by him on his right hand and on his left.” The angels on the right hand go forth for righteousness, and the ones on the left go forth for evil, for judgment.

“And the Lord said, Who shall persuade Ahab, that he may go up and fall at Ramoth–gilead?” One said one thing and another said another. “And there came forth a spirit, and stood before the Lord, and said, I will persuade him.” “I will go forth, and I will be a lying spirit in the mouth of all his prophets. And he said, Thou shalt persuade him, and prevail also: go forth, and do so.”

God gave that spirit the authority to do it, the same way he gave Satan the authority in Job 1 to tempt Job: destroy everything, but do not touch Job himself. Even the lying spirit stands before the throne and goes out only when the Lord sends it. That is why the fallen angel doctrine is crap, and why it is a shame to hear black pastors, not only Edomite pastors, repeating that same garbage rhetoric and defiling the minds of the people.

precepts.label: Psalms 103:20-22
precepts.why:
“Bless the Lord, ye his angels, that excel in strength, that do his commandments, hearkening unto the voice of his word.” That do his commandments. I thought he kicked them out of heaven because they were disobedient and tried to overthrow him, and now they are fallen? No: they do his commandments. We just read about the spirit sent forth in 1 Kings 22, and about Satan working for the Most High in Job 1. The angels hearken unto the voice of the Most High.

“Bless ye the Lord, all ye his hosts; ye ministers of his, that do his pleasure.” Keep that word ministers in mind. They minister unto the Most High, doing his pleasure, and they also minister unto us.

“Bless the Lord, all his works in all places of his dominion: bless the Lord, O my soul.” Every angel in every place of his dominion is under his rule, carrying out his commandments, which is why Satan could only go as far as the Lord allowed him with Job.

precepts.label: Hebrews 1:14
precepts.why:
The psalm calls the angels “ministers of his, that do his pleasure.” They minister unto the Most High, but they minister unto us as well: “Are they not all ministering spirits, sent forth to minister for them who shall be heirs of salvation?”

Who is going to be heir of salvation? Us, if we keep the commandments. So the angels work on our behalf. They are ministering spirits, sent forth by God for his people.

So the angels that come before the Lord in Job 1 are not rebels running loose. They are sent forth at his word, whether to try a man like Job or to minister for the heirs of salvation.

precepts.label: Ecclesiasticus 39:28-31
precepts.why:
This shows how the angels do what the Most High tells them. “There be spirits that are created for vengeance, which in their fury lay on sore strokes; in the time of destruction they pour out their force, and appease the wrath of him that made them.” Those are the angels on the left hand of God, and they minister unto God and to us.

“Fire, and hail, and famine, and death, all these were created for vengeance; Teeth of wild beasts, and scorpions, serpents, and the sword punishing the wicked to destruction.”

Here is the point: “They shall rejoice in his commandment, and they shall be ready upon earth, when need is; and when their time is come, they shall not transgress his word.” They do what God tells them to do. They do not have free will to say, let’s go down and sleep with some human women today. That is not what goes on in the heavens.

So when Satan went forth to touch all that Job had, he was doing what God allowed and no more. Even the spirits made for vengeance do not transgress his word.

precepts.label: Psalms 34:7
precepts.why:
The angels minister unto the Most High, and they minister unto us. “The angel of the Lord encampeth round about them that fear him, and delivereth them.” These are the good angels. They encamp around them that fear him and deliver them from all evil, like it says in the Lord’s prayer.

Our forefathers never looked at the angels as some demonic thing that came down to earth to persecute and kill them. When three men stood by Abraham in the plains of Mamre, he ran to meet them, bowed himself, had water fetched to wash their feet and prepared a calf for them to eat. When two angels came to Sodom, Lot rose up to meet them, bowed with his face to the ground and made them a feast, and they did eat. They look like us.

The angel in Revelation told John, I am thy fellow servant and of thy brethren; the angels have tribes too. Raphael presented the prayers of the saints. They are our brothers, working on our behalf. Calling them demons and fallen angels is Esau’s popular persuasion. The angel of the Lord camps round about them that fear God, just as the Lord set a hedge about Job, and delivers them.

thread.label: Job 5:11-27
thread.text: To set up on high those that be low; that those which mourn may be exalted to safety.

classes.title: Edom's Achilles' Heel

precepts.label: 1 Samuel 2:3-8
precepts.why:
Job 5:11 says the Lord will “set up on high those that be low.” That is us: we are low right now, but he is going to set us up on high. And “those which mourn may be exalted to safety”: our people that mourn shall be exalted to safety and comfort. 1 Samuel 2 goes with it.

“Talk no more so exceeding proudly; let not arrogancy come out of your mouth.” The arrogancy is the foolishness, the teaching and the wisdom of this world. Pastor, don’t let that come out of your mouth. “For the Lord is a God of knowledge, and by him actions are weighed.” He is going to judge all of us on our actions. Not your thoughts, though you must control your thoughts, but on what you do.

“The bows of the mighty men are broken, and they that stumbled are girded with strength.” “The Lord killeth, and maketh alive”: it is the Lord that kills and the Lord that makes alive. “The Lord maketh poor, and maketh rich: he bringeth low, and lifteth up.” That is what Job 5:11 just said: we are being brought low, but we are going to be exalted.

“He raiseth up the poor out of the dust.” The dust represents confusion, a low state of confusion, and the poor are the poor in spirit. “And lifteth up the beggar from the dunghill.” We are the beggar. Our people are begging for reparations, give us money; I want Section 8, I want a job, I want this. And the dunghill is this low place: whatever kind of house you have, compared to where we came from, it is a dunghill.

But he lifts them up “to set them among princes, and to make them inherit the throne of glory: for the pillars of the earth are the Lord’s, and he hath set the world upon them.” The Lord is going to make us inherit the throne of glory. That is the setting up on high of those that be low in Job 5:11.

precepts.label: Romans 5:3-5
precepts.why:
Job 5:17: “Behold, happy is the man whom God correcteth: therefore despise not thou the chastening of the Almighty.” We get corrected all the time. We might not be happy while we are going through it, but it says happy is the man whom God corrects. Romans 5 shows why.

“And not only so, but we glory in tribulations also: knowing that tribulation worketh patience.” There is a purpose behind tribulation: it works patience. “And patience, experience”: patience teaches you experience. “And experience, hope: And hope maketh not ashamed; because the love of God is shed abroad in our hearts.”

That means we understand why God is allowing us to go through tribulation. He is teaching us something. While we are in it we might not understand it, but he is saying, I am trying to teach you a lesson here. That is why we do not despise the chastening of the Almighty.

precepts.label: Hebrews 12:6-8
precepts.why:
“For whom the Lord loveth he chasteneth.” Whom the Lord loves, he chastises. This is why we go through things in our lives that we might not like at the moment. It is the same thing Job 5:17 says: “happy is the man whom God correcteth.”

“And scourgeth every son whom he receiveth.” So if you are in this truth, expect to get scourged. Expect to get beat.

“If ye endure chastening, God dealeth with you as with sons; for what son is he whom the father chasteneth not?” If you endure that chastisement, God is dealing with you like a son. “But if ye be without chastisement, whereof all are partakers, then are ye bastards, and not sons.” Nobody wants to be a bastard. So “despise not thou the chastening of the Almighty”: the chastening is the proof that you are his son.

precepts.label: Isaiah 1:4-6
precepts.why:
Job 5:18: “For he maketh sore, and bindeth up: he woundeth, and his hands make whole.” He makes us sore, and Isaiah 1 shows where we are bruised from the top of our head.

“Ah sinful nation”: that is us, you and me. “A people laden with iniquity, a seed of evildoers, children that are corrupters”: we are the corrupters. “They have forsaken the Lord”: our people have forsaken the Lord. “They have provoked the Holy One of Israel unto anger, they are gone away backward”: we have gone backwards from God’s laws.

“Why should ye be stricken any more?” God is saying, I keep punishing you over and over, why should you be stricken any more? “Ye will revolt more and more: the whole head is sick, and the whole heart faint. From the sole of the foot even unto the head there is no soundness in it; but wounds, and bruises, and putrifying sores: they have not been closed, neither bound up, neither mollified with ointment.”

In Isaiah 1:4-6 he is talking about us in comparison with Job. Job was real, don’t get it wrong, but his life represents the nation of Israel. He lost everything, even his health, from the top of his head to the soles of his feet, and that is what Isaiah says about the nation of Israel as a whole. But the same God that “maketh sore” also “bindeth up”; “his hands make whole.” He will make us whole again.

precepts.label: Revelation 11:15
precepts.why:
Job 5:19: “He shall deliver thee in six troubles: yea, in seven there shall no evil touch thee.” The six troubles mean the six trumps. And the seventh?

“And the seventh angel sounded; and there were great voices in heaven, saying, The kingdoms of this world are become the kingdoms of our Lord, and of his Christ; and he shall reign for ever and ever.”

So by the seventh trump there shall no evil touch us. It is going to be kingdom time. Then Job goes on: “In famine he shall redeem thee from death: and in war from the power of the sword.” “Thou shalt be hid from the scourge of the tongue”: nobody is going to utter a word ever against the twelve tribes of Israel; you fix your lips to call us something, that’s off with your head. “Neither shalt thou be afraid of destruction when it cometh”: he is telling us not to be afraid when destruction comes, because it is going to come. Some don’t believe that because of America, God bless the USA, nothing could ever happen here. But it is coming, and the angels are going to protect the brothers and sisters that are alive at that time.

precepts.label: Isaiah 60:21-22
precepts.why:
Job 5:24: “And thou shalt know that thy tabernacle shall be in peace; and thou shalt visit thy habitation, and shalt not sin.” We won’t sin. Isaiah 60:21 says the same.

“Thy people also shall be all righteous”: our people shall be all righteous. “They shall inherit the land for ever”: we shall inherit the land forever. “The branch of my planting, the work of my hands, that I may be glorified”: we are the branch of God’s planting.

“A little one shall become a thousand, and a small one a strong nation: I the Lord will hasten it in his time.” We are going to have a whole lot of children. He is going to make sure to bring back certain spirits through marriage and childbearing; certain spirits are going to come back real quick.

That is Job 5:25-26: “thy seed shall be great, and thine offspring as the grass of the earth.” Our children are going to grow up quick. “Thou shalt come to thy grave in a full age, like as a shock of corn cometh in in his season.” Like a shock of corn comes back over and over, Israel is going to have a long, long life. That is why he calls it forever, eternal.

precepts.label: Romans 10:14-18
precepts.why:
David says “Day unto day uttereth speech, and night unto night sheweth knowledge”, and “Their line is gone out through all the earth”. You might think that speech and knowledge is the sun, the moon and the stars. No, it is the teachers, brothers out teaching day by day and night by night. Paul broke it down for us so we don't have to do guesswork: “But I say, Have they not heard? Yes verily, their sound went into all the earth, and their words unto the ends of the world.” Paul is quoting Psalm 19, and their sound is the sound of teaching.

Start at verse 14: “How then shall they call on him in whom they have not believed? and how shall they believe in him of whom they have not heard? and how shall they hear without a preacher?” Our people cannot call on the Lord if they have not heard. You need a preacher to hear this gospel. “And how shall they preach, except they be sent?” To preach is to prophesy, and it takes being sent. “How beautiful are the feet of them that preach the gospel of peace, and bring glad tidings of good things!” That is why brothers are told: be prepared. Prepare yourself to be sent.

“Lord, who hath believed our report?” The report is the Bible, the scriptures. The prophets preach the report, and the question is who has believed it.

“So then faith cometh by hearing, and hearing by the word of God.” That is how you increase faith. New brothers and sisters ask how to increase their faith: you must consistently addict yourself to the hearing of the gospel, over and over. However old you are, calculate it: that is how many years of brainwashing you must undo. Coming in once a week will not undo it. It must be daily listening to the word, and reading more than the four chapters a day.

precepts.label: Job 9:24
precepts.why:
“Truly God is good to Israel, even to such as are of a clean heart”: to the twelve tribes, those who walk in righteousness and do the commandments. “But as for me, my feet were almost gone; my steps had well nigh slipped. For I was envious at the foolish, when I saw the prosperity of the wicked.” Some of us in here get envious the same way when we see the prosperity of the wicked.

Who is the wicked? Job says: “The earth is given into the hand of the wicked”. If you don't know who the wicked is, it is telling you by a process of elimination. It ain't the black man and the Latin man; we are not ruling anything. We can't even rule our own homes. The white man rules supreme on this planet. You want anything done in your country, you have to go through that white man.

“he covereth the faces of the judges thereof”. The judges are God, Christ, the angels and the Israelites, and it is the white man who covers their faces. Look at the paintings: black Mary with a black baby Christ, and somehow that baby grows up and, Shazam, becomes a white man, and nobody sees anything wrong with that.

So the wicked whose prosperity Asaph envied is the one the earth has been given to for a time: the man who whitewashed the faces of the judges.

precepts.label: Malachi 1:3-4
precepts.why:
Job 9:24 says the wicked has the earth. Malachi names him: “And I hated Esau, and laid his mountains and his heritage waste for the dragons of the wilderness.” That is the Dark Ages, when God made Esau poverty-stricken.

“Whereas Edom saith, We are impoverished, but we will return and build the desolate places”. They returned in the time called the Renaissance, and that is when they conquered us and made us their slaves, Christian slaves. “thus saith the Lord of hosts, They shall build, but I will throw down”. God said, I will give you a chance to build: they built up America, England, France, Germany, Australia, all those places they robbed and pillaged.

“and they shall call them, The border of wickedness, and, The people against whom the Lord hath indignation for ever.” Indignation means righteous anger, for ever. So it identifies who the wicked is: Esau, Edom.

That is why Asaph saw him prospering: wherever Esau goes, it seems whatever he touches turns to gold. But he is building only to be thrown down.

precepts.label: Psalms 140:1-5
precepts.why:
“Therefore pride compasseth them about as a chain; violence covereth them as a garment.” They have so much wealth that pride covers them like a chain, and much of their old slave money is invested in war companies, weaponry and the military. David names him: “Deliver me, O Lord, from the evil man: preserve me from the violent man”. This is about the white man. Preserve us from him.

“Which imagine mischiefs in their heart; continually are they gathered together for war.” If there is no war, you can bet your last dollar the white man will start one. He can never let there be peace on earth; the way God made him, it is his nature. Trump pledged to end global conflict and bombed at least seven countries in 2025; under Obama in 2016, 26,171 bombs were dropped on seven countries. And they took Maduro with weapons that shut his military down in minutes.

“They have sharpened their tongues like a serpent; adders’ poison is under their lips. Selah.” Selah means it is true. Whatever comes out of their mouth, religion or politics, is the worst kind of poison; for some of them politics is their religion. Take hold of it and you will die.

“Keep me, O Lord, from the hands of the wicked; preserve me from the violent man; who have purposed to overthrow my goings.” Their purpose on earth is to overthrow the twelve tribes of Israel. They can't rest if they see one of us in a nice car or a nice home: he must be selling drugs. “The proud have hid a snare for me, and cords; they have spread a net by the wayside; they have set gins for me.” The cords and the net are their traps of religion and politics, and a gin is a trap too. He is the wicked of Job 9:24 and Malachi 1, and he wears violence like he wears clothes.

precepts.label: Micah 6:11-12
precepts.why:
“Behold, these are the ungodly, who prosper in the world; they increase in riches.” Read the top ten billionaires: Elon Musk, Jeff Bezos, Bernard Arnault, Bill Gates, Mark Zuckerberg, and the rest. Zuckerberg stole Facebook from the college kids who hired him to create it. Micah asks: “Shall I count them pure with the wicked balances, and with the bag of deceitful weights?” Wicked balances are unjust judgments.

“For the rich men thereof are full of violence”. These rich people come from old money, gotten through the rape, robbery and pillaging of our nations and our people.

“and the inhabitants thereof have spoken lies, and their tongue is deceitful in their mouth.” Their descendants will say anything to justify the evil of their ancestors: it wasn't me, it was my ancestors, but I enjoy what they did. Why? Because they benefit from it.

That is what Asaph envied before he went into the sanctuary of God. Many times we envy people without knowing how they got their money, but nine times out of ten, especially with white folks, it came through criminality. Only by reading and understanding the word of God will you understand their end: set in slippery places and cast down into destruction.

precepts.label: Deuteronomy 29:29
precepts.why:
“He that dwelleth in the secret place of the most High shall abide under the shadow of the Almighty.” The secret place of the Most High is the Bible. Moses says so: “The secret things belong unto the Lord our God: but those things which are revealed belong unto us and to our children for ever, that we may do all the words of this law.” God's word is his secrets, and what he has revealed of it belongs to Israel and our children forever, so that we may do his law.

So dwelling in the secret place means living in his word and keeping it. That is why “his truth shall be thy shield and buckler”: his law is thy shield and buckler. The one who dwells there can say “He is my refuge and my fortress: my God; in him will I trust.”

That is who the psalm protects when destruction comes. And it is coming, though some do not believe it because of God bless the USA, nothing could ever happen here. Job says “neither shalt thou be afraid of destruction when it cometh”, because the Lord is telling us it is going to come. The arrow that flieth by day is the missile, and the destruction that wasteth at noonday tells you the time.

“A thousand shall fall at thy side, and ten thousand at thy right hand; but it shall not come nigh thee. Only with thine eyes shalt thou behold and see the reward of the wicked.” The only reason we will see that and not be touched is “Because thou hast made the Lord, which is my refuge, even the most High, thy habitation”: because we dwell in the secret place, his word and his law.

precepts.label: Matthew 24:30-31
precepts.why:
“For he shall give his angels charge over thee, to keep thee in all thy ways. They shall bear thee up in their hands, lest thou dash thy foot against a stone.” What is that talking about? Matthew 24 shows it.

“And then shall appear the sign of the Son of man in heaven: and then shall all the tribes of the earth mourn, and they shall see the Son of man coming in the clouds of heaven with power and great glory. And he shall send his angels with a great sound of a trumpet, and they shall gather together his elect from the four winds, from one end of heaven to the other.” Those are the angels given charge over us.

There is going to be so much destruction that the angels will make sure we do not get hurt. We are going to be delivered while our enemies are being put to death. That is “Only with thine eyes shalt thou behold and see the reward of the wicked.” The angels will protect the brothers and sisters alive at that time, so that, as Job says, “At destruction and famine thou shalt laugh.”

Then “Thou shalt tread upon the lion and adder: the young lion and the dragon shalt thou trample under feet”: these are the nations, and we are going to trample them. Because the believer has set his love upon the Lord, he says “therefore will I deliver him: I will set him on high, because he hath known my name.” “I will be with him in trouble; I will deliver him, and honour him. With long life will I satisfy him, and shew him my salvation.”

precepts.label: Proverbs 16:18
precepts.why:
The first thing on the list of what the Lord hates is “A proud look.” Proverbs 16 shows where that proud look ends: “Pride goeth before destruction, and an haughty spirit before a fall.”

Whenever you see somebody fall off, just know there is some form of pride in that man or that woman: something they do not want to address, an inflated ego, disdain, a haughty look, a refusal to come back to God. You might not have seen it. They might have masked it as confidence in your eyes, but God saw it as pride.

Pride is not always loud and in your face. It can be subtle: not asking for help because you do not want to seem weak, holding grudges because you feel justified, saying I am good when you are not, shutting down and thinking you do not need anybody. Pride always points the finger at somebody else and never at yourself. So when you start feeling yourself too much, puffing your chest out, say, Oh no, I am not trying to fall; let me be humble, let me be loving.

Every kingdom has failed because of pride, even ours. “Woe to the crown of pride, to the drunkards of Ephraim”: the northern kingdom fell because of pride, separating from God to do their own thing, going back to the split under Rehoboam, who would not listen to the elders. Then the southern kingdom: “After this manner will I mar the pride of Judah, and the great pride of Jerusalem.” And the warning to us: “Hear ye, and give ear; be not proud: for the Lord hath spoken.”

So the proud look is first on God’s list because it is the start of the fall. God made your eyes, your body and the mind you think with; walking in pride is departing from your maker, and it ends in destruction.

precepts.label: Romans 15:4
precepts.why:
“For whatsoever things were written aforetime were written for our learning.” The excellent things God wrote in Proverbs 22:20, the counsels and knowledge that make us “know the certainty of the words of truth”, were written for us to learn.

And not only to learn: “that we through patience and comfort of the scriptures might have hope.” These excellent things are written for us to apply to our lives, so that we can be excellent and great in God’s eyes. Learn and apply, that is what Romans 15:4 is telling us.

Everything in this Bible is the excellent things of God, the truth he wants us to know. It is not to be used to get rich off of prosperity teaching, and it is not up for debate for us to decide what we should and should not do. It is not up for debate whether we want to be great or average. God gave us excellent things because he expects excellence out of us.

So we have to change our mindset and live up to the standards of God, not the standards the world has placed on black men and women and Hispanic men, to be comfortable with the crumbs society gives us. Those excellent things are what we have to apply, and it starts with a change in the mind.

precepts.label: 1 Samuel 2:3
precepts.why:
“Talk no more so exceeding proudly; let not arrogancy come out of your mouth: for the Lord is a God of knowledge, and by him actions are weighed.”

Actions are weighed when it comes to the Most High. That is why he gave us the excellent things of Proverbs 22:20: to learn them and apply them, because he wants actions behind those things. Not lip service, but actual action from all of us that he called.

Romans 15:4 says the scriptures were written for our learning; 1 Samuel 2:3 says what he does with that learning. He weighs what we do with it. Proud talk and arrogancy out of the mouth weigh nothing with him, because he is a God of knowledge and knows whether the words are backed by works.

That is the pride of thine heart: to talk big about the things of God and not live them. The one who has been given the excellent things has to put his actions where his mouth is, and keep arrogancy out of it.

precepts.label: Isaiah 45:15
precepts.why:
“Verily thou art a God that hidest thyself, O God of Israel, the Saviour.” He hides himself. That means he is not dealing with everybody. It is not like you just say, hey God, and he turns around. He answers and reveals himself to whom he wants to.

So for you to have even a little understanding of his excellent things, to learn them and apply them to your life, means something. He is the “God of Israel, the Saviour.” If God has revealed himself to you, that you are an Israelite, that you even have a mind to conceive his words and understand them, that means something to God. It means you are worthy enough for him to reveal his words to you, so that you get a chance to know what these excellent things are.

You can’t take that lightly. Far too many people in this world do, and use the Bible for material gain and to feel good on their terms. God doesn’t get down like that. He is a God that hides himself, so if he is letting you know what these words mean, you better take heed to him.

And that is where the humbling comes in. Romans 12:3 follows it: “not to think of himself more highly than he ought to think; but to think soberly, according as God hath dealt to every man the measure of faith.” If he is revealing himself to you when he does not deal with everybody, you better have some humbleness, because that is the King of kings, the omnipotent Most High God. We are Israelites and we have to keep God’s commandments, so don’t think too highly of yourself. Humble down.

precepts.label: 1 John 1:9
precepts.why:
“He that covereth his sins shall not prosper”: when you try to cover that bitterness, the roots keep growing, and you are just bringing in dump trucks to load more soil on top of it. But whoso confesses shall have mercy, and John shows why: “If we confess our sins, he is faithful and just to forgive us our sins”. The Lord is faithful and just when we confess our sins.

That goes all the way back to Leviticus. When you brought your sacrifice before the priest, that was a public confession. You had to walk through the midst of all Israel with your offering.

Now we have the white man, his walls and his technology. We have VPNs: yeah, don't nobody know I'm on OnlyFans, I got a VPN, I'm broadcasting from the Philippines. No, brother, the Lord sees right through it.

So in order to get over the root of bitterness we have to confess it: damn, I had the devil on me. Covering it will never prosper; confessing it is how we get the mercy we all want.

precepts.label: James 5:16
precepts.why:
Confessing is not only to the Lord. James says: “Confess your faults one to another, and pray one for another, that ye may be healed. The effectual fervent prayer of a righteous man availeth much.”

We should be comfortable confessing our faults, because, as 1 Corinthians 10:13 says, no temptation has taken you but such as is common to man. You confess your fault, and a brother might say, brother, I was dealing with the same spirit. Woo, man, I feel a lot better. All of this is common. We all have levels of bitterness; some have a higher degree than others, but everybody deals with a level of bitterness, a level of lust, a level of lack of faith.

That doesn't mean getting on the public announcement. It means you see a godly man and say, hey Cap, hey D, I have this going on, I need help with it. They are going to help you. They are not going to say, brother, you got the devil on you, get away from me. It is Satan telling us otherwise.

That is whoso confesseth and forsaketh: confessing to the Lord, confessing one to another, and being healed, instead of covering the sin and letting the root grow.

precepts.why:
Isaiah had just told Ahaz, “the Lord himself shall give you a sign”. Then in chapter 8 the Lord has Isaiah write the name Maher-shalal-hash-baz, quick to the plunder, swift to the spoil, and Isaiah goes unto the prophetess, his wife, and “she conceived, and bare a son.” The child was named before he was conceived, the same way Gabriel named John and named Christ before they were conceived.

Then Isaiah says who the sign is: “Behold, I and the children whom the Lord hath given me are for signs and for wonders in Israel from the Lord of hosts, which dwelleth in mount Zion.” Behold who? I, Isaiah, and the children. Not his wife. He never counts the woman.

So the sign of Isaiah 7:14 was not the virgin; it was the child. The virgin birth was garbage. The birth of Isaiah's son was the sign that Ephraim and Syria banding together against Judah would fail. Before the child could cry “My father, and my mother,” the riches of Damascus and the spoil of Samaria were taken away before the king of Assyria. Assyria would pass through Judah and “reach even to the neck”, coming close to conquering but failing, because of Immanuel: “Take counsel together, and it shall come to nought; speak the word, and it shall not stand: for God is with us.” Once Isaiah's son was born, the two kings could not succeed against Judah.

precepts.label: Ezekiel 12:6
precepts.why:
The Lord told Ezekiel to bear his stuff on his shoulders in their sight and carry it forth in the twilight, covering his face “that thou see not the ground: for I have set thee for a sign unto the house of Israel.” God made Ezekiel himself a sign unto the house of Israel.

Read on to verse 11 and Ezekiel is told to say it to Israel plainly: “Say, I am your sign: like as I have done, so shall it be done unto them: they shall remove and go into captivity.” What the prophet did, Israel would go through.

This lines up with Isaiah 8. When the Lord gives a sign, it is the man and the child he gives, not the woman. Isaiah and his children were signs and wonders in Israel, and Ezekiel was set for a sign to the house of Israel, which is why the sign of Isaiah 7:14 is the child born to Isaiah and the prophetess.

precepts.label: Ezekiel 24:24
precepts.why:
“Thus Ezekiel is unto you a sign.” What is he? A sign. Not his wife: Ezekiel. “according to all that he hath done shall ye do: and when this cometh, ye shall know that I am the Lord God.”

The Lord told Ezekiel to eat dung, and what did we end up doing? Eating dung. He was a sign, and what he did came upon Israel.

Read on to verse 27: “thou shalt be a sign unto them; and they shall know that I am the Lord.” Again and again the man is the sign. So when Isaiah says “I and the children whom the Lord hath given me are for signs”, it fits the pattern of the prophets: the sign given to Ahaz was the child Isaiah's wife bare, Maher-shalal-hash-baz, not a virgin.

precepts.label: Luke 11:29-30
precepts.why:
When the people were gathered thick together, Christ said, “This is an evil generation: they seek a sign; and there shall no sign be given it, but the sign of Jonas the prophet.” Then: “For as Jonas was a sign unto the Ninevites, so shall also the Son of man be to this generation.”

Jonas was a sign. The Son of man was a sign. Men were always the signs. There is no scripture where the women were signs. Hosea was also a sign, and his marriage was a sign, but the woman by herself was never a sign.

That settles Isaiah 7 and 8. The Lord said he would give Ahaz a sign, and Isaiah tells us who it was: himself and the children the Lord gave him. The son born to Isaiah and the prophetess was the sign that God was with Judah, Immanuel, and that the two kings coming against Judah would come to nought.

thread.text: How art thou fallen from heaven, O Lucifer, son of the morning! how art thou cut down to the ground, which didst weaken the nations!

precepts.label: Lamentations 2:1
precepts.why:
“How art thou fallen from heaven, O Lucifer”: before we can know who Lucifer is, we have to know what heaven is. Lamentations shows it: “How hath the Lord covered the daughter of Zion with a cloud in his anger, and cast down from heaven unto the earth the beauty of Israel.”

Heaven is dominion and rulership. That was the high standard, the high estate Israel held, and the beauty of Israel was cast down from it to the earth. We were set down to a low state. No one thinks Israel was literally thrown out of the sky; we fell from rulership.

So it is with Lucifer. Esau takes Jude and Isaiah 14, mixes them up and comes with this fallen angel teaching. But keep it in context. Lucifer, the lightbearer, is the king of Babylon of verse 4, the oppressor, the one who “smote the people in wrath with a continual stroke.” It is talking about a nation: this so-called white man, America, whom everybody looks at as god and all knowing because he controls communication everywhere.

He is falling from heaven the same way Israel did: he is losing his dominion and his rulership. “They that see thee shall narrowly look upon thee, and consider thee, saying, Is this the man that made the earth to tremble”: not a fallen angel, not the Nephilim, but the man, the one who made the earth tremble by dropping atom bombs everywhere. The angels are not falling out of heaven; they take their directive from the Most High God.

precepts.label: Daniel 7:27
precepts.why:
Daniel shows again what heaven means: “And the kingdom and dominion, and the greatness of the kingdom under the whole heaven, shall be given to the people of the saints of the most High.” That is rulership. The greatness of the kingdom under the whole heaven is dominion over the nations, and it is given to the saints of the Most High, Israel.

So when Isaiah says “How art thou fallen from heaven, O Lucifer, son of the morning! how art thou cut down to the ground, which didst weaken the nations!”, it is the fall of a ruler from his dominion. How did you fall from rulership? Lucifer is the king of Babylon, the oppressor who weakened the nations with his bombs, his lies and his fornication.

He said in his heart, “I will ascend into heaven, I will exalt my throne above the stars of God: I will sit also upon the mount of the congregation, in the sides of the north”, North America, and “I will be like the most High.” “Yet thou shalt be brought down to hell, to the sides of the pit.”

Put the two together. The rulership he grasped at, he loses, and the kingdom and dominion under the whole heaven is given to the people of the saints of the Most High. It is not an angel cast out of the sky; it is the man, this so-called white man, America, brought down, and Israel lifted up to rule.

precepts.label: Revelation 11:8
precepts.why:
“The burden of Egypt.” Egypt was before Isaiah’s time, so what Egypt is this speaking about? Revelation answers it: “their dead bodies shall lie in the street of the great city, which spiritually is called Sodom and Egypt, where also our Lord was crucified.”

It says spiritually. Sodom is not around anymore; it is destroyed, those cities of Sodom and Gomorrah near Ein Bokek are nothing. But spiritual Sodom is here. It goes on even in the landmass of Israel among the Israelis, but prominently and predominately here in America, with all types of switcheroos: men acting like women and women acting like men, committing things contrary to the laws of God. And it is spiritual Egypt, the house of bondage. So replace Egypt with America: the burden of America.

“where also our Lord was crucified.” They crucify Christ in his image, in his message, and in denying that you men are the greatest thing on the face of this earth. They say, hell no, all people, God loves everybody.

“And their dead bodies shall lie in the street of the great city.” America is that great city, and our people are spiritually dead here. They are fearful of freedom; there is no spirit in them to rebel with the laws of God.

So when Isaiah says the Lord rides upon a swift cloud and comes into Egypt, it is the Lord coming with his chariots and angels to bring wrath and destruction upon America. Its idols shall be moved at his presence, and its heart, the mindset, doctrines and mentality of the oppressive kingdom, shall melt in the midst of it. He will set the Egyptians against the Egyptians: militia against militia, civil war, brother against brother, city against city. This place is divided; the stars are falling and the stripes are broken. That is Esau rising against himself, and it is not our fight.

“where also our Lord was crucified.” Christ was crucified in Jerusalem, but this is a spiritual crucifixion: they have crucified Christ’s image here and crucified his teachings here.

There will be a civil war in this country.

Christ “will destroy in this mountain the face of the covering cast over all people.” Somebody might ask, what mountain is this? Mount Ararat, Mount Fuji, Mount Kilimanjaro? No. Isaiah 13 shows it: “The burden of Babylon, which Isaiah the son of Amoz did see.” That is Babylon the great.

thread.label: Isaiah 26:3
thread.text: Thou wilt keep him in perfect peace, whose mind is stayed on thee: because he trusteth in thee.

precepts.label: Jude 1:20-21
precepts.why:
Isaiah says the Lord keeps him in perfect peace “because he trusteth in thee.” That is the key part. You trust in the Lord, you trust in his words, and you build yourself up. Jude says it: “But ye, beloved, building up yourselves on your most holy faith, praying in the Holy Ghost”.

It is the leaders' job to build the man, but once you have the foundation, it is on you to take the notes from the classes, apply them to yourself and add to them. Do a serious checkup from the neck up. Take an erasable dry marker to your mirror and write your issues with the scriptures next to them, what you need to fix, and at the top write: execute. Those are your orders for the day. If you don't see it, you're never going to fix it. Too many brothers and sisters don't write anything down: notes done, Bible closed the rest of the week, and then they're stressing, when the fix to what they were dealing with last week and what they will face this week came out in the class. We don't examine ourselves.

Don't ask the captain what he sees in you. What do you see in you? Leadership has the blessing of discernment, but that only goes so far; we can't see through you or know all the deep recesses of what you're dealing with. You have to go before the Lord, explain it, confess it, and ask him in sincerity to remove those things from you.

Don't play with what you know you are dealing with. The spirits on brothers and sisters who could care less can rub off even on leadership; a lot of brothers and sisters are spiritual vampires, and it takes a toll on leaders who love our people. God has this hospital set up for you to get the help, and the medicine is the laws. You have a headache, you don't throw the Tylenol in the trash, you take it. So why throw away the medicine when it concerns your soul and your salvation? Why be fearful of freedom?

“Keep yourselves in the love of God, looking for the mercy of our Lord Jesus Christ unto eternal life.” Keep yourselves in the love of God, not in the crosshairs of his anger, his rage, his wrath. It is our job to keep ourselves there. I can't save you, and you can't save me. It ain't going to be easy; you have to go through this fiery trial to get the kingdom. So do your part. You have the keys to freedom, and that is the trust that keeps the mind stayed on the Lord in perfect peace.

precepts.label: Joshua 1:8
precepts.why:
What actually brings us peace? Not enlisting in this war, and not hoping America goes back to the old ways. “Thou wilt keep him in perfect peace, whose mind is stayed on thee”. The mind that is stayed on the Lord is the mindset of Joshua 1:8: the book of the law does not depart out of your mouth, and you meditate on it day and night.

That is your four chapters a day. That is you not separating yourself, and having that godly conversation consistently, as in Malachi, where they thought upon the Lord's name and a book of remembrance was written. That is making sure the sick among us in the congregations are well taken care of. That is you men doing the blitz, traveling, doing your due diligence by all manner to get out of that black shirt and get out here and teach your people, to become men of valor and soldiers of the Lord, and put in your brick.

You establish yourself on the laws of God. That is your meditation, your chief joy. You're not worried about what is played on the radio, and you could give a damn about what's on the internet unless it is funneled through the Bible so you can keep up with the times.

Then the news, the destruction and the chaos won't worry you. You'll have a Coke bottle smile from one ear to the next, because you know the mysteries. You're not fearful of freedom. The mind that meditates on the law day and night is the mind the Lord keeps in perfect peace.

thread.text: Woe to the crown of pride, to the drunkards of Ephraim, whose glorious beauty is a fading flower, which are on the head of the fat valleys of them that are overcome with wine!

classes.title: The Pride Of Thine Heart

precepts.label: Jeremiah 13:9-17
precepts.why:
Every kingdom on earth has failed because of pride, even ours. Isaiah says “Woe to the crown of pride, to the drunkards of Ephraim”: the northern kingdom fell because of pride. They separated from God, went to the north and said, we are doing our own thing. It goes back to the split between Rehoboam and Jeroboam. Rehoboam could have listened to the elders who were already there to run the nation correctly, but he mocked the leadership above him and dealt with his buddies, and we are in the condition we are in today because of that pride.

The northern kingdom was the first to fall, but the southern kingdom was not exempt. “Thus saith the Lord, After this manner will I mar the pride of Judah, and the great pride of Jerusalem.” Judah looked at what their brother was doing and followed right after their treacherous sister Israel. The great pride of Jerusalem takes in Benjamin and Levi too: all of the southern kingdom was full of pride in God's eyes.

“This evil people, which refuse to hear my words, which walk in the imagination of their heart, and walk after other gods, to serve them, and to worship them, shall even be as this girdle, which is good for nothing.” When pride comes, you separate yourself from your maker, as Sirach 10 says, and walk after your own heart. When you are full of pride you are good for nothing in God's eyes.

Then the judgment for it: “And I will dash them one against another, even the fathers and the sons together, saith the Lord: I will not pity, nor spare, nor have mercy, but destroy them.” Pride destroyed the kingdom, and it destroys every kingdom.

“Hear ye, and give ear; be not proud: for the Lord hath spoken.” You better listen up, Israel, and not separate yourself from him. He is our creator and he controls all of this, so you better humble yourself and do as he tells you. This could be over right now if all of us said, Lord, I'm done with pride, I humble myself, what do you want me to do? And Christ would crack the sky.

But not on the surface, saying forgive me and then waiting till you get out of here. You are not fooling God. That is why we are still here as a people: even those of us that repented are not ready to go back to the kingdom yet. And pride is not always loud. It can be subtle, shutting down, thinking you can do it on your own, and Satan still has you there.

precepts.label: Amos 5:10
precepts.why:
Isaiah says the terrible one, Edom, is brought to nought: the one that does terrible things to the nations behind the cloak, behind the scenes, to maintain power and authority on the earth, destroyed as Ezekiel 35 said. The scorner is consumed, and all that watch for iniquity are cut off, those “That make a man an offender for a word, and lay a snare for him that reproveth in the gate.” Who is the one that reproveth in the gate? Amos answers: “They hate him that rebuketh in the gate, and they abhor him that speaketh uprightly.”

They hate him that rebukes in the gate, in the streets. They abhor him that speaks uprightly. That is the one teaching in the streets, and that is who they lay the snares for, in the legal system, in their music and their media.

So they will pass laws to make those of us who reprove offenders for our words. Say certain things and you face jail time, imprisonment, exile, banishment; they are even trying to pass laws where you can be put to death, talking about bringing back beheadings and the guillotine. They will call it hate speech, terrorism, treason, being unpatriotic. You are anti-MAGA, against abortion, against same-sex, against white supremacy? Lock that brother up, lock that sister up. You say you are an Israelite, that they are fake Jews? Hate speech; five years; fire them from their job; fine them thousands; put a lien on their house.

They will do it because they can, and they will. But the most frightening one to them is the one they cannot kill, the righteous one they cannot pay off, bribe, drug, slander, poison or shoot. And Isaiah’s end is sure: the terrible one is brought to nought, and all that lay snares for him that reproveth in the gate are cut off.

precepts.label: Proverbs 16:27
precepts.why:
The first sign of a bitter brother is that he is easily offended; he will “make a man an offender for a word”. The next sign is that he holds grudges, the thing Leviticus 19:18 forbids: “Thou shalt not avenge, nor bear any grudge against the children of thy people”. And he is always revisiting past wrongs.

Proverbs names him: “An ungodly man diggeth up evil”. That is the bitter brother digging up evil, the plumber brother, digging up old ish. As we say up in the States, he's digging it up like he's a plumber.

“and in his lips there is as a burning fire.” That is deceit, and he is always hating. That is the brother with the banana on his lips, the certified hater like Cain: I don't like that. That's you.

So the one who makes a man an offender for a word is the same one who keeps digging up the old things. He lacks forgiveness, as Sirach 28 showed, and he will not let the past rest. Brother, you are not in the right spirit.

precepts.label: Ecclesiasticus 20:22
precepts.why:
Another sign of bitterness is quiet resentment: they sit back and stew in silence. Sirach shows that brother: “There is that destroyeth his own soul through bashfulness”. He is the bitter bashful brother, brother BB.

precepts.label: Romans 9:21-23
precepts.why:
“For my sword shall be bathed in heaven: behold, it shall come down upon Idumea, and upon the people of my curse, to judgment.” Who is in heaven? Edom, the ruling kingdom of today. We read “the people of my curse” all the time, so look at the other versions. The NIV says the people he has totally destroyed; the NLT, the nation marked for destruction; the ESV and Berean, the people devoted to destruction; the New American Standard, the people designated for destruction. That is their purpose: to be destroyed. Paul says the same.

“Hath not the potter power over the clay, of the same lump to make one vessel unto honour, and another unto dishonour?” The same lump is Isaac. One child was made for honour and one child was made for dishonour, of the same lump.

“What if God, willing to shew his wrath, and to make his power known, endured with much longsuffering the vessels of wrath fitted to destruction.” Which child of Isaac was the vessel of wrath fitted to destruction? Edom, just as Isaiah 34 said.

“And that he might make known the riches of his glory on the vessels of mercy, which he had afore prepared unto glory.” Who are the vessels of mercy? We are.

So Edom is prepared, predestined for destruction in totality. There is no saving any of them, no matter how good you think they are, no matter how much you love grandma and mama. They are getting destroyed. And they are the robbers of our people: Khazarian royals who fled to Spain and became conquistadors, who took over Israel to be the Jews and took over the natives over here to be Christians.

precepts.label: Zechariah 12:3
precepts.why:
“For the Lord hath a sacrifice in Bozrah, and a great slaughter in the land of Idumea.” Bozrah was the capital of Edom, and the land of Idumea is the land of Israel today, the Middle East, the Near East. “Their land shall be soaked with blood” … “For it is the day of the Lord’s vengeance, and the year of recompences for the controversy of Zion.” What is the controversy of Zion? Zechariah answers.

“And in that day will I make Jerusalem a burdensome stone for all people: all that burden themselves with it shall be cut in pieces, though all the people of the earth be gathered together against it.” God makes Jerusalem a burdensome stone to whoever holds it. These Israelis are trying to hold on to that land and spread it and expand it as much as they can, but it is becoming a burdensome stone to them, because they are not the chosen people of God and it doesn't belong to them.

Zechariah 14 shows it: all nations gathered against Jerusalem, the city taken, and then the Lord goes forth to fight and his feet stand on the Mount of Olives, and after that “there shall be no more utter destruction; but Jerusalem shall be safely inhabited.” Isaiah 60 says “Violence shall no more be heard in thy land” and “Thy people also shall be all righteous.” Ezekiel 38 says they “shall dwell safely all of them”, without walls, bars or gates.

Are the Israelis dwelling safely right now? No. They are in unsanitary bomb shelters, running and hiding and crying, behind walls. Where is their God at? The Messiah must return for us to get into the land, not before. That is why they are getting blown to hell over there: they don't belong there, and Jerusalem is cutting them in pieces.
