precepts.label: 1 Esdras 5:72-73
precepts.why:
Haggai brings the word to Zerubbabel the governor and Joshua the high priest: “This people say, The time is not come, the time that the Lord’s house should be built.” Why were they saying that? First Esdras shows what was happening: “But the heathen of the land lying heavy upon the inhabitants of Judea, and holding them strait, hindered their building”.

They were hindering the building of the temple. “And by their secret plots, and popular persuasions and commotions, they hindered the finishing of the building all the time that king Cyrus lived: so they were hindered from building for the space of two years, until the reign of Darius.” See that: secret plots, persuading the multitude to go against us, causing commotions.

So everybody was discouraged, with all the other nations hindering them, and they said, maybe this is not the time for the temple to be built. Zerubbabel and Joshua stopped building. Then God raised up Haggai and Zechariah to blast the high priest and the governor so they would go back to the work, and they finished it in the sixth year of the reign of Darius.

That is why it is important to read your four chapters a day. Captains, make sure your soldiers are reading, so they graduate properly at the end of the year having read the whole Bible; then you know the history behind a verse like Haggai 1:2. And the lesson stands for us: the enemy's plots are no reason to let the Lord's house lie waste while we dwell in our cieled houses.

precepts.label: 2 Corinthians 13:5
precepts.why:
Haggai says, “Now therefore thus saith the Lord of hosts; Consider your ways.” Do you know what consider your ways means? Examine yourself. Paul says it: “Examine yourselves, whether ye be in the faith; prove your own selves. Know ye not your own selves, how that Jesus Christ is in you, except ye be reprobates?”

If you don't know Christ is in you, you are reprobate. That is what all of us have to do: examine ourselves day by day. And don't say consider your ways was only for Zerubbabel; it is not.

Haggai shows what happens when we don't. “Ye have sown much, and bring in little”: you worked a lot with little profit to show for it. “Ye eat, but ye have not enough ... and he that earneth wages earneth wages to put it into a bag with holes.” I just worked 48, 52 hours, and I don't have enough money to show for it. That was going on with Zerubbabel, and it is why many of us are always struggling: because God is second or third in your life, just like Zerubbabel. “Because of mine house that is waste, and ye run every man unto his own house.”

When Zerubbabel and Joshua heard it, they “obeyed the voice of the Lord their God, and the words of Haggai the prophet”. Haggai was not governor or high priest, but they humbled themselves, because they knew it was the word of the Lord. They did not say, arrest him. That is how we have to be. When we correct a brother he takes it personal, like we stabbed his mama; correct his wife and he says you are trying to destroy my marriage. No, we are trying to help. That's love. Examine yourself and fix your life.

precepts.label: Ezra 3:12-13
precepts.why:
“Who is left among you that saw this house in her first glory? and how do ye see it now? is it not in your eyes in comparison of it as nothing?” They had been in Babylon for 70 years; Cyrus came in at the end of the 70 years, then Darius. So the question is, who is still alive that saw the temple Solomon built? When they rebuilt the temple, it did not look half as good as what Solomon had built.

Ezra shows those men: “But many of the priests and Levites and chief of the fathers, who were ancient men, that had seen the first house, when the foundation of this house was laid before their eyes, wept with a loud voice”. Old men who had seen Solomon's temple cried with a loud voice.

“and many shouted aloud for joy: So that the people could not discern the noise of the shout of joy from the noise of the weeping of the people: for the people shouted with a loud shout, and the noise was heard afar off.” The young rejoiced at a foundation; the ancient men wept, because in their eyes it was as nothing in comparison to the first glory.

That house Zerubbabel rebuilt was completed around 515 BC, but it did not compare. That is why, in the time of Rome, Herod the Edomite would come and renovate it to make it look good.

precepts.label: Jeremiah 22:13
precepts.why:
The second temple did not look good in comparison to Solomon's, so King Herod the Great, around 20 to 19 BC, began a massive expansion and renovation: to beautify the site, impress the Roman world, and win favor with his Jewish subjects. He doubled the Temple Mount platform with giant retaining walls, used enormous white limestone blocks, some over 500 tons, trimmed the temple with gold, and added grand colonnades, entry gates and spacious public spaces for worshippers and pilgrims. That last part means the other nations now had a place to come and look at what was going on in the temple. That was not in the original design God gave us. Herod added it.

Jeremiah is read against that building: “Woe unto him that buildeth his house by unrighteousness, and his chambers by wrong; that useth his neighbour’s service without wages, and giveth him not for his work”.

Herod was an Idumean, an Edomite, despised by the Judahites because he was not one of their own stock. He hated the people of Judah, executed forty-five of their leaders, and destroyed the priestly line of Hyrcanus. All that building was to get in good graces, and it was built by unrighteousness and by wrong.

precepts.label: Matthew 11:12
precepts.why:
Herod the Edomite rebuilt the temple to win favor with the Jews and impress Rome. Christ spoke of what was happening in his day: “And from the days of John the Baptist until now the kingdom of heaven suffereth violence, and the violent take it by force.”

Who are the violent Christ was talking about? Rome. Rome took the kingdom by force.

And in the years just before the time of Christ, Judea was controlled by an Edomite faction who usurped the Judahite name, land and heritage. Usurped the name means they became Jewish: we are converts, we are Jews now. That is what Herod was doing. Historically the Edomites became known as Jews, derived from Judea and from Judah, though they were never of Judah or Israel. The violent took the kingdom by force, and then they took the name.

precepts.label: John 10:10
precepts.why:
Christ said: “The thief cometh not, but for to steal, and to kill, and to destroy: I am come that they might have life, and that they might have it more abundantly.” Who is he talking about? Rome. Remember, Herod was an Idumean, and Rome were Idumeans: they were the same race.

That thief stole the name. Their own book, written by Esau and not by a negro, says the Jews of today are of two types, the Sephardic and the Ashkenazi. Initially we were the Sephardim in Spain; when they conquered us and cast us out, Esau became the Sephardic ones. The Ashkenazi, 90 percent of the so-called Jews, came from the Khazars, and their own Jewish Encyclopedia says the Khazars are of Edomite stock, from the land of Edom. We had to find out whether they were Japheth or Esau, and their own sources answer it. We have second, third and fourth book sources, and the Bible is always our main source.

“Jacob have I loved, but Esau have I hated.” God calls Edom “the people of my curse”. If God hated you and your ancestors, you would want to hide that you are Esau. That is why they claim to be Israel, form the Anti-Defamation League, push hate crime laws, and infiltrate the churches. The thief came to steal, kill and destroy; Christ came that we might have life.

precepts.label: Psalms 78:68
precepts.why:
“Ho, ho, come forth, and flee from the land of the north, saith the Lord”: the land of the north is North America. “for I have spread you abroad as the four winds of the heaven.” Then: “Deliver thyself, O Zion, that dwellest with the daughter of Babylon.” Which Zion?

“But chose the tribe of Judah, the mount Zion which he loved.” The Lord chose the tribe of Judah, mount Zion. So we know that the Zion dwelling with the daughter of Babylon is Judah: deliver thyself, O Judah.

Benjamin does not dwell with the daughter of Babylon; they are on a nice, pleasant island. Levi does not dwell with the daughter of Babylon. That's why all the tribes make fun of Judah: we have places to go back to when we want to run; y'all have no place to go. Why? Because Judah dwells with the daughter of Babylon, with Edom, in North America.

“For thus saith the Lord of hosts; After the glory hath he sent me unto the nations which spoiled you: for he that toucheth you toucheth the apple of his eye”: he that touches you touches my favorite. “For, behold, I will shake mine hand upon them, and they shall be a spoil to their servants”: Edom shall be a spoil to us, and we are the servants here. “and ye shall know that the Lord of hosts hath sent me.”

precepts.label: Isaiah 11:12
precepts.why:
People will hear us teaching and say, oh, you're saying all Judah is in North America. No, that's not what we're saying, just like we know all Levi is not on the island of Haiti, and all Benjamin is not on the island of Jamaica or Trinidad. “And he shall set up an ensign for the nations, and shall assemble the outcasts of Israel, and gather together the dispersed of Judah from the four corners of the earth.” Israel and Judah were scattered worldwide.

Zechariah is pointing out a remnant of Judah that is in North America. And what's so special about this group here? The house of David is here. You are going to find that thing out.

Why are they so hard on Judah here as opposed to Judah scattered elsewhere? The civil rights hearings of 1959 before the Senate, under the title American Negro problems, say it: the Negro question in the United States of America must be treated in its relation to the huge Negro masses oppressed and exploited by white imperialism in Africa and South America, and the Negroes of the United States are the most advanced section of the Negro population of the world and can play a decisive role in helping and leading the liberation movement of the Negro colonies. You have Negroes in Jamaica, Haiti, Africa, Saudi Arabia; Judah is everywhere, the southern kingdom is everywhere. But the white man examined all the Negro populations and said the American Negro is the most advanced.

Deacon Malachi brought it out: when Nebuchadnezzar came against Judah, they took the best of the best, the most educated. Esau isn't stupid; he knows that history. At Elmina Castle in Ghana, the tour guide said it himself: you never ask why the American black is more advanced; when they came to Africa, they took the best of them. Look right after slavery, without even reparations, how the blacks here advanced, and how they came and dropped bombs and destroyed them. That's why Esau always has his eye on the American blacks: that group here is more dangerous than all the other groups where the blacks are. And that's why the Lord said, “The Lord also shall save the tents of Judah first.” It isn't Judah over in Africa or in Saudi Arabia. It's Judah here. This history you should be proud of.

classes.title: The Nativity: the Bloodline, Birthright, & the Messiah

precepts.label: Zechariah 4:7
precepts.why:
“for, behold, I will bring forth my servant the BRANCH.” Who is that? Christ. And the next chapter says who brings him forth: “Who art thou, O great mountain? before Zerubbabel thou shalt become a plain.” The great mountain is Babylon, made a plain, destroyed.

“and he shall bring forth the headstone thereof with shoutings, crying, Grace, grace unto it.” Who shall bring forth the headstone? Zerubbabel. Chapter 3 said the Lord will bring forth his servant the Branch; here Zerubbabel brings forth the headstone, which is the same as the Branch. And the headstone brings grace unto us.

How will Zerubbabel bring him forth? Through his line. And Zerubbabel comes out of Solomon's line. Matthew 1 shows it: “And after they were brought to Babylon, Jechonias begat Salathiel; and Salathiel begat Zorobabel”, born in Babylon, and from Zorobabel down to “Jacob begat Joseph the husband of Mary, of whom was born Jesus, who is called Christ.” Joseph comes out of the line of kings, the kingdom of Solomon, heir to the throne, but in captivity, with Rome calling the shots and an Edomite, Herod, on the throne, until Christ returns and conquers Edom. There is no scripture that says Jeconiah's line was cursed from being kings; that doctrine was made to justify a virgin birth. The Zerubbabel of Luke 3 is a different one, of Nathan's line: Joseph is written there because he inherited Heli's inheritance as his son-in-law, Heli being Mary's father with no sons.

precepts.label: Psalms 118:22
precepts.why:
Zechariah says, “For behold the stone that I have laid before Joshua; upon one stone shall be seven eyes.” The Branch and the stone are Christ. Then Zerubbabel “shall bring forth the headstone thereof.”

What is the headstone? “The stone which the builders refused is become the head stone of the corner.” Who is the Branch, who is the stone? It's the same thing. The headstone Zerubbabel brings forth is the same stone laid before Joshua, and the same servant the Branch the Lord said he would bring forth: Christ, refused by the builders and made the head of the corner.

So when the Lord says “I will remove the iniquity of that land in one day”, he is going into Christ. The stone laid before Joshua the high priest and his fellows, men wondered at for a sign, is the Christ who would come through Zerubbabel's loins.

precepts.label: Ephesians 2:20
precepts.why:
Zerubbabel built the second temple, so he brought forth a literal stone with a foundation. That's the first level. But it is twofold: he also brought forth the other stone through his loins, to build up the temple which is us here in the room.

“And are built upon the foundation of the apostles and prophets, Jesus Christ himself being the chief corner stone”: the chief corner stone, the headstone. “In whom all the building fitly framed together groweth unto an holy temple in the Lord”: that's us. “In whom ye also are builded together for an habitation of God through the Spirit.”

So we are that holy temple that Christ builds. Zerubbabel laid the foundation of the second temple, and he brought forth the same stone and the same foundation, which is Christ, on whom we are built. Praise the Lord for that.

thread.label: Zechariah 3:8-10
thread.text: Hear now, O Joshua the high priest, thou, and thy fellows that sit before thee: for they are men wondered at: for, behold, I will bring forth my servant the BRANCH.

precepts.label: Jeremiah 23:5-6
precepts.why:
In the Persian captivity there was Joshua the high priest, of the tribe of Levi, and Zerubbabel the governor, of the tribe of Judah. The Lord speaks to Joshua and his fellows, “for, behold, I will bring forth my servant the BRANCH.” The Branch is Christ, and Jeremiah 23 shows it.

“Behold, the days come, saith the Lord, that I will raise unto David a righteous Branch, and a King shall reign and prosper, and shall execute judgment and justice in the earth.” The righteous Branch raised unto David is Christ, the King who will reign and execute justice.

“In his days Judah shall be saved, and Israel shall dwell safely: and this is his name whereby he shall be called, THE LORD OUR RIGHTEOUSNESS.” That is the same day Zechariah speaks of. The stone laid before Joshua with its seven eyes, and those eyes are the angels. “I will remove the iniquity of that land in one day”: that is Christ dying on the cross. And “In that day”, every man shall call his neighbour “under the vine and under the fig tree”: that is in the kingdom, when Israel dwells safely under the Branch.

precepts.label: Zechariah 6:12-13
precepts.why:
The Branch appears again in Zechariah 6: “Behold the man whose name is The BRANCH; and he shall grow up out of his place, and he shall build the temple of the Lord.” That is not the second temple; it is about the third and the fourth.

“Even he shall build the temple of the Lord; and he shall bear the glory, and shall sit and rule upon his throne; and he shall be a priest upon his throne: and the counsel of peace shall be between them both.” Both is the priesthood and the kingship. He sits and rules on his throne as a king, and he is a priest on that same throne.

That is why Zechariah 3 speaks to Joshua the high priest, and why Zerubbabel the governor stands alongside him: the priest from Levi and the ruler from Judah. Christ fulfilled both offices, the priesthood and the kingship, in one man, the Branch.

precepts.label: Genesis 49:10
precepts.why:
The priesthood and the kingship that Christ fulfilled go back to Jacob's blessing on Judah: “The sceptre shall not depart from Judah”: the kingship shall not depart from Judah. “nor a lawgiver from between his feet”: that is the priesthood, and what is between a man's feet is his rod. It shows Christ would come from the rod. There is no immaculate anything; that is make-believe, Egyptian and Babylonian fairy tales. “until Shiloh come”: that is the Messiah, Christ. “and unto him shall the gathering of the people be.”

Matthew 1 traces the line through the captivity. “And after they were brought to Babylon, Jechonias begat Salathiel; and Salathiel begat Zorobabel”, and so down to “Jacob begat Joseph the husband of Mary, of whom was born Jesus, who is called Christ.” That is the Branch coming out of Zerubbabel, the governor who stood with Joshua the high priest.

In the sit-down with Captain Matathias and Captain Galiah, the dude with that stupid hat argued there was a curse on Jechonias that no one of his seed would sit as king, so the genealogy is ruled out. But after Babylon came in, that was it: Zedekiah was taken away and his sons were killed, and no king sat on the throne in Israel. There was no king in the time of Christ. When he came, the people loved him so much that they wanted to “take him by force, to make him a king”, and “he departed again into a mountain himself alone.” By the prophets, there would be no more king until Christ returns: the sceptre waits for Shiloh.

thread.label: Zechariah 4:6-9
thread.text: Then he answered and spake unto me, saying, This is the word of the Lord unto Zerubbabel, saying, Not by might, nor by power, but by my spirit, saith the Lord of hosts.

precepts.label: Psalms 118:22
precepts.why:
Zerubbabel is the branch in the line of Christ: Matthew's genealogy runs from Zerubbabel through Abiud, Eliakim, Azor, Sadoc, Achim, Eliud, Eleazar, Matthan and Jacob to “Joseph the husband of Mary, of whom was born Jesus, who is called Christ.” So when the Lord speaks to Zerubbabel, he is speaking to the father of Christ's line.

“Not by might, nor by power, but by my spirit, saith the Lord of hosts.” Zerubbabel was of the king's bodyguard, one of the top fighters. The Lord is telling him, no, this has nothing to do with your fighting skills; we know you can break bones, but that's not what is going to overcome everything. The spirit of the Lord is what's going to do it.

“Who art thou, O great mountain? before Zerubbabel thou shalt become a plain.” The great mountain is Babylon the great, and it shall become a plain: flattened, destroyed. “and he shall bring forth the headstone thereof with shoutings, crying, Grace, grace unto it”: crying mercy, mercy unto it.

What is the headstone? “The stone which the builders refused is become the head stone of the corner.” Who is that? Christ. He is the headstone. Not only would Christ come from Zerubbabel's lineage; Zerubbabel shall bring forth the headstone.

“The hands of Zerubbabel have laid the foundation of this house; his hands shall also finish it.” His hands started the foundation of the temple, and he did finish the temple. But this goes deeper than that: because of verse 7, verses 6 through 9 are going into the last days as well, when the great mountain, Babylon the great, is brought down to a plain and the headstone, Christ, is brought forth.

thread.label: Zechariah 4:6-7
thread.text: Then he answered and spake unto me, saying, This is the word of the Lord unto Zerubbabel, saying, Not by might, nor by power, but by my spirit, saith the Lord of hosts.

precepts.label: Jeremiah 51:24-26
precepts.why:
Zechariah asks, “Who art thou, O great mountain? before Zerubbabel thou shalt become a plain”. Zerubbabel was in the Persian captivity, and Babylon was already destroyed by Persia. So who is this great mountain? Jeremiah shows where the mountain is: “And I will render unto Babylon and to all the inhabitants of Chaldea all their evil that they have done in Zion in your sight, saith the Lord.”

Watch what he calls Babylon: “Behold, I am against thee, O destroying mountain, saith the Lord, which destroyest all the earth: and I will stretch out mine hand upon thee, and roll thee down from the rocks, and will make thee a burnt mountain.” The great mountain is Babylon.

“And they shall not take of thee a stone for a corner, nor a stone for foundations; but thou shalt be desolate for ever, saith the Lord.” That lets you know it is not Iraq. Are people still living in Iraq today? Yes. This says “thou shalt be desolate for ever”, so it is not talking about ancient Babylon.

So the great mountain before Zerubbabel is Babylon to come: Babylon the great. Before him it becomes a plain, flattened and destroyed, and it is done “Not by might, nor by power, but by my spirit, saith the Lord of hosts.” Everything we do must be according to the spirit of the Most High God; it has nothing to do with our physical powers and our skills.

precepts.label: Isaiah 19:18-20
precepts.why:
Zechariah says Zerubbabel “shall bring forth the headstone thereof with shoutings, crying, Grace, grace unto it.” Who is the headstone? Christ. Why are they crying grace, grace? Isaiah shows it, and shows that Zerubbabel is in these last days as well: “In that day shall five cities in the land of Egypt speak the language of Canaan, and swear to the Lord of hosts; one shall be called, The city of destruction.”

The language of Canaan is the scriptures, and one city shall be destroyed. “In that day shall there be an altar to the Lord in the midst of the land of Egypt, and a pillar at the border thereof to the Lord.” An altar is for sacrifice, and this is talking about where the Israelites are: here in Babylon the great.

“And it shall be for a sign and for a witness unto the Lord of hosts in the land of Egypt: for they shall cry unto the Lord because of the oppressors, and he shall send them a saviour, and a great one, and he shall deliver them.” Who is that saviour? Christ.

So Zechariah is saying the same thing. The headstone is that saviour we just read about in Isaiah, and the crying of grace, grace is because of the oppressor. The great mountain, Babylon the great, becomes a plain before him, and he delivers his people out of the land where they cried.

precepts.label: 2 Chronicles 20:12
precepts.why:
“The burden of the word of the Lord in the land of Hadrach, and Damascus shall be the rest thereof”: this is Syria. And it comes “when the eyes of man, as of all the tribes of Israel, shall be toward the Lord.” All the eyes of Israel, our people, shall be toward the Lord.

2 Chronicles 20:12 has the wording for it: “O our God, wilt thou not judge them? for we have no might against this great company that cometh against us; neither know we what to do: but our eyes are upon thee.” That is what we are saying to the Lord.

The nations are at war around Syria, Lebanon, Gaza and Ashkelon, and we have no might against that great company. We do not know what to do. So we keep our eyes on the Lord, and we have to put our attention toward him. That is the moment Zechariah is speaking of, when the burden of the Lord falls on those lands and all the tribes of Israel look to him.

precepts.label: Leviticus 17:10-14
precepts.why:
Zechariah 9:7 says “And I will take away his blood out of his mouth, and his abominations from between his teeth”. First the scripture about blood: “whatsoever man there be of the house of Israel, or of the strangers that sojourn among you, that eateth any manner of blood; I will even set my face against that soul that eateth blood, and will cut him off from among his people. For the life of the flesh is in the blood”.

“Therefore I said unto the children of Israel, No soul of you shall eat blood”. Whoever hunts and catches a beast or fowl “shall even pour out the blood thereof, and cover it with dust.” “Ye shall eat the blood of no manner of flesh: for the life of all flesh is the blood thereof: whosoever eateth it shall be cut off.” That includes those of you who came from Santo Domingo: you are not to be eating blood sausage, black sausage. Don't eat that.

Now look at the blood in his mouth and the abomination between his teeth. These people, these bastards in Ashdod, in the ritual they call metzitzah b'peh, remove the foreskin of the baby and put their mouth on the wound and suck the blood from it. Infants have caught herpes from it, and the rabbis in New York negotiate to keep doing it. That is an abomination from between your teeth. What the hell is wrong with you? Your mom ain't teach you nothing?

One man called them a militarized vampire nation, living on death and destruction, on blood. Ezekiel 35:5-6 says it of Esau: because thou hast had a perpetual hatred and shed the blood of the children of Israel, “sith thou hast not hated blood, even blood shall pursue thee.” The Most High is exposing them: the bloody mattress and baby clothes in the tunnels in Brooklyn, the baby clothes and toys on Epstein Island. God will take away the blood out of his mouth.

precepts.label: 2 Samuel 5:8
precepts.why:
Zechariah 9:7 ends: “but he that remaineth, even he, shall be for our God, and he shall be as a governor in Judah, and Ekron as a Jebusite.” He that remaineth is you and I. And on the map, Ekron sits right there above Jerusalem.

What does it mean to be as a Jebusite? “And David said on that day, Whosoever getteth up to the gutter, and smiteth the Jebusites, and the lame and the blind, that are hated of David’s soul, he shall be chief and captain. Wherefore they said, The blind and the lame shall not come into the house. So David dwelt in the fort, and called it the city of David.”

When you read the history, David smote the Jebusites and made them servants. That is what he did. So when Zechariah says “Ekron as a Jebusite”, the land that the Philistines hold will be brought under Israel the way David brought the Jebusites under him.

precepts.label: 1 Kings 9:20-21
precepts.why:
“And all the people that were left of the Amorites, Hittites, Perizzites, Hivites, and Jebusites, which were not of the children of Israel, Their children that were left after them in the land, whom the children of Israel also were not able utterly to destroy, upon those did Solomon levy a tribute of bondservice unto this day.”

They were our servants, our slaves. The Jebusites left in the land did not rule over Israel; Solomon put them under a tribute of bondservice.

So when we go back to the last part of Zechariah 9:7, “and Ekron as a Jebusite”, it means they are going to be our servants. Those that are left of the Philistines will be to Israel what the Jebusites were to David and Solomon, while he that remaineth of Israel “shall be as a governor in Judah.” The pride of the Philistines is cut off, and the order is turned back the way God set it.

precepts.label: Exodus 2:25
precepts.why:
Zechariah 9:8: “And I will encamp about mine house because of the army, because of him that passeth by, and because of him that returneth: and no oppressor shall pass through them any more: for now have I seen with mine eyes.” No oppressor shall oppress us any more; they will not pass through.

And “now have I seen with mine eyes” is the same as Exodus 2:25: “And God looked upon the children of Israel, and God had respect unto them.” In Egypt God looked upon Israel under their oppressors and had respect unto them, and then he brought them out.

So when he says now have I seen with mine eyes, he is looking upon us to have respect unto us. The Lord encamps about his house, the oppressor is stopped, and right after it Zechariah says “Rejoice greatly, O daughter of Zion”, because the King comes.

thread.text: Rejoice greatly, O daughter of Zion; shout, O daughter of Jerusalem: behold, thy King cometh unto thee: he is just, and having salvation; lowly, and riding upon an ass, and upon a colt the foal of an ass.

precepts.label: Mark 11:4-7
precepts.why:
“Rejoice greatly, O daughter of Zion; shout, O daughter of Jerusalem: behold, thy King cometh unto thee”. We have to believe our king is coming. He “is just, and having salvation; lowly, and riding upon an ass, and upon a colt the foal of an ass.”

Mark shows the history of what Zechariah was prophesying: “And they went their way, and found the colt tied by the door without in a place where two ways met; and they loose him. And certain of them that stood there said unto them, What do ye, loosing the colt? And they said unto them even as Jesus had commanded: and they let them go. And they brought the colt to Jesus, and cast their garments on him; and he sat upon him.”

So when people say Christ isn't mentioned in the Old Testament, shut up; you don't know what you're talking about. Zechariah saw the King of Zion riding upon the colt, and Mark records Christ sitting upon that colt. He is our King, just and having salvation, and he is coming to the daughter of Zion.

precepts.label: Psalms 72:8
precepts.why:
Zechariah says the King “shall speak peace unto the heathen: and his dominion shall be from sea even to sea, and from the river even to the ends of the earth.” David says the same: “He shall have dominion also from sea to sea, and from the river unto the ends of the earth.” And he reads on: “They that dwell in the wilderness shall bow before him; and his enemies shall lick the dust.”

They are scared of the saying from the river to the sea. Well, that's in the Bible too. And it is not just that little area. It is from sea to sea, meaning the whole planet earth is ours. When we went into the land, the Lord gave us that portion according to the number of the children of Israel, but the whole earth really belongs to us, to the ends of the earth.

In that day “I will cut off the chariot from Ephraim, and the horse from Jerusalem, and the battle bow shall be cut off”, meaning we would have no military during that time. The King's dominion is our defence, and his enemies shall lick the dust.

precepts.label: Hebrews 13:20
precepts.why:
Zechariah says, “As for thee also, by the blood of thy covenant I have sent forth thy prisoners out of the pit wherein is no water.” What is the blood of thy covenant? Hebrews shows it: “Now the God of peace, that brought again from the dead our Lord Jesus, that great shepherd of the sheep, through the blood of the everlasting covenant”.

The blood of the everlasting covenant is Christ dying on the cross. By that blood God sends forth his prisoners out of the pit.

If you didn't know it, this is the pit. Like it says, yea, though I walk through the valley of the shadow of death; Ezekiel 37 calls America the valley of dry bones. This is the pit, and “no water” means there is no truth here.

Then Zechariah says, “Turn you to the strong hold, ye prisoners of hope”. We are the prisoners of hope, and the stronghold is the Lord, this Bible: “The Lord is good, a strong hold in the day of trouble; and he knoweth them that trust in him.” By Christ's blood we are brought out of the pit to the stronghold.

thread.text: Turn you to the strong hold, ye prisoners of hope: even to day do I declare that I will render double unto thee;

classes.title: Zionism in the Face of Syria & Hezbollah

precepts.label: Nahum 1:7
precepts.why:
Zechariah says “Turn you to the strong hold, ye prisoners of hope.” Nahum tells us what that stronghold is: “The Lord is good, a strong hold in the day of trouble; and he knoweth them that trust in him.” The stronghold is the Lord, and that means this Bible.

The verse before in Zechariah speaks of the pit “wherein is no water”, meaning there is no truth. That pit is America, the valley of dry bones of Ezekiel 37. Out of that pit, the prisoners are told to turn to the stronghold.

So turning to the stronghold is turning to the Lord and his word. He is good, he is our strong hold in the day of trouble, and he knows them that trust in him. We are the prisoners of hope, and the Bible calls us that.

precepts.label: Proverbs 1:23
precepts.why:
Zechariah says turn you to the stronghold; Proverbs says “Turn you at my reproof: behold, I will pour out my spirit unto you, I will make known my words unto you.” God's reproof is his laws.

So there is a stipulation to get God's Holy Spirit: you must turn at God's reproof. The laws come before the spirit. Only when you turn to his laws will he pour out his spirit on you and make known his words to you.

That is why all these dumb Christians that say they have the Holy Spirit and won't keep a commandment do not have it. They have Satan on them. Turning to the stronghold, for us prisoners of hope, means turning at his reproof and keeping his laws.

precepts.label: John 14:15-18
precepts.why:
More proof that the spirit comes after the laws: Christ said the same thing. “If ye love me, keep my commandments. And I will pray the Father, and he shall give you another Comforter, that he may abide with you for ever”.

Who is that Comforter? “Even the Spirit of truth; whom the world cannot receive, because it seeth him not, neither knoweth him: but ye know him; for he dwelleth with you, and shall be in you.” Then Christ says, “I will not leave you comfortless: I will come to you.” He is letting us know he is the Comforter. It ain't Muhammad. Christ is the Comforter; he is the Holy Spirit.

So the one who turns to the stronghold and keeps the commandments is the one who receives Christ, the Spirit of truth. Those who claim the Holy Spirit and keep no commandment do not have him.

People don't reject the truth because it is false; they reject it because it is uncomfortable. Black and Latino people hate the discomfort of change. But knowledge you won't act on just sits there and becomes nothing, like people who say they want to lose weight, know what to do, and won't do a damn thing.

precepts.label: 1 Peter 3:19-20
precepts.why:
Why does Zechariah call us prisoners of hope? Peter says Christ “went and preached unto the spirits in prison”. When Christ came, he preached to the spirits in prison. That's us: our mothers and fathers, our sons and daughters. We are in a spiritual prison.

When Rome was dominating us, that was a prison. We didn't have free rule; Rome was over us.

Those spirits in prison are the ones “Which sometime were disobedient, when once the longsuffering of God waited in the days of Noah, while the ark was a preparing, wherein few, that is, eight souls were saved by water.” That disobedient people is you and me. We are the prisoners, and our hope is in the stronghold.

precepts.label: Isaiah 61:1
precepts.why:
Isaiah shows what Christ was sent to do for those prisoners: “The Spirit of the Lord God is upon me; because the Lord hath anointed me to preach good tidings unto the meek; he hath sent me to bind up the brokenhearted, to proclaim liberty to the captives, and the opening of the prison to them that are bound”.

We are in a prison house, and we are bound in sin. Christ is anointed to proclaim liberty to us captives and to open the prison to us that are bound.

That is why we are prisoners of hope: the prison is real, but the one anointed to open it has come, and we are told to turn to him, the stronghold.

precepts.label: John 8:32-34
precepts.why:
Christ said, “And ye shall know the truth, and the truth shall make you free.” They answered him, “We be Abraham’s seed, and were never in bondage to any man: how sayest thou, Ye shall be made free?” So they knew being made free referred to being in bondage. They said, we were never slaves.

They couldn't see that Rome was over them. They were paying taxes to Rome and were oblivious to it, because they were rich and wealthy.

So watch what Christ says: “Verily, verily, I say unto you, Whosoever committeth sin is the servant of sin.” He took it down a level: you won't understand what I just said, but you are a servant. You are bound in your sins.

That is the prison of the prisoners of hope: bound under the nations and bound in sin. The truth, turning to the stronghold, is what makes us free.

precepts.label: Romans 6:12-13
precepts.why:
If sin is the prison, Paul tells us how to walk out of it: “Let not sin therefore reign in your mortal body, that ye should obey it in the lusts thereof.” Don't let sin reign, meaning rule, within you.

“Neither yield ye your members as instruments of unrighteousness unto sin: but yield yourselves unto God, as those that are alive from the dead, and your members as instruments of righteousness unto God.”

Our bodies must be vessels of righteousness, used for the commandments of God and nothing else. That is how the prisoners of hope turn to the stronghold: no longer servants of sin, but instruments of righteousness unto God.

precepts.label: Isaiah 61:7-9
precepts.why:
Zechariah says “even to day do I declare that I will render double unto thee”. Isaiah shows what that double is: “For your shame ye shall have double”. The shame we have suffered in captivity after captivity, we shall have double for it.

“and for confusion they shall rejoice in their portion”, because we are a confused people; take a look at TikTok and Instagram. “therefore in their land they shall possess the double: everlasting joy shall be unto them.” God says “I the Lord love judgment, I hate robbery for burnt offering; and I will direct their work in truth, and I will make an everlasting covenant with them.”

Watch the double we are going to get: “And their seed shall be known among the Gentiles, and their offspring among the people: all that see them shall acknowledge them, that they are the seed which the Lord hath blessed.” We have never experienced that. Imagine walking down the street and everybody knows your kids' names and moves the hell out of their way: that's brother so-and-so's kid. All people are going to know our children. That's double.

Write down the chain of events: awakening, which is us waking up; followed by tribulation, and we are between those now; World War III; Armageddon in the midst of that war, where Christ makes his advent; deliverance; wilderness; then kings and priests, rulership.

precepts.label: Isaiah 60:18
precepts.why:
Zechariah ends the day of the Lord with this: “And men shall dwell in it, and there shall be no more utter destruction; but Jerusalem shall be safely inhabited.” The it is the land. When the Lord returns, men shall dwell in it and there shall be no more destruction. Isaiah says the same: “Violence shall no more be heard in thy land, wasting nor destruction within thy borders”.

That is the time when all Israel, all of us, will be in the land. No bombs in Tel Aviv, no bombs in Ashdod, no bombs in Ashkelon, none of that, once the rightful people are rightfully placed in the land. That is not now. “But thou shalt call thy walls Salvation, and thy gates Praise”, because we will be safe living in them.

So if you are the people of the land, why is the war taking place? The prophecy says there will be no more war and destruction in the land once the Lord returns and we get the land. That means you don't belong there. Prophecy shows the Messiah must return for us to get into the land, not before; that is against prophecy. That is why they are getting blown to hell over there.

What is happening now is the first half of Zechariah 14: all nations gathered against Jerusalem to battle, the city taken, the houses rifled, the women ravished. Jerusalem has become “a burdensome stone for all people”: the Israelis are trying to hold on to this land and expand it, and it is becoming a burdensome stone to them, because they are not the chosen people of God. Only when the Lord's feet stand on the mount of Olives, and he is king over all the earth, is violence no more heard in the land.

precepts.label: Isaiah 60:21
precepts.why:
Zechariah says that when the Lord is king over all the earth, “Jerusalem shall be safely inhabited.” Isaiah says who will inhabit it: “Thy people also shall be all righteous: they shall inherit the land for ever”.

Are the people over there in Israel today all righteous? No. So they cannot be the guys, because they are not all righteous. That doesn't make any damn sense at all.

Ezekiel confirms it: in the latter years we come “into the land that is brought back from the sword, and is gathered out of many people, against the mountains of Israel, which have been always waste: but it is brought forth out of the nations, and they shall dwell safely all of them.” Is the land still waste today? Yes, it is even worse now. Are the Israelis dwelling safely right now? No. They are in bomb shelters, running and hiding, crying about how unsanitary the shelters are. Where is their God at? On vacation? With Epstein? With Bibi? Where is the great Hashem at?

The righteous people who inherit the land for ever are the ones brought forth out of the nations, gathered by the Lord when he returns. That is why Joel says he pleads “for my people and for my heritage Israel”: my people and my land, not all people. He is coming to save his people and give the land to his people, and they shall be all righteous.

precepts.label: Malachi 4:1
precepts.why:
The Lord said, “I have created the waster to destroy.” What weapon at that time could have been called the waster? Nothing. Zechariah describes it: “Their flesh shall consume away while they stand upon their feet, and their eyes shall consume away in their holes, and their tongue shall consume away in their mouth.” Could anybody then fathom a weapon that did those things? Malachi shows the day it is fulfilled: “For, behold, the day cometh, that shall burn as an oven”.

The prophets did not know about nuclear weapons and atoms back then. They got these visions and explained them the best they could, and the best way to say it was: the waster. God put it on man to make that instrument, and there will be a day when that plague is fulfilled.

“And all the proud, yea, and all that do wickedly, shall be stubble”: not just Esau and the other nations, but even rebellious Israel, the ones that do not repent. “And the day that cometh shall burn them up, saith the Lord of hosts, that it shall leave them neither root nor branch.” When you burn something it leaves ashes, but with this waster nothing remains. They show dramatic images, but the body does not survive that heat; whatever ash there is is blown into the atmosphere. You are totally gone.

And here is the beauty of it: God put it in their spirit to make that thing, and he is going to use that same thing to end them. The weapon they feel gave them their power, authority and respect, he will turn against them.

precepts.label: 2 Peter 3:9
precepts.why:
Zechariah's plague and Malachi's day that burns as an oven are coming, so why has it not come yet? Peter answers: “The Lord is not slack concerning his promise, as some men count slackness; but is longsuffering to us-ward, not willing that any should perish, but that all should come to repentance.”

The only reason it tarries is that the Lord is waiting for us. It is not really a set time the way we see it: the time is when that set number is sealed, and God knows when that will be. That is why there is no date for it that we are aware of.

“But the day of the Lord will come as a thief in the night”: when you least suspect it, that is when it comes. “In the which the heavens shall pass away with a great noise, and the elements shall melt with fervent heat”. In those days they could not imagine what that sounded like; it sounded terrifying. Now that we understand it, it is no less terrifying, because we know what those nukes can do.

The Lord stays their hand enough that they do not want to use them. They sign treaties against nuclear proliferation because they know if one fires, the other fires back, and it's a wrap, a zero-sum game, the end of the world as they know it. It is like the game Civilization: it lets you build and use a nuke, but once you use it the game ends, because you destroyed the whole earth. The Lord holds it back while he waits for his people to come to repentance.

precepts.label: 2 Peter 3:12
precepts.why:
Peter says, “Seeing then that all these things shall be dissolved, what manner of persons ought ye to be in all holy conversation and godliness, Looking for and hasting unto the coming of the day of God, wherein the heavens being on fire shall be dissolved, and the elements shall melt with fervent heat?” The heavens will be on fire: what else could he be talking about? It is the waster of Zechariah, flesh consuming away while they stand upon their feet.

We hear all this and say, okay, great, but it should move us. What manner of persons ought we to be? In all holiness and godliness. Paul says the same: “Therefore let us not sleep, as do others; but let us watch and be sober.” Sober means don't drink of the mark of the beast, don't drink her wine, don't be so asleep that you think you're an American and nothing is going to touch you. God has not appointed us to wrath; he does not want his elect to be part of that death and destruction.

Looking for and hasting unto that day means you should be able to look boldly and say, I'm looking for it and I want it to come quickly. It is not the time to be divided in BS and simple issues, but to come together stronger and more united, growing in faith and understanding and applying it.

Don't worry that this place is going to be burned away: “Nevertheless we, according to his promise, look for new heavens and a new earth, wherein dwelleth righteousness.” That fire is a baptism by fire that cleanses all the evil and reforms the earth so it is fit for our new forms and for the new kingdom. Thy will be done in earth as it is in heaven: the kingdom is coming down, and this place has to be transformed.

precepts.label: Genesis 36:8
precepts.why:
Malachi moves from one name to the other. God says “Was not Esau Jacob’s brother? saith the Lord: yet I loved Jacob, And I hated Esau,” and then in the next breath, “Whereas Edom saith, We are impoverished.” He goes from Esau to Edom because they are the same man. Genesis 36:8 settles it: “Thus dwelt Esau in mount Seir: Esau is Edom.” There is no argument. Esau is Edom, the one who came out of his mother red, hairy like a garment, and whose name was changed to Edom, meaning red. He became the father of the Edomite nations.

So when Malachi says “I loved Jacob,” it is Jacob and all his descendants, the twelve tribes, the whole nation of Israel. When he says “I hated Esau,” it is Esau and all his nation. God does love us, even though, looking at our condition in the ghetto with everything going wrong, we ask “Wherein hast thou loved us?”

Edom said, “We are impoverished, but we will return and build the desolate places.” Living in the Caucasus Mountains and in the caves, they came back; it is called the Renaissance. They built major cities and took control of the whole earth. But “They shall build, but I will throw down”: the Lord, the God of war, will tear it down.

“they shall call them, The border of wickedness”: not him, but them, all of them. There is not one righteous Edomite in that verse, and no one can make the Bible say what it does not say. They are “The people against whom the Lord hath indignation for ever.” Indignation is anger aroused by something unjust, unworthy, and Esau is both. Forever means forever. If the Lord has indignation against them forever, the Christian who argues they can be saved has been drugged by his religion.

precepts.label: Job 9:24
precepts.why:
“The burden of the word of the Lord to Israel by Malachi.” “I loved Jacob, And I hated Esau, and laid his mountains and his heritage waste”. That is what Paul refers to in Romans 9 when he says, as it is written. Esau went through some things at different times: they became the cavemen, came out of the caves and started taking people's identity, the fugitives and vagabonds that they were. But his ultimate, permanent judgment was deferred for a set time. “Whereas Edom saith, We are impoverished, but we will return and build the desolate places”, and during the Renaissance they did. “They shall build, but I will throw down; and they shall call them, The border of wickedness, and, The people against whom the Lord hath indignation for ever.”

Job shows why he has the power for now: “The earth is given into the hand of the wicked: he covereth the faces of the judges thereof; if not, where, and who is he?” The border of wickedness is the mark; people will know. And the indignation for ever tells you judgment was reserved for him, but God needed to use him for a time for his plan.

If not, who is he? If it is not Esau, if it is not the United States of America, who is it? The prophets saw visions of rooms like this: the president seated up high with the vice president and the speaker beside him, and the United Nations the same on a bigger scale, all the nations with their hierarchies on one accord. That is why the scriptures say they were confederate.

It is like Cain: he was supposed to be judged, pleaded, and the Lord put a mark on him and deferred it. Revenge is a dish best served cold. How much better to let this man get so high in power and authority that he thinks he can stop God, and then take him down.

precepts.label: Luke 21:24
precepts.why:
Esau's judgment was deferred for a time, and Christ gave the time: “And they shall fall by the edge of the sword, and shall be led away captive into all nations: and Jerusalem shall be trodden down of the Gentiles, until the times of the Gentiles be fulfilled.”

There is a set time that has to be fulfilled for these heathen nations, starting with Esau at the top: the same spirit of Cain in rulership. But it is temporary.

Through the process of time, waiting generation after generation for his judgment, Esau has forgotten it, or at least his pomp and pride make him think he is untouchable. Obadiah says, “The pride of thine heart hath deceived thee”, “that saith in his heart, Who shall bring me down to the ground?” And who blames him? Look at what they just did to the air defenses Russia and China supplied. Trump now talks like that, of taking Venezuela and coming after Colombia and Mexico, and boasts that it was so fast and violent.

But it is prophesied who will bring him down. All those he dealt with will turn against him, and then Christ and his elect will have the glory and the honor to take him down. “evil shall hunt the violent man to overthrow him.” When the times of the Gentiles are fulfilled, his time is up.

precepts.label: Malachi 4:4-6
precepts.why:
“Behold, I will send my messenger, and he shall prepare the way before me”. You may think at first that is only John the Baptist. That is a good thought, but it is the John the Baptist work in the last days, and the end of Malachi shows it.

“Remember ye the law of Moses my servant, which I commanded unto him in Horeb for all Israel, with the statutes and judgments.” Then here it comes: “Behold, I will send you Elijah the prophet before the coming of the great and dreadful day of the Lord”. That is still the John the Baptist work, but in the last days it is Elijah, sent before that great and dreadful day.

What would he do? “And he shall turn the heart of the fathers to the children”. Why? Because we would forget who we are. We would lose our way. “And the heart of the children to their fathers”: he is going to show us our forefathers, Abraham, Isaac and Jacob, and turn us back to them, “lest I come and smite the earth with a curse.”

So the messenger of Malachi 3 is the messenger sent before the Lord comes to his temple in the last days, to bring a people who forgot themselves back to their fathers and their law before the day of his coming.

precepts.label: Zechariah 13:8-9
precepts.why:
“For he is like a refiner’s fire, and like fullers’ soap”. Christ is like a refiner's fire. Zechariah shows what that fire and that soap mean.

“And it shall come to pass, that in all the land, saith the Lord, two parts therein shall be cut off and die”. Two out of every three of our people shall be cut off and die. Why? Because we know damn good and well.

“But the third shall be left therein.” There is going to be a third: one third will be saved out of this land, America. “And I will bring the third part through the fire, and will refine them as silver is refined, and will try them as gold is tried”. That is the refiner sitting over the silver in Malachi 3, purging the sons of Levi “as gold and silver”.

“They shall call on my name, and I will hear them: I will say, It is my people: and they shall say, The Lord is my God.” That is the wilderness right there. That is how you know Malachi 3 is the last days: “who may abide the day of his coming? and who shall stand when he appeareth?” Only the third part that comes through the fire refined.

precepts.label: Malachi 1:11
precepts.why:
Malachi 3 ends with the refined people offering again: “Then shall the offering of Judah and Jerusalem be pleasant unto the Lord, as in the days of old, and as in former years.” What is the offering of Judah and Jerusalem? Malachi already said it in the first chapter.

“For from the rising of the sun even unto the going down of the same my name shall be great among the Gentiles; and in every place incense shall be offered unto my name, and a pure offering: for my name shall be great among the heathen, saith the Lord of hosts.”

Incense offered unto his name, and a pure offering. That is the offering in righteousness that the purified sons of Levi will offer after the Lord sits as a refiner and purifier of silver: a pure offering, with his name great from the rising of the sun to the going down of it.

precepts.label: Exodus 22:18
precepts.why:
“And I will come near to you to judgment; and I will be a swift witness against the sorcerers”. That is what we wanted to get to. The law already said what God thinks of sorcery: “Thou shalt not suffer a witch to live.”

Look at what our people are doing. Growing numbers of black women in Maryland and across the nation are leaving church worship for what they call ancient forms of spiritual contact. Some call it witchcraft, a term they accept and embrace, offering prayers to spirits and deities like Oshun. More than two hundred witches gathered at a convention in Baltimore. They grew up Christian, Baptist, Episcopal, a grandfather a preacher, a father a deacon, and now they call themselves witches. God said he is going to be a swift witness against the sorcerers.

A sister who used crystals testified that instead of healing you, it entices you and traps you into depending on it for every little thing; it is like a placebo effect. So brothers, be careful. Sisters come in with these crystals and say, oh no, it’s just spirituality. It is witchcraft. Don’t fall for it, or you are going to have demons all up in your house.

precepts.label: Deuteronomy 22:22
precepts.why:
“and against the adulterers”. What is adultery? When the brothers had the sit down, the Christian pastors could not explain adultery. The law explains it: “If a man be found lying with a woman married to an husband, then they shall both of them die, both the man that lay with the woman, and the woman: so shalt thou put away evil from Israel.”

A site advertises connecting with swingers of color, black swingers in the lifestyle. This is adultery.

And it happened among us. In San Antonio a sister bought another sister lingerie to spice up her marriage, and invited her and her husband over. They switched partners, and it went on for months without anyone knowing. It only came out when one wife decided she wanted the other husband. The husband left without a wife got mad, and then he revealed it, as if the Holy Spirit came on him. You didn’t reveal it because a spirit told you to; you revealed it because you were mad.

We had to put him out; everybody had to go. Now that brother is on YouTube and TikTok like an all knowing teacher, teaching everything we teach, but he is not going to reveal that he was that swinger brother. God said he will be a swift witness against the adulterers, and so shalt thou put away evil from Israel.

precepts.label: Leviticus 19:12
precepts.why:
“and against false swearers”. What is a false swearer? “And ye shall not swear by my name falsely, neither shalt thou profane the name of thy God: I am the Lord.”

That goes into perjury and false statements. To swear by his name falsely is to profane the name of our God.

So when God comes near to judgment, he will be a swift witness against the ones who lie under oath and make false statements, the same as against the sorcerers and the adulterers. He is the Lord; he signs the command with his own name, and he will not let his name be profaned.

precepts.label: Leviticus 19:13
precepts.why:
“and against those that oppress the hireling in his wages”. You might say to yourself, this does not apply to us; nobody among us oppresses the hireling in his wages. Oh, you would be shocked. It took place right here.

The brothers said, let’s all be truckers. Some got their own authority: I control all this, I’ll hire you, and you, and you. But I like these brothers better, so I’m giving you the good, high paying jobs, and the rest of you I’m not giving too much work.

“Thou shalt not defraud thy neighbour, neither rob him: the wages of him that is hired shall not abide with thee all night until the morning.”

Some brothers were being paid late, and were not getting paid the same amount. Everything was unjust. That is defrauding your neighbour and robbing him, and it is exactly what Malachi says God will be a swift witness against. Don’t get mad; get glad, and get it right.

precepts.label: Exodus 22:22-24
precepts.why:
“and against those that oppress the hireling in his wages, the widow, and the fatherless”. The law on the widow and the fatherless is heavy: “Ye shall not afflict any widow, or fatherless child. If thou afflict them in any wise, and they cry at all unto me, I will surely hear their cry”.

“And my wrath shall wax hot, and I will kill you with the sword; and your wives shall be widows, and your children fatherless.” Damn. Whoever afflicts the widow and the fatherless, God makes his own wife a widow and his own children fatherless.

Then Malachi finishes: “For I am the Lord, I change not; therefore ye sons of Jacob are not consumed.” The same God who wrote these laws has not changed, and he still judges the sorcerers, the adulterers, the false swearers and the oppressors. And because he changes not, the sons of Jacob are not consumed. That is why we are still in existence today, the twelve tribes.

precepts.label: John 6:15
precepts.why:
Matthew traces the line “after they were brought to Babylon”: Jechonias begat Salathiel, Salathiel begat Zorobabel, and on down to “Joseph the husband of Mary, of whom was born Jesus, who is called Christ.” That is the Branch, right through Zerubbabel.

In the sit down with Captain Matathias and Captain Galiah, the dude with that stupid hat said there was a curse on Jeconiah that nobody of his seed would sit as king, so the genealogy is ruled out. Think. After Jeconiah, was there a king in Israel sitting on the throne? No. When Babylon came in, that was it. Zedekiah came, and they got rid of him and killed him with his sons. There was no king during the time of Christ.

John shows it: “When Jesus therefore perceived that they would come and take him by force, to make him a king, he departed again into a mountain himself alone.” That is how much Israel loved him. They said, we want him to be our king. He said no.

Why? Because the prophets said there would be no more king until Christ returns. The sceptre was held for Shiloh, the Messiah, “and unto him shall the gathering of the people be.” Christ would not be made king by force before the time, so the line through Jeconiah and Zerubbabel is not ruled out; it runs straight to the one king still to sit on the throne.

precepts.label: Genesis 29:22-23
precepts.why:
Matthew says Mary was espoused to Joseph, and “before they came together, she was found with child of the Holy Ghost.” What does “came together” mean? Genesis 29 shows the custom. Jacob served seven years for Rachel, then said, “Give me my wife, for my days are fulfilled, that I may go in unto her.” “And Laban gathered together all the men of the place, and made a feast. And it came to pass in the evening, that he took Leah his daughter, and brought her to him; and he went in unto her.”

The feast is the coming together. Coming together was the customary wedding feast, the same custom seen with Tobit. So before Joseph and Mary came together in the wedding feast, they lay together. There was no fornication, because they were already espoused. Espousal is marriage: once the father made the promise, she could not go and marry another, and a man who lies with a betrothed woman commits adultery. That is why the angel called Mary Joseph's wife. She was his wife by espousal, not because he had lain with her; sex alone does not make a marriage.

Then “Joseph her husband, being a just man, and not willing to make her a publick example, was minded to put her away privily.” The commentators say that means he meant to divorce her secretly, because the child was not his. But if a just man's espoused wife were pregnant by another man, the law said she must die; a just man would not hide her. Put her away privily means hide her, the way “Elisabeth conceived, and hid herself five months.” A public example means being put to death in public. Had Mary gone back to her father's house showing, they would have said she played the harlot, just as they said of Tamar at three months.

So here is the question: why would a just man hide a pregnant woman he did not impregnate? And if she had committed adultery, why would a just man hide her sin? There is no way around that question. Minded means he was thinking about it: he was going to hide her so nothing would happen to her for what the two of them had done, because the child was his.

precepts.label: 2 Samuel 7:12
precepts.why:
The Lord promised David a king out of his own body: “And when thy days be fulfilled, and thou shalt sleep with thy fathers, I will set up thy seed after thee, which shall proceed out of thy bowels, and I will establish his kingdom.”

The seed that proceeds out of David's bowels is the promised king. So when the angel came to Joseph in the dream, he called him “Joseph, thou son of David”. The line is Joseph's, David's line.

The angel said, “fear not to take unto thee Mary thy wife: for that which is conceived in her is of the Holy Ghost.” That which is conceived in her is of the prophecy of 2 Samuel: the seed promised to David, coming out of his bowels.

That is why the Nativity begins with the bloodline. The child Mary conceived is the fulfilling of the promise made to David, that God would set up his seed after him and establish his kingdom.

precepts.label: Psalms 132:11
precepts.why:
The promise to David was sworn: “The Lord hath sworn in truth unto David; he will not turn from it; Of the fruit of thy body will I set upon thy throne.”

The Lord swore it in truth, and he will not turn from it. The king on David's throne would be the fruit of David's body. That is the same promise as 2 Samuel 7:12, the seed that shall proceed out of David's bowels.

So when the angel said to Joseph, “Joseph, thou son of David, fear not to take unto thee Mary thy wife: for that which is conceived in her is of the Holy Ghost”, that which is conceived in her is of the prophecy: the fruit of David's body that the Lord swore to set upon his throne. The line runs through Joseph, the son of David.

“And she shall bring forth a son, and thou shalt call his name JESUS: for he shall save his people from their sins.” The son is the fruit of David's body, sworn in truth, set on David's throne.

precepts.label: Acts 2:30
precepts.why:
Peter said of David: “Therefore being a prophet, and knowing that God had sworn with an oath to him, that of the fruit of his loins, according to the flesh, he would raise up Christ to sit on his throne”.

God swore to David that of the fruit of his loins he would raise up Christ, and notice the words: according to the flesh. Not according to the spirit. Christ sits on David's throne as the fruit of David's loins in the flesh.

That is why the angel spoke to “Joseph, thou son of David”, and why “that which is conceived in her is of the Holy Ghost” means it is of the prophecy: the promise sworn to David in 2 Samuel 7 and Psalm 132 that the king would come out of his bowels, the fruit of his body.

So the child of Matthew 1 is the Christ God swore to raise up of the fruit of David's loins, according to the flesh, to sit on his throne. The bloodline is the birthright.

precepts.label: Romans 1:3
precepts.why:
Paul says it plainly: “Concerning his Son Jesus Christ our Lord, which was made of the seed of David according to the flesh”. According to what? The flesh.

According to the flesh, he was made like you and I: made flesh and blood like unto his brethren, like his children. The same thing.

That is how Matthew 1 reads. Joseph was minded to put Mary away privily, “But while he thought on these things”, not did them but only thought about doing them, the angel appeared to him saying, “Joseph, thou son of David, fear not to take unto thee Mary thy wife: for that which is conceived in her is of the Holy Ghost.” That which is conceived in her is of the prophecy: the seed promised to David in 2 Samuel 7 and Psalm 132, of the fruit of his loins according to the flesh.

So Jesus Christ our Lord was made of the seed of David according to the flesh. He came into this world as a son of man, made flesh and blood like his brethren, and that is how he fulfils the promise to David.

The Exponential Maturation In The Days Of Decadence

precepts.label: Acts 1:6
precepts.why:
“Thy kingdom come.” Christ said to pray for the Lord's kingdom to come on earth. We are joint heirs with him, so what are we actually praying for? Our kingdom as well.

“When they therefore were come together, they asked of him, saying, Lord, wilt thou at this time restore again the kingdom to Israel?” The apostles, when they came together, asked Christ to restore the kingdom to Israel. So Christ's kingdom is Israel's kingdom as well. We are asking Christ to bring us the kingdom, because we are joint heirs with him.

We have always wanted to know when it is coming. Ezra asked it: “What shall be the parting asunder of the times? or when shall be the end of the first, and the beginning of it that followeth?” When shall be the end of the first world we are subjugated to, in bondage under, and the beginning of our kingdom, where the saints can rejoice in glory? The disciples asked it on the mount of Olives: “Tell us, when shall these things be? and what shall be the sign of thy coming, and of the end of the world?” Christ told them to learn the parable of the fig tree: when the branch is tender and puts forth leaves, you know summer is nigh. “So likewise ye, when ye shall see all these things, know that it is near, even at the doors.” When you see the decadence of this society, know that the tribulation and the destruction are near, even at the doors.

And God told Ezra what to watch: “For Esau is the end of the world, and Jacob is the beginning of it that followeth.” Jacob's hand held fast Esau's heel for a reason. When Esau goes down, we come up; when Esau is destroyed, we are in our kingdom. That's why the churches don't teach about Esau: the people at the top know, and they make sure it's hidden. So every time you pray thy kingdom come, you are praying for the destruction of the present kingdom. Christ's kingdom is not going to rule beside Babylon the Great; Christ isn't setting a throne beside the president.

precepts.label: Psalms 40:8
precepts.why:
“Thy will be done in earth.” The Lord's will will be done in earth, because this is the will that we want. David said it: “I delight to do thy will, O my God: yea, thy law is within my heart.” The laws of God are within our hearts, so we want what God wants. That's why he says be ye perfect, even as our Father is perfect. The objective is to become one with him: one with Christ, one with the Most High, one with the angels. That's the hierarchy the Most High is setting up. We are his heirs, his ambassadors on this earth, and that's why he gave us the name Israel. We are the prince of his power. That's us, not anybody else.

If the will of God is going to be done in this earth, and there is a will here already, then this will has got to be destroyed. Two kings cannot sit on the same throne. “The earth is given into the hand of the wicked: he covereth the faces of the judges thereof.” Notice: is given. Esau took the planet and ruled it in evil, yes, but God gave him the power to do so, for a time, and when that time is up it's over.

“What if God, willing to shew his wrath, and to make his power known, endured with much longsuffering the vessels of wrath fitted to destruction.” Esau struts with his chest out, bombing countries and stealing their resources, their minds, their women, and everybody wants to look like him. And the Most High says, I'm the one who put him up there, so that I can destroy him and everybody will know I'm the true power. The Lord endures with longsuffering because he will not break his word: he gave this man a time to rule, until the times of the nations be fulfilled. The whole nation of Edom is the vessels of wrath, a channel through which God shows how angry and how powerful he is, fitted to destruction, created for that purpose, just as he set up Pharaoh.

These are diabolical, demonic people; look at James Byrd dragged through the streets of Jasper, Texas. That's not teaching hatred; it's the facts. There's no such thing as a nice snake. Stick by these commandments. Come out from among them, be separate, gather yourselves together, organize and prepare for your kingdom while he brings this kingdom down. That is the maturing we have to do.

precepts.label: Zechariah 8:7
precepts.why:
A Christian pastor was played saying the other nations will come in the same gate Abraham comes through, because Abraham was not an Israelite. They try to get slicker and slicker. Abraham was not one of the 12, but he was the father of the 12. Christ said “many shall come from the east and west, and shall sit down with Abraham, and Isaac, and Jacob, in the kingdom of heaven.” So let's find out who's coming from the east and west.

“Thus saith the Lord of hosts; Behold, I will save my people from the east country, and from the west country; And I will bring them, and they shall dwell in the midst of Jerusalem: and they shall be my people.” My people. So that's only the Israelites.

The chapter opens with who it is for: “I was jealous for Zion with great jealousy.” Zion is not all nations on the planet. The ones coming from the east country and the west country to sit down with Abraham, Isaac and Jacob are Zion.

And the mere fact that he has to address it proves our teaching is in his school, his church. He is trying to do a cleanup; it is impacting the church.

precepts.label: Romans 9:7
precepts.why:
They always like to go to Abraham, like that is going to get the other nations in. The pastor said the nations come in through Abraham's gate because Abraham was not an Israelite and we have the faith of Abraham. Paul had to clean that up.

“Neither, because they are the seed of Abraham, are they all children: but, In Isaac shall thy seed be called.” Being of Abraham does not make you one of the children. The calling is on Isaac: Abraham, Isaac, Jacob, 12 tribes. That is why Christ said the many from the east and west “shall sit down with Abraham, and Isaac, and Jacob”, the fathers of one line.

That cuts his stuff about bringing up Abraham. You just close your Bible up and sit down.

thread.label: Matthew 11:12
thread.text: And from the days of John the Baptist until now the kingdom of heaven suffereth violence, and the violent take it by force.

classes.title: Zionism in the Face of Syria & Hezbollah
Nolan Wells: The Perpetual Hatred We Never Learned

precepts.label: 1 Chronicles 28:5
precepts.why:
How is the kingdom of heaven suffering violence? Is somebody jumping up in the sky punching God in the face? No. David answers it: “And of all my sons, (for the Lord hath given me many sons,) he hath chosen Solomon my son to sit upon the throne of the kingdom of the Lord over Israel.” Israel is called the kingdom of the Lord. The throne Solomon sat on was over a nation of people on the earth.

So when Christ says “from the days of John the Baptist until now the kingdom of heaven suffereth violence”, the kingdom of heaven is the nation of Israel. It is our people who suffered the violence.

“and the violent take it by force”. That is Rome. The violent man Christ speaks of is the same one just read in Psalms 140: “preserve me from the violent man; Which imagine mischiefs in their heart; continually are they gathered together for war.” They sharpen their tongues like a serpent, and “adders’ poison is under their lips”: their media, their philosophies, their religions, their politics. They have “purposed to overthrow my goings”, and the one whose goings they overthrow is the Israelites.

It is the same man being violent to us today. So what would Jesus say? He already spoke on it: Christ called Rome the violent man. They are the violent, and the kingdom they take by force is Israel.

classes.title: Raising Cain: The Son of Perdition, Merchants, and Captive Nations

precepts.label: Amos 9:9
precepts.why:
In the parable, “while men slept, his enemy came and sowed tares among the wheat”. A mixing happened: bad seed sown in among the good seed. “An enemy hath done this.” It was done on purpose. For the Northern Kingdom tribes in this hemisphere, that was the whitening the Spaniards practiced: marrying to lighter skin to better the race, with a whole caste system of names for every kind of mixing. They found the tribes, and since they could not kill us all outright, they tried to pollute the royal seed. But however watered down the daughter is, one man with the seed of an Israelite brings it back.

The servants asked, should we gather up the tares? “Nay; lest while ye gather up the tares, ye root up also the wheat with them. Let both grow together until the harvest”. It is not for us to determine, because of the way this went down; we do not know who is and who is not. At the harvest the angels will know who is Israel.

Amos proves it: “For, lo, I will command, and I will sift the house of Israel among all nations”. Why among all nations? Because through the whitening, the mixing and the captivities, God himself has to be the one to sift us. “Like as corn is sifted in a sieve, yet shall not the least grain fall upon the earth.” It will be determined who is who. Even Adam had to walk through a gate; you do not have twelve gates with twelve names and think somebody is going to sneak through. God said he will do it. My sheep hear my voice, and you know them by their works.

“All the sinners of my people shall die by the sword, which say, The evil shall not overtake nor prevent us.” He is going to kill a lot of them, before, during and even some after. So we narrow down where our people gather and go to the chief places of concourse, not to where the Edomites are, and give the word; and let God do the separating.

thread.label: Matthew 13:55-56
thread.text: Is not this the carpenter’s son? is not his mother called Mary? and his brethren, James, and Joses, and Simon, and Judas?

classes.title: The Nativity: the Bloodline, Birthright, & the Messiah

precepts.label: 1 Maccabees 2:2-5
precepts.why:
Matthew names Christ's family: “is not his mother called Mary? and his brethren, James, and Joses, and Simon, and Judas?” Mary his mother and Mary his aunt at the cross, a brother named Simon among Simons everywhere: Israel used the same names over and over, even inside one family. The Maccabees prove it.

“In those days arose Mattathias the son of John, the son of Simeon, a priest.” “And he had five sons, Joannan, called Caddis: Simon; called Thassi: Judas, who was called Maccabeus: Eleazar, called Avaran: and Jonathan, whose surname was Apphus.” Stop at Jonathan. Joannan and Jonathan are the same name: John and John, two sons of one father. Like George Foreman naming his sons George, George, George and George.

So it was a common thing for Israel to name sons the same name. You had Mary and Mary, John and John, John the Baptist too; they loved that name. You had Simon Iscariot, Simon the Canaanite, Simon Peter, and Christ's own brother Simon. That is why two Zerubbabels in the genealogies is no puzzle at all.

precepts.label: John 1:45
precepts.why:
In Matthew his own people asked, “Is not this the carpenter's son?” John shows his own disciples said the same thing: “Philip findeth Nathanael, and saith unto him, We have found him, of whom Moses in the law, and the prophets, did write, Jesus of Nazareth, the son of Joseph.”

The son of who? The son of Joseph. The one Moses and the prophets wrote about is called by his disciple the son of Joseph, the carpenter.

And Matthew says he had brethren, James, Joses, Simon and Judas, and sisters, more than one: a bunch of siblings. James wrote the book of James and Judas wrote Jude. So you Christians who say Mary was a virgin who never had sex read this all the time. Now some hear us teach it and act like they came up with it, saying the Roman Catholic doctrine is wrong, playing catchup. Christ had a father and a mother, brothers and sisters.

precepts.label: Mark 6:3
precepts.why:
Mark gives the same account as Matthew 13. On the sabbath Christ “began to teach in the synagogue: and many hearing him were astonished, saying, From whence hath this man these things?” Then: “Is not this the carpenter, the son of Mary, the brother of James, and Joses, and of Juda, and Simon? and are not his sisters here with us? And they were offended at him.”

They knew his family. They knew his background, his mother, his brothers by name, and his sisters. Who do he think he is? We grew up with this guy. He ain't nobody special. You're from the hood like us, from Nazareth; what you talking about, Savior? In his own home, where he was from, he got disrespected by his own neighbors and family members.

So the scripture itself shows Christ was born into a real family, the son of Mary with brothers and sisters, and that the people offended at him were the ones who knew exactly where he came from.
