precepts.label: Matthew 23:1-3
precepts.why:
Christ said, “Take heed and beware of the leaven of the Pharisees and of the Sadducees.” What was the leaven of the Pharisees and Sadducees? Matthew 23 shows the first part of it.

“The scribes and the Pharisees sit in Moses’ seat: All therefore whatsoever they bid you observe, that observe and do; but do not ye after their works: for they say, and do not.” They were hypocrites. What they said out of Moses' seat was the law, and that you do. But their works did not match their words.

“Do not ye after their works”, because their works were after someone else, and that is the rest of the leaven: who their works followed. The Passover reminds us that we were delivered because we were unleavened, righteous; so to be delivered again we have to move in the same spirit and purge the leaven out, not just check the box on the physical bread.

precepts.label: Mark 8:15
precepts.why:
Christ warned in Matthew 16 to beware of the leaven of the Pharisees, and in Matthew 23 he said to do what they bid from Moses' seat, but not after their works. Whose works were they following? Mark tells it: “And he charged them, saying, Take heed, beware of the leaven of the Pharisees, and of the leaven of Herod.”

The leaven of Herod. That lets you know whose manner they were following: they were following the white man, Esau. That is why he tells us to beware.

So their leaven was not just being hypocrites. They were following after the manner of the wicked. Leaven is an influence that spreads, and when the rulers of Israel took on Herod's leaven, it spread through them; they came to move in the same spirit as the wicked they served. That is the warning to us: do not take on the leaven of Herod, the spirit of Esau, while wearing the garments of Israel.

precepts.label: John 11:45-48
precepts.why:
John 11 shows the leaven of the Pharisees and of Herod at work. “Then many of the Jews which came to Mary, and had seen the things which Jesus did, believed on him.” They believed on Christ.

“But some of them went their ways to the Pharisees, and told them what things Jesus had done.” Wherever there is good, evil has to be there. You had the believers, and then you had coons set up there, running to tell.

“Then gathered the chief priests and the Pharisees a council, and said, What do we? for this man doeth many miracles. If we let him thus alone, all men will believe on him: and the Romans shall come and take away both our place and nation.” The Romans. That lets you know who their masters were and who they were following after. That is the leaven of Herod.

Leaven is an influence that spreads. That bitterness is on the inside, and it corrupts the spirit, the same bitterness that was in Cain toward Abel. The scribes and Pharisees were bitter toward Christ and wanted him dead to keep their place under Rome. If you are bitter toward your brother, you are in the same position as the scribes and Pharisees: the same spirit.

precepts.label: Proverbs 16:1
precepts.why:
Christ told the twelve, “Whatsoever ye shall bind on earth shall be bound in heaven”. Someone thinks it's just leadership saying it. No: “The preparations of the heart in man, and the answer of the tongue, is from the Lord.” The Lord had already ordained you to come up to that leadership table. Even your walking up to the council you want to go against was declared before time, as Isaiah 46:10 says, declaring the end from the beginning. God already agreed.

The preparing of your mind is from the Lord. You may say, I'm going to get up at 9:00 today and make it to the gym. The Lord says no, you are getting up at 10:00, and you'll get out the bed on the left-hand side and stub your damn toe. You set that timer to the T all week, you're a light sleeper, and that joker doesn't ring, because that was the Lord's doing. The Lord seals man's instruction in his sleep.

And the answer of the tongue, is that from the man or the woman? It is from the Lord. The Lord dictates even what you are going to respond back. The Lord may send a spirit down on you to go contrary to the doctrine, contrary to what leadership says in counsel to save your life, and you don't even catch that it is a spirit speaking through you. That is also a learning experience, for you to catch yourself.

But many cannot shake that legion. They ride that wave onto the bitterness boat and find themselves outside the congregation, making three- and four-part emotional videos and complaining on Clubhouse about how they were done unjustly. Then the Lord blinds your mind; you are reprobate, and only if the Lord chooses will he bring you back.

So your issue is not with leadership; you are bitter toward the Lord. Leadership has nothing to gain by telling you the word. All we gave you was the word of God, and we will be judged for it. Take it here and forbear, or go out there and get burnt. Our people hate their freedom; they are fearful of freedom, of responsibility, and of leadership.

thread.label: Matthew 24:3-6
thread.text: And as he sat upon the mount of Olives, the disciples came unto him privately, saying, Tell us, when shall these things be? and what shall be the sign of thy coming, and of the end of the world?

precepts.label: Isaiah 46:10
precepts.why:
“See that ye be not troubled: for all these things must come to pass”. Why must they come to pass? Because it was already ordained to happen this way. That is why this Bible is a great mystery given to the sons of the living God.

“Declaring the end from the beginning”. God declared the end from the creation of the earth. There was already a council with us and our heavenly Father, and all of us agreed to take our roles as the twelve tribes of the children of Israel. “And from ancient times”: there is no time with God; he is beyond time. God declared the end of this white man's captivity from the beginning. He declared our rulership from the beginning. He gave us the playbook before time was even created.

“The things that are not yet done”. We are walking and living through the timeline of prophecy. Things declared from ancient times are unfolding right before our eyes, and still many read it and do not believe it.

“Saying, My counsel shall stand”. God's counsel and his will shall be done. You cannot move it around, thwart it, or throw it off track. Whether you believe it or not, prophecy will be fulfilled; the word of the Lord will not go out void.

“And I will do all my pleasure”. This destruction was declared before time existed, and it is pleasure in the sight of the Lord. But many of our people do not see it as pleasure; they are fearful of the Lord's pleasure, fearful of freedom, while they love sin. Every war and rumour of war since 1917 has been a birthing pain. The ones who are troubled are the ones with secret sin on the back end. Now is not the time to play with your salvation.

thread.label: Matthew 24:7-10
thread.text: For nation shall rise against nation, and kingdom against kingdom: and there shall be famines, and pestilences, and earthquakes, in divers places.

classes.title: Eleutherophobia the Fear of Freedom

precepts.label: 2 Corinthians 6:7-10
precepts.why:
“And then shall many be offended, and shall betray one another”. Many in the body are here for the wrong reasons: opportunists out to make a quick buck, and some sent by the three-letter boys, the FBI and CIA, to spy out our liberties. But to the pure all things are pure. If you are among us to spy, all you are going to learn is to repent. You will not find us making maps or plotting to take over buildings. You will find no guns, no pimping, no drugs; only the word of God, our weapon of mass destruction. They want to know the secret sauce, and it is always God's commandments.

Paul lays it out: “By the word of truth, by the power of God”. That is how we roll: God's laws, statutes and commandments. “By the armour of righteousness on the right hand and on the left”: wherever we turn, that is our way.

“By honour and dishonour”: some honour the works, the platforms and the doors opening, and some see it as dishonour. “By evil report and good report”: evil report from some, but our intentions are pure. We are about family, raising our children and taking care of our wives. “As deceivers, and yet true”: those who hate God's commandments call us deceivers, but our word is true.

“As unknown, and yet well known”: they label us black Hebrew extremists as if they know nothing about us, but they know exactly that we are the sons of the living God. “As dying, and, behold, we live”: we are afflicted, and they think we have no life because we keep the Sabbath; but Christ is in us, and we keep more feast days than their wicked holidays and enjoy our families. “As chastened, and not killed; As sorrowful, yet alway rejoicing; as poor, yet making many rich”.

precepts.label: James 2:5
precepts.why:
Paul said we are “as poor, yet making many rich”. James shows why we are rich. They like to think this life we live is miserable. No: we are fulfilling God's prophecy.

“Hearken, my beloved brethren, Hath not God chosen the poor of this world”. How are we poor? Because they robbed us. We have been robbed of our nationality and robbed of our land. Israel is your land: black man, black woman, Latino man, Latino woman, Native American man, Native American woman. We did not know our nationality or our history. But that stops now; now we know.

“Rich in faith”. We are rich because Christ came for us; that is our faith. We keep the commandments and the faith of Jesus Christ, and we have the hope of deliverance coming our way: “heirs of the kingdom which he hath promised to them that love him”.

That is why we are not fearful of freedom. Every bomb dropped and every war fought is loosening the links of the shackles of our captivity. The Lord is the director of this thing, and those he chose out of poverty are the heirs of the kingdom.

precepts.label: Ruth 4:13
precepts.why:
Gabriel tells Mary, “thou shalt conceive in thy womb, and bring forth a son”. It is the same word used of her cousin: “And after those days his wife Elisabeth conceived”. What does it mean to conceive? To conceive you need seed; the man’s seed has to go in and fertilize the egg. Some might be confused, so Ruth shows how that happens.

“So Boaz took Ruth, and she was his wife: and when he went in unto her, the Lord gave her conception, and she bare a son.” When Boaz went in unto her, the Lord gave her conception. That is how it works: a husband goes in unto his wife, and the Lord gives the conception.

And when Luke 1:28 says the angel “came in unto her”, he came in and talked with her. He did not come in and have sex with her; he came in and talked to her, plain and simple. So when Luke 1:31 says Mary shall conceive, it is conception the way Ruth conceived, the Lord giving it when her husband came unto her. It could well have been the first time Joseph touched her that the Lord made her conceive.

precepts.label: Leviticus 12:2
precepts.why:
The law shows what conceiving is: “Speak unto the children of Israel, saying, If a woman have conceived seed, and born a man child: then she shall be unclean seven days”. She conceived what? Seed.

A woman conceives seed through intercourse. That is the same seed Onan spilled on the ground in Genesis 38, knowing the inheritance would not be his. It is the same exact thing.

So Luke 1:31, “thou shalt conceive in thy womb, and bring forth a son”, is a woman conceiving seed and bearing a man child. It is said to Mary in the same form of words as to Zacharias about Elisabeth: “thy wife Elisabeth shall bear thee a son, and thou shalt call his name John,” and “shalt call his name JESUS.” The same thing being done, the same thing being said.

precepts.label: Wisdom of Solomon 19:7-8
precepts.why:
Luke 1:35 says “the power of the Highest shall overshadow thee”. What does overshadow mean? Wisdom of Solomon shows it: “For the whole creature in his proper kind was fashioned again anew, serving the peculiar commandments that were given unto them, that thy children might be kept without hurt”. The whole creature is Israel, the whole nation that came out of Egypt, made new, serving the peculiar commandments.

“As namely, a cloud shadowing the camp; and where water stood before, dry land appeared; and out of the Red sea a way without impediment; and out of the violent stream a green field: Wherethrough all the people went that were defended with thy hand, seeing thy marvellous strange wonders.”

What did the cloud shadowing the camp do for us at the Red Sea? It led us. It guided us through the Red Sea, and the people went through “defended with thy hand.” That is what overshadow means: to lead, guide and defend.

So when the angel says the power of the Highest shall overshadow Mary, it is not the spirit coming into her and making her pregnant. It is the Lord guiding and defending her, leading her to where she had to go.

precepts.label: Baruch 5:7-9
precepts.why:
Baruch gives another one. Overshadow does not mean that it got her impregnated. It means to guide her to where she had to go. “For God hath appointed that every high hill, and banks of long continuance, should be cast down, and valleys filled up, to make even the ground, that Israel may go safely in the glory of God”.

“Moreover even the woods and every sweetsmelling tree shall overshadow Israel by the commandment of God. For God shall lead Israel with joy in the light of his glory”. The trees shall overshadow Israel, for God shall lead Israel. To overshadow is to lead, guide or defend.

So in Luke 1:35 the Lord would lead Mary to Joseph. When it says overshadow thee, it means he will guide and lead her, like he led Zacharias home to his wife to lay with her. That is what it is talking about, not him overshadowing her into pregnancy.

precepts.label: Proverbs 20:24
precepts.why:
This goes with overshadow: the Lord guided Mary, and she went and came together with her husband. “Man’s goings are of the Lord; how can a man then understand his own way?”

A man’s goings are of the Lord because the Lord guides us and overshadows us in everyday life. Sometimes you are walking in the street, something tells you to pick something up off the ground, and a car goes right by where you would have been. Why? The Lord was there guiding you.

“how can a man then understand his own way?” Remember, Mary did not understand. She said, “How shall this be, seeing I know not a man?” She was espoused to Joseph but had not yet come together with him. The Lord said, don’t worry, you are going to fulfil the scriptures; I am going to guide you. She could not understand her way, but the Most High had plans for her, and he guided her, the same way he guided every one of us here.

precepts.label: Mark 14:58
precepts.why:
Christ said, “Destroy this temple, and in three days I will raise it up”, and the Jews answered, “Forty and six years was this temple in building, and wilt thou rear it up in three days?” They thought he meant the building.

At his trial the false witnesses brought it back: “We heard him say, I will destroy this temple that is made with hands, and within three days I will build another made without hands.” They had overheard his teachings, and they lied on him. He never said he would destroy the temple made with hands.

Even their lie points to the truth: another temple “made without hands.” The temple Christ spoke of raising up in three days was not stone at all. It was his own body, and that is what the rest of the scriptures read here make plain.

precepts.label: Mark 15:29-30
precepts.why:
This is Christ on the cross. “And they that passed by railed on him, wagging their heads, and saying, Ah, thou that destroyest the temple, and buildest it in three days, Save thyself, and come down from the cross.”

They mocked him with the very words of John 2:19, still thinking he had boasted about the building in Jerusalem. But there he was, hanging on the cross: the temple he spoke of was being destroyed right in front of them, and they could not see it.

So we know Christ was talking about his body. “Destroy this temple, and in three days I will raise it up”: they destroyed his body on the cross, and in three days he raised it up again. What the passersby railed at as a failed boast was the prophecy being fulfilled before their eyes.

precepts.label: Matthew 27:63
precepts.why:
After the crucifixion the chief priests and Pharisees came to Pilate, “Saying, Sir, we remember that that deceiver said, while he was yet alive, After three days I will rise again.”

They called him a deceiver, but they remembered exactly what he said, and they understood it: after three days I will rise again. That was what he meant when he said in three days I will rebuild this temple.

They had heard him teach it. So when they put up false witnesses saying he would destroy the temple and build it back, they were lying on him, twisting his words about the building, while among themselves they knew he spoke of rising from the dead. The temple raised up in three days is his body raised the third day.

precepts.label: Matthew 16:21
precepts.why:
This is what he actually said: “From that time forth began Jesus to shew unto his disciples, how that he must go unto Jerusalem, and suffer many things of the elders and chief priests and scribes, and be killed, and be raised again the third day.” He was talking about raising up himself the third day. Christ's body was the temple.

And his temple today is us. Peter says, “Ye also, as lively stones, are built up a spiritual house, an holy priesthood, to offer up spiritual sacrifices, acceptable to God by Jesus Christ.” That's the real temple: wherever our people are gathered is a spiritual house. Lively means the laws percolate within us, with zeal, passion and fire, not a boring spirit. Paul says, “In whom all the building fitly framed together groweth unto an holy temple in the Lord”: stones have to come together, so play your position and don't try to change it through deceit. And “Know ye not that ye are the temple of God, and that the Spirit of God dwelleth in you?” “for the temple of God is holy, which temple ye are”.

How does that temple grow? “Wherefore laying aside all malice, and all guile, and hypocrisies, and envies, and all evil speakings, As newborn babes, desire the sincere milk of the word, that ye may grow thereby”. Everybody forgets verse one: you have to put away malice, deceit, jealousies and murmuring first. The sincere milk of the word is the law, and we have to drink it like a baby drinks milk, not once a month or once a week, but constantly. That is why we have to change the way we conduct ourselves and our communications: we are the temple.

precepts.label: Matthew 24:9
precepts.why:
The rulers “commanded them not to speak at all nor teach in the name of Jesus”, and again: “Did not we straitly command you that ye should not teach in this name?” We read that and say it could never happen in America. Don't fool yourself. It will happen here.

Christ warned it: “Then shall they deliver you up to be afflicted, and shall kill you: and ye shall be hated of all nations for my name’s sake.” Imagine they shut your bank account down. Now you can't pay your rent, your mortgage, your car note; you lose your car, your home, and maybe your wife: that's what you get for teaching that Bible, don't block Jesus. Everybody says, I'm strong, I can go through it. Wait till that day, with a newborn baby and you can't get infant formula. Some will say, I'm going back to being a Christian so I can get access to my money.

That hatred starts with the followers of Christ, but it applies to all twelve tribes of Israel. Look at the news: black and brown people killed, and they cry, what did we do to these white people? Why did they kill Sandra Bland? Why did they kill Tamir Rice? Christ said you would be hated of all nations. Christ is our king whether you accept it or not, and the white man looks at you and says, these are the people of Christ. You are the children of God, and they are the children of the devil. You might not like it, but it's true.

precepts.label: 2 Esdras 7:14
precepts.why:
Being hated of all nations is not only for those who teach the Bible; Ezra shows who it will affect. “For the entrances of the elder world were wide and sure, and brought immortal fruit.” The elder world was paradise in the time of Adam. “If then they that live labour not to enter these strait and vain things, they can never receive those that are laid up for them.”

You have to enter those hard things to enter paradise. The angel is telling Ezra that if we don't go through the hardships of Jacob's trouble, we can never get paradise. If you decide to kill yourself before it happens, you cannot get paradise. If you say, I'm going to join another religion to escape punishment from these other nations, you will never receive it.

Read on: “Nevertheless the righteous shall suffer strait things, and hope for wide”. The righteous shall suffer hard things, that is Jacob's trouble, and hope for paradise. “for they that have done wickedly have suffered the strait things, and yet shall not see the wide.” The wicked Israelites are going through Jacob's trouble too, but they are not going to see the kingdom.

So when Christ said you shall be hated of all nations, it covers all Israel. Whether you teach or not, the strait things are coming; the only question is whether you come out of them into what is laid up for you. That is why you cannot run from the persecution when they command us not to teach in his name.

precepts.label: Ecclesiastes 1:9
precepts.why:
“And at that time there was a great persecution against the church which was at Jerusalem; and they were all scattered abroad”. We saw persecution against our brothers in France; it hasn't gotten here yet, and they say America is the major hub. When it happens, can you stand the rain? That's why we say don't take the convocations lightly.

People read these things and say, oh, that's old time. But Solomon says: “The thing that hath been, it is that which shall be; and that which is done is that which shall be done: and there is no new thing under the sun.” That's you and me. We read Maccabees and Acts 8:1 and say that could never happen again? You're simple as hell. What happened in 1 Maccabees 1 and Daniel 3 is what Revelation 13 speaks of, no buying and selling, and it leads to death.

Paul said the same thing: “For whatsoever things were written aforetime were written for our learning, that we through patience and comfort of the scriptures might have hope.” Those old-time things were written for us to learn from, because they are going to happen again. We need patience and the comfort of the scriptures because we are going to go through what our ancestors went through: how did they deal with it, how did they survive?

Herod killed James and, because it pleased them, took Peter also. And Trump joked about bringing back public executions. The Christians don't understand what is about to come; in here we understand, because what has been is what shall be.

precepts.label: Psalms 91:1
precepts.why:
God exalted Christ “to be a Prince and a Saviour, for to give repentance to Israel, and forgiveness of sins.” Repentance is for Israel, the children of the captivity, of the slave trade, of the colonization of Africa, not the fake people in the land right now. The law was only given to us. Esau's only job is to whoop us into shape. We are in punishment right now; it is like we are in jail and they are the correction officers. We just have to do our time in peace and we are going to come out. But while we do our time, any time we move weirdly, they will break our back.

So when brothers say we should gather guns and go fight Esau: Negro, something is wrong with you. The Bible said the sword was his gift; the Lord gave him the sword. Read the name written on your gun: Smith & Wesson. We don't make guns; the AK-47 is the Russians, the Uzi is the Israelis. All they have to do is cut the water off in the hood. In Haiti a gang leader bought five of ten cases of bullets from a rich oligarch's man, and within the hour the police came, a three hour shootout used up all his bullets, and he had to call the same rich man for the rest. That is the setup: America will have a shootout with you, make you waste your bullets, and then you are dead. In 1985 they dropped a bomb on MOVE in Philly; at Waco, Esau came with tanks on white people, an offshoot of the Seventh-day Adventist Church, with kids inside. Stop playing.

Your only defense against this man is the Bible. “He that dwelleth in the secret place of the most High shall abide under the shadow of the Almighty.” This is the place. This is where you find your rest and your protection.

We have to learn to come back to the Lord and walk in righteousness, because that man does not know peace. All he knows is war, even though he loves saying the word peace. The protection of Israel is not in the sword but in dwelling with the Most High, the same God who exalted Christ to give Israel repentance and forgiveness.

precepts.label: Amos 5:26
precepts.why:
The Iranians burned large statues of a horned, bull-headed figure bearing the so-called Star of David, and they knew what they were doing: they were burning statues of Baal. That is not the Star of David. You cannot find it anywhere in the Bible; it is a sign in the occult.

Stephen said, “Yea, ye took up the tabernacle of Moloch, and the star of your god Remphan, figures which ye made to worship them: and I will carry you away beyond Babylon.” If you didn't know, Moloch is Baal: the same thing, both the devil. The star is the star of their god, the devil, Baal or Moloch.

Stephen was quoting Amos: “But ye have borne the tabernacle of your Moloch and Chiun your images, the star of your god, which ye made to yourselves.” Which ye made to yourselves: it is idolatry. God did not give us that star. When King Solomon was dabbling in witchcraft, that is how he got that star; God never gave it to us.

So the star so-called Israel and America carry is the star of Baal, and Baal worship shows up in plain sight: the bull's head statue at the 1933 Chicago World's Fair on Jewish Day, the giant mechanical bull at the 2022 Commonwealth Games, the bull on Wall Street. Even bullheaded, stupidly stubborn, comes from Baal worship, and stubbornness is as iniquity and idolatry. That idolatry is why Israel was carried away, and why we are in captivity today.

precepts.label: John 14:6
precepts.why:
“And the same time there arose no small stir about that way.” What way is this? Christ answers it: “I am the way, the truth, and the life: no man cometh unto the Father, but by me.” The way that Ephesus was stirred up about, the thing that caused a huge commotion in that city, was Christ himself.

They had a problem with Christ because a whole city was given to witchcraft. Ephesus owed its fame to the temple of Diana, and the “curious arts” practised there were the magical arts of the Ephesian conjurers. When Paul came preaching Christ, “many that believed came, and confessed, and shewed their deeds”, and those who used curious arts brought their books of witchcraft together and burned them before all men, fifty thousand pieces of silver worth. “So mightily grew the word of God and prevailed.”

That is what stirred the city. Demetrius the silversmith, “which made silver shrines for Diana”, called the craftsmen together and told them “by this craft we have our wealth”, and that Paul had “persuaded and turned away much people, saying that they be no gods, which are made with hands.” People were repenting and turning away from their witchcraft, and that put both the craftsmen’s living and the temple of “the great goddess Diana” in danger. Diana, with all the breasts on her, goes into fertility: satanic worship at the end of the day.

So the stir “about that way” was a city given over to idolatry and sorcery fighting against Christ, the only way to the Father. There is no salvation without him, and the same call goes out to our people now: repent from the idolatry, the fornication and the lasciviousness, and come to the way.

precepts.label: Isaiah 8:20
precepts.why:
“Know ye not, that to whom ye yield yourselves servants to obey, his servants ye are to whom ye obey; whether of sin unto death, or of obedience unto righteousness?” That is the million-dollar question: who do you give your service to? Money? The spirit of fornication? Alcoholism? The big-mouthed black woman that sleeps right next to you? Weakness as a man? Fear? Satan whispering that God can never use you because of your past? When you come into this truth and apply it, you are a new creature; old things are passed away.

“But God be thanked, that ye were the servants of sin, but ye have obeyed from the heart that form of doctrine which was delivered you.” What is that form of doctrine? “To the law and to the testimony: if they speak not according to this word, it is because there is no light in them.” The law and the testimony, the commandments and the testimony of Christ, is the doctrine delivered to us, and we obeyed it from the heart.

Thank God you understand your mission. You have your crown; it is already there, and it is for you to keep it on your head. You erase yourself out of the book of life; you are already ordained to get it. Will you hold on? “Here is the patience of the saints: here are they that keep the commandments of God, and the faith of Jesus.”

Your opponent is not the brothers that look like you. First it is the man in the mirror, and sin is the op. Use this Bible to shoot down all sin that opposes you, and put your energy there. Many cannot function without an oppressor, because with freedom comes change and responsibility. Choose this day who your Lord is: sin unto death, or obedience to the law and the testimony unto righteousness.

precepts.label: Ecclesiasticus 33:10-13
precepts.why:
“Hath not the potter power over the clay, of the same lump to make one vessel unto honour, and another unto dishonour?” Sirach shows the same potter at work: “And all men are from the ground, and Adam was created of earth: In much knowledge the Lord hath divided them, and made their ways diverse.”

“Some of them hath he blessed and exalted and some of them he sanctified, and set near himself”: that is Jacob, whom he loved. “but some of them hath he cursed and brought low, and turned out of their places”: that is Esau, whom he hated. The vessels of wrath “fitted to destruction”, fitted meaning created, are Esau.

“As the clay is in the potter’s hand, to fashion it at his pleasure: so man is in the hand of him that made him, to render to them as liketh him best.” Think of a movie: the writer has to have a good guy and a bad guy, and he hires you to be the bad guy. Why do I have to be the bad guy? Because I am paying you to be the bad guy. The pot cannot say to the one making it, why are you making me like this? It stays quiet, and the creator forms it and shapes it whichever way he will.

So it is “not of him that willeth, nor of him that runneth”. You cannot will yourself to be the people of God; you cannot positively think your way into changing the mind of God, and you cannot run throughout the earth building churches to make yourself the people of God. The potter divided the lump, and the mercy goes to Jacob.

precepts.label: Wisdom of Solomon 18:13
precepts.why:
“Even for this same purpose have I raised thee up, that I might shew my power in thee, and that my name might be declared throughout all the earth.” Paul is comparing Esau to Pharaoh. Pharaoh was the world's superpower. In the time of Paul and the apostles, Rome was the Pharaoh of the time; Paul says Esau because Rome read every letter at its checkpoints and nobody could speak ill against Rome. The Lord did not smite Rome; Rome just transformed. Now we are in America, the world superpower, with more bombs and greater technology than any nation, 850 bases covering the planet. Nobody can defeat them one on one; God has to take them down.

Wisdom shows how it ended in Egypt: “For whereas they would not believe any thing by reason of the enchantments; upon the destruction of the firstborn, they acknowledged this people to be the sons of God.” Bring it up to today: the enchantments today are called science, Esau's science, his technology. They will not believe anything because of it.

As it was then, it is going to be now. When death comes, great death, that is when they are going to acknowledge we are the sons of God. When this country is destroyed, the same thing that happened in the time of Moses will happen: everybody is going to say, we heard what your God did for you.

“and whom he will he hardeneth”. He hardened Pharaoh, and he is going to harden Esau. So do not believe the ones teaching that the white man will let millions of Israelites take his planes and boats to the wilderness; that is not in the Bible. The Israelites are as the sand of the sea, and no nation on this earth is going to let all of us come there.

precepts.label: Isaiah 14:1
precepts.why:

“So then it is not of him that willeth, nor of him that runneth, but of God that sheweth mercy.” You cannot will yourself to be the people of God, and you cannot run around setting up churches to be the people of God. It is of God that showeth mercy.

And Isaiah says who God will show that mercy to: “For the Lord will have mercy on Jacob, and will yet choose Israel, and set them in their own land”. That is what God said he is going to do. Not the League of Nations, not the UN, not America: God.

So the Zionists who set themselves up in the land by the nations have not been set there by God. Jacob, whom God loved, is the one he will have mercy on and choose again and set in their own land, and Esau, whom he hated, is raised up like Pharaoh only so that God can show his power in bringing him down.

thread.label: Romans 12:2
thread.text: And be not conformed to this world: but be ye transformed by the renewing of your mind, that ye may prove what is that good, and acceptable, and perfect, will of God.

classes.title: Bitterness: The Hidden Leaven From Cain To Esau

precepts.label: Psalms 119:9
precepts.why:
Paul says, “be not conformed to this world”, because of who rules over this world: the white man. Don't have the mind of the Edomite, the mind of Cain. Instead, “be ye transformed by the renewing of your mind”, after Christ. Just before, Ephesians told us, “Let all bitterness, and wrath, and anger, and clamour, and evil speaking, be put away from you, with all malice.” That is what we have to do. But how do we really go about doing it?

David asks the same question: “Wherewithal shall a young man cleanse his way?” How can we cleanse our ways? “by taking heed thereto according to thy word.”

The renewing of the mind comes by the word. We have to take heed according to the word, and that is how the bitter spirit, the leaven of Cain and Esau, is cleansed out, so that we may prove “what is that good, and acceptable, and perfect, will of God.”

precepts.label: 1 Peter 2:1-2
precepts.why:
Peter shows what the renewing of the mind looks like: “Wherefore laying aside all malice.” Lay aside all malice, family: all malice, all leaven. “and all guile”: that is the fake talk, because you are bitter. “and hypocrisies, and envies, and all evil speakings.” We have to lay these things aside.

“As newborn babes, desire the sincere milk of the word, that ye may grow thereby.” We have to be born again in Christ like newborn babes. The sincere milk of the word is the thing we have to desire, and it is what makes us grow.

This is Romans 12:2 at work. Being conformed to this world is carrying the mind of Cain and Esau: the malice, the guile, the envy and the evil speaking of the bitter spirit. Being transformed is laying all of that aside and feeding on the word until the mind is renewed after Christ.

precepts.label: James 1:21-24
precepts.why:
James tells us what to put off and what to take in: “Wherefore lay apart all filthiness and superfluity of naughtiness, and receive with meekness the engrafted word, which is able to save your souls.” The word received with meekness is what saves the soul.

“But be ye doers of the word, and not hearers only, deceiving your own selves.” We have to be doers of the word, family. We hear the class about putting away all bitterness, and then we don't do it.

“For if any be a hearer of the word, and not a doer, he is like unto a man beholding his natural face in a glass: For he beholdeth himself, and goeth his way, and straightway forgetteth what manner of man he was.” When you read the scriptures, you see yourself in them. But after you read them, you go your way and don't really address the matter.

We don't want to do that. We want to examine ourselves, look to the scriptures and say: Lord, thank you for revealing that evil in me and showing me I have a bitter spirit. I'm bitter toward my wife, I'm bitter toward the leadership, I'm bitter toward my brother. We have to confess that thing and pray to the Lord to remove that spirit from us. That is being transformed by the renewing of the mind, and not conformed to this world.

thread.label: Romans 12:3
thread.text: For I say, through the grace given unto me, to every man that is among you, not to think of himself more highly than he ought to think; but to think soberly, according as God hath dealt to every man the measure of faith.

classes.title: The Pride Of Thine Heart

precepts.label: Ecclesiastes 3:18-20
precepts.why:
Paul says “not to think of himself more highly than he ought to think; but to think soberly”. If God is revealing himself to you, and he doesn't deal with everybody, you had better have some humbleness, because that is the King of kings, the omnipotent Most High God.

Solomon shows why: “I said in mine heart concerning the estate of the sons of men, that God might manifest them, and that they might see that they themselves are beasts.” We are all beasts. Although we may be the sons and daughters of God, at the same time we are still beasts in his eyes.

“For that which befalleth the sons of men befalleth beasts; even one thing befalleth them: as the one dieth, so dieth the other”. The lion, the bug that has no value in the eyes of God and just serves the purpose it was created for: we die just like them. “yea, they have all one breath; so that a man hath no preeminence above a beast: for all is vanity.” This is Solomon, the wisest man ever to walk the earth besides Jesus the Christ, saying you have no preeminence above a beast.

So who are you to think you are better than that, to reject what God has written and do as thou wilt? Break it down to its lowest form, and we perish just like everything else. That is where humbleness comes in. We came here and we are going to leave here, so apply these excellent things to your life before you go back to your Maker.

precepts.label: Psalms 82:6-7
precepts.why:
“I have said, Ye are gods; and all of you are children of the most High.” That's why we say it: the Israelites are gods upon this earth, children of the Most High.

But read on: “But ye shall die like men, and fall like one of the princes.” We die just like men, just like the beasts of Ecclesiastes 3. In the grand scheme of things, we have no more power over death than the animals do. Are we higher up on the ladder of God's creation? Sure we are. But we perish just like everything else he has created.

That is exactly why a man must not think of himself more highly than he ought to think. Being called gods and children of the Most High is no ground for pride, because the same ones called gods fall like the princes. Think soberly: the one who knows he will die like men humbles himself before the God who made him.

precepts.label: Psalms 90:10
precepts.why:
“The days of our years are threescore years and ten”: seventy years is what we have. “and if by reason of strength they be fourscore years”: if God is merciful, we might get eighty years out of this body. You know the Bible is a true book: you get to hitting around forty and you say, damn, David was right.

That's why Captain Gideon did the class about working out, not drinking sodas and calcifying the bones, eating once a day and taking good care of yourself, so God can be merciful: he did real good with that temple I gave him; let me give him eighty years.

“yet is their strength labour and sorrow; for it is soon cut off, and we fly away.” We fly away means the spirit goes back to its Creator. That is the one day a man is going to fly: when he gets up out of this body.

And even eighty years is nothing to God. Peter says one day with the Lord is as a thousand years; by that measure a whole human lifetime is less than two hours in God's eyes, and it could be even less. Your life is but a vapor. So how do you look down on others and think so highly of yourself? Think soberly, and humble yourself.

precepts.label: Sirach 14:17-19
precepts.why:
“All flesh waxeth old as a garment: for the covenant from the beginning is, Thou shalt die the death.” That is what we just read in David: seventy, maybe eighty years. That is the covenant God pronounced from the beginning: thou shalt die the death.

“As of the green leaves on a thick tree, some fall, and some grow; so is the generation of flesh and blood, one cometh to an end, and another is born.” That is why we have kids. You watch them grow up, and you say, man, I'm getting old. You know the covenant God pronounced upon all flesh, and you are about to cross it too.

“Every work rotteth and consumeth away, and the worker thereof shall go withal.” That is the covenant: thou shalt die the death, thus saith the Lord. Everything a man builds goes with him. So there is no room to think of yourself more highly than you ought; think soberly, knowing the covenant is coming for you like every other leaf on the tree.

precepts.label: Romans 6:23
precepts.why:
Why do we die? We try to break it down so the new people coming into the faith can put the puzzle together: “For the wages of sin is death”. That is why the covenant, thou shalt die the death, passed upon all of us. When Adam listened to his wife Eve and consented to the idolatry she brought to him, sin came into the world, and when sin came, death came with it.

“but the gift of God is eternal life through Jesus Christ our Lord.” That is what we get in the repentance. But we still have to go through the covenant of all flesh. You can't receive the gift of eternal life while you are still in the flesh; flesh and blood cannot enter into the kingdom of heaven. We have to pass through that covenant.

And one thing we had better make sure we don't have on us when we leave this body is pride. That will keep us out of it for sure. That is why Paul says not to think of yourself more highly than you ought: the one who dies like the beasts receives the gift only through Christ, and only if he goes to his grave humble.

precepts.label: 1 Peter 2:21
precepts.why:
“Purge out therefore the old leaven, that ye may be a new lump, as ye are unleavened. For even Christ our passover is sacrificed for us”. What is the example that Christ left? Peter: “For even hereunto were ye called: because Christ also suffered for us, leaving us an example, that ye should follow his steps”.

Christ suffered for us: that goes back to him being our Passover, sacrificed for us. And he left an example, so as believers in Christ we must follow his steps. Christ came to bring peace. Bitterness does not do that.

So we apply the scriptures. Purge out the old sin, the old man, that we may be a new lump, a new creature in Christ, following in the steps of Christ. “Therefore let us keep the feast, not with old leaven, neither with the leaven of malice and wickedness”. That malice is the bitterness: a dumb thought jumps in, the seed gets planted, it gets nourished, and next thing you know you have malice, hatred toward your brother, and wickedness, because it leads to sin.

“but with the unleavened bread of sincerity and truth”. Meaning: I have the bitter spirit, so I have to go to my brother and talk to him in sincerity and truth. Brothers sweep under the floor mats and dump out the toaster at Passover, and there is not a grain of yeast in the house, while they carry an evil eye toward a brother or bitterness toward a wife. We are the temple of God; the leaven has to come out of the spirit.

And do not tuck it away for later, like the brother who puts the bread in the storage closet during the feast and brings it back when the season is over. Following Christ's steps means letting the bitterness go entirely.

precepts.label: Proverbs 22:24-25
precepts.why:
“evil communications corrupt good manners.” Bitterness spreads like leaven through words: the yeast makes things rise, and that is what bitterness does. The root of bitterness corrupts your spirit and messes with your attitude, and that angry influence spreads to others through words and through attitude.

So Proverbs warns: “Make no friendship with an angry man; and with a furious man thou shalt not go”. You see that brother is bitter; he is like that dangerous overgrown brush. There could be a viper in there, anything on the other side of that bush. Move.

“Lest thou learn his ways, and get a snare to thy soul.” Now that bitter brother has put the bitter spirit on you. You got bit, like Bird Box, and now you are looking dumb. That is the snare right there.

That is why the scripture says be not deceived. Keeping company with the bitter brother is how the leaven gets into you. His evil communications will corrupt your good manners, and his offenses will reach others, starting with the first offense, the one in your own house.

thread.label: 2 Corinthians 2:8-11
thread.text: Wherefore I beseech you that ye would confirm your love toward him.

classes.title: The Pride Of Thine Heart

precepts.label: Psalms 18:20-23
precepts.why:
Paul forgives “Lest Satan should get an advantage of us: for we are not ignorant of his devices.” So examine yourself: has Satan been using some form of pride to hold you back and keep you down? It may be subtle: not asking for help, thinking too highly of yourself, I'm good, I'm fine. Satan has many devices and can transform himself into an angel of light. Captain Matthew put it plainly: fat brothers are too prideful, and that is why they won't change their eating habits.

David shows the other way. “The Lord rewarded me according to my righteousness; according to the cleanness of my hands hath he recompensed me. For I have kept the ways of the Lord, and have not wickedly departed from my God. For all his judgments were before me, and I did not put away his statutes from me.” We all know David committed adultery and put out a hit on a brother. So what does it mean that he did not put away his statutes?

When Nathan the prophet brought it to him, he said, that's me. God was going to take away the child; he fasted and prayed, and when it happened he washed his face, ate bread and said it was the Lord's judgment. He was not prideful. He did not say, I'm the king, I can have as many women as I want, God chose me. He acknowledged his sin, humbled himself and did not put the judgments away.

“I was also upright before him, and I kept myself from mine iniquity.” He went on forward and walked in the ways of the Lord, to the point where God said David is a man after my own heart, because he humbled himself when his sins were brought to him. That is how you keep Satan from getting an advantage of you.

precepts.label: Proverbs 29:23
precepts.why:
Look what pride does: “A man’s pride shall bring him low: but honour shall uphold the humble in spirit.” Pride is one of Satan's devices, and it does not have to be loud and in your face. It can be subtle. Sometimes it shuts you down, I can do this on my own, I don't need anybody, and it always points the finger at somebody else and never at yourself. Pride destroyed us in the kingdom, and it can keep destroying us right now.

Pride destroyed every kingdom on the earth. The king of Assyria sent his messenger with big words against Hezekiah and the Lord, and the angel of the Lord smote a hundred fourscore and five thousand in one night; then his own sons killed Sennacherib with the sword while he worshipped his god. Nebuchadnezzar said, is not this great Babylon, built by the might of my power, and while the word was in his mouth the kingdom departed from him, and he ate grass as oxen until he knew that the Most High ruleth in the kingdom of men. Antiochus spoke proudly and was smitten with a remedyless pain of the bowels. Herod took the glory of a god and was eaten of worms.

No kingdom is exempt, not Assyria, Babylon, Greece, Rome or America. And none is more prideful than Edom, the white man, of whom it is written, the pride of thine heart hath deceived thee.

But honour upholds the humble in spirit. Nebuchadnezzar humbled himself and came back saying there is no God like the God of Daniel. David humbled himself and God called him a man after his own heart. The only way our kingdom will last forever is to walk in wisdom and humility towards God; outside of that, pride brings us low like every nation before us.

“Wherefore come out from among them, and be ye separate”. How do you come out? Stop doing the things they are doing; stop following their ways. As Proverbs says, “Envy thou not the oppressor, and choose none of his ways.” None.

If the Bible says choose none of his ways, who is the his? Esau. Who created Christianity? Esau. So you have to let Christianity go. No Jehovah's Witness, none.

Let go of his ways and start choosing to keep God's ways. “and touch not the unclean thing”: your Christmas, let it go; Thanksgiving, let it go; your Christianity, let it go; your masonry, your sororities and fraternities, let them go. Come out.

When you cleanse yourself of all the uncleanness this world has to offer, then the Lord will receive you and be a Father to you, and you shall be his sons and daughters. Those are not our words; they were written long before any of us were born. The churches were given to us by our enemy, and our enemy will never teach us anything right.

thread.label: 2 Corinthians 7:10
thread.text: For godly sorrow worketh repentance to salvation not to be repented of: but the sorrow of the world worketh death.

classes.title: Bitterness: The Hidden Leaven From Cain To Esau

precepts.label: Proverbs 1:28-31
precepts.why:
Paul says “the sorrow of the world worketh death.” Here is what that worldly sorrow looks like: “Then shall they call upon me, but I will not answer; they shall seek me early, but they shall not find me”. When the Lord increases the affliction, after you have been wicked the whole time, now you are calling on the Lord: it's getting real down here, the persecution is on, I ain't got no food. You call, and the line says the number you have dialed is no longer available to you, dummy. You'll seek him early, like getting on a pre-call, and you still won't find him. You won't have any connection to the Lord on that day.

Why? “For that they hated knowledge, and did not choose the fear of the Lord”. They had the carnal mind, the mind of Cain and Esau, and cast the word behind their back like their father did. “They would none of my counsel: they despised all my reproof.” They literally threw the word behind their back, and a lot of our brothers and sisters do that. We all have to examine ourselves.

“Therefore shall they eat of the fruit of their own way, and be filled with their own devices.” If you are out there sowing sin, that is what you are going to reap.

That is Esau's sorrow. He sold his birthright, then realized, damn, I want that blessing back, and cried bitterly over what he himself threw away. So we have to be sincere when we come to the Lord and have the real godly sorrow that works repentance to salvation, to our inheritance, not to be repented of. We can't be out here faking the funk.

precepts.label: Proverbs 14:10
precepts.why:
“Examine yourselves”: not your neighbor, yourself. And you can do it, because “The heart knoweth his own bitterness”. Your mind knows its own bitterness. Brother, sister, you can't play confused when somebody asks, man, where is that bitterness coming from?

“and a stranger doth not intermeddle with his joy.” So you can't say, oh Bishop, tell me what's going on with me. You know exactly what is going on in your mind. Nobody else can get in and decipher exactly what it is. We can say, brother, you're off, you ain't moving right, there is sin in there; we may not know it specifically, but you know the specifics of what you are dealing with.

This is a heavy topic. A lot of brothers and sisters are bitter. It came up in our congregation with a brother dealing with his wife, and then we came down here and saw the same thing, and it destroyed a household. If that spirit is left unchecked it can destroy the congregation. That is why each of us has to prove our own self: the heart already knows where the bitterness is.

precepts.label: Psalms 139:23-24
precepts.why:
To examine ourselves we ask the Lord to do it with us: “Search me, O God, and know my heart: try me, and know my thoughts: And see if there be any wicked way in me”. We ask the Lord to reveal the iniquity in us and not leave us blind to our own folly.

How is he going to do that? When you say, Lord, search me, that means you have to search the scriptures. The Lord ain't going to come down and say, open that door right there, let me see what's behind it. No, brother. You have to search the scriptures.

Then, in order to get over the root of bitterness, we have to confess it: damn, I had the devil on me. We look to the scriptures and say, Lord, thank you for revealing that evil in me and showing me I have a bitter spirit, bitter toward my wife, toward the leadership, toward my brother, and we pray to the Lord to remove that spirit from us. That is how we prove our own selves, whether we be in the faith.

precepts.label: Isaiah 29:13
precepts.why:
Paul marvels that they were “so soon removed from him that called you into the grace of Christ unto another gospel”. In Paul's day the Pharisees were deceiving the people to go back to animal sacrifice and give their fealty, their loyalty, to Rome. It is “not another”, because they were using the same scriptures, but “there be some that trouble you, and would pervert the gospel of Christ”: the scribes, Sadducees, Pharisees and Rome. What is Christianity today? A perversion of the truth of Christ: a white Jesus loved by Negroes and Latinos worshipping their oppressor. You are mad at white folks when they shoot you, then you go to church on Sunday and pray to white folks, and at Christmas and Easter you worship a white man again. It makes no sense.

Isaiah saw it: “Wherefore the Lord said, Forasmuch as this people draw near me with their mouth, and with their lips do honour me”. Praise God, praise Jesus, I love the Lord, yes I does. “but have removed their heart far from me”: you won't do a damn thing, not one law, not one commandment.

“and their fear toward me is taught by the precept of men”. The white man taught us the Bible. The white man said you don't have to worship God on the Sabbath day, you can do it on Sunday; in fact God is a white man, and anything the white man says is absolute, and Negroes and Latinos bow to that.

So the Lord says “I will proceed to do a marvellous work among this people, even a marvellous work and a wonder: for the wisdom of their wise men shall perish, and the understanding of their prudent men shall be hid.” How? God is raising up the prophets. Christianity will not perish on its own; it perishes through you brothers out there teaching on the streets, doing the videos and the classes seven days a week. The white man they call the wise and prudent man will realize he does not know what he thinks he knows, because the Holy Spirit is in the Israelites, and it is through our teaching that our people are repenting.

precepts.label: Psalms 148:14
precepts.why:
Paul writes “to the saints which are at Ephesus.” People say those are white people, or that the saints are anybody. No, those are not white people. Let the scripture say who the saints are, and be patient to comfort the new people watching, who have never heard this truth, with the scriptures, so that they too may have hope.

“He also exalteth the horn of his people, the praise of all his saints.” The horn of his people is Jesus the Christ. And the saints are named: “even of the children of Israel, a people near unto him.”

So the saints are indeed the children of Israel: the so-called blacks, Latinos and Native Americans who are under the curses found in Deuteronomy 28:15-68. When Paul greets the saints at Ephesus with “Grace be to you, and peace, from God our Father”, he is addressing the Israelites that were in Ephesus, scattered in Asia. That is who the book was sent to in the seven churches, and that is who the blessings in the verses that follow belong to.

precepts.label: Romans 9:3-4
precepts.why:
Ephesians says God has “predestinated us unto the adoption of children by Jesus Christ.” People say all nations can be adopted. No. Paul clears it up in Romans 9, line upon line, here a little and there a little. This is how you get the understanding, and so-called Catholics, Puerto Rican Catholics and Christians who don't know how to read the Bible that way need to hear it.

“For I could wish that myself were accursed from Christ for my brethren, my kinsmen according to the flesh.” My brethren, my relatives; my kinsmen, my family, blood relation. According to what flesh? Israelite flesh: black flesh, Latinos, Native Americans. We are family. We are the nation of Israel.

“Who are Israelites; to whom pertaineth the adoption.” So Paul was talking to the twelve tribes of Israel that were scattered in Asia, and that is who the adoption is for. The adoption is not for everyone; it is for the Israelites.

Don't let the wicked of our people deceive you, and don't go back and get rocked to sleep. Keep these precepts so that you remember them: write them down and study them.

precepts.label: 1 Corinthians 10:13
precepts.why:
“There hath no temptation taken you but such as is common to man.” Bitterness is a very common thing that many of us battle with. We are never alone in it: if leadership sees a spirit in one congregation, they have to understand that the same spirit is elsewhere. That is the “one body, and one Spirit” of Ephesians 4:4. The classes are not rehearsed, yet the same talking points come out in different places, because the Lord puts the spirit on the leadership to address the prevalent issue of the time, and in the midst of Passover He revealed bitterness throughout the congregations.

“But God is faithful, who will not suffer you to be tempted above that ye are able; but will with the temptation also make a way to escape, that ye may be able to bear it.” Even while being tried and tempted, the Lord in His faithfulness makes a way out.

What is the way to escape? Put a class on. Call a brother. Speak to your brother, to get that spirit off of you. A lot of times the devil jumps on us and we start battling in our own mind, and we create a whole other reality that does not even exist in real life. You talk to the brother and you say, damn, all that mess I was thinking and rehearsing is not even the case.

That matters, because bitterness is the hidden leaven that must be purged. If it is not purged, it grows into a root that defiles the soul. Many brothers who left the body and came out with crazy videos started with a root of bitterness.

thread.text: And grieve not the holy Spirit of God, whereby ye are sealed unto the day of redemption.

precepts.label: Colossians 3:12-13
precepts.why:
Ephesians 4 says what to put away: “Let all bitterness, and wrath, and anger, and clamour, and evil speaking, be put away from you, with all malice.” Bitterness comes first, and the rest come along with it: wrath, anger, clamour, and evil speaking, talking foolish and reckless about the brother, the sister, your wife. That thing has to be put away with extreme hatred. Instead: “be ye kind one to another, tenderhearted, forgiving one another, even as God for Christ’s sake hath forgiven you.” You want to seek pardon from the Lord, but you have hatred toward your brother?

Colossians says what to put on in its place: “Put on therefore, as the elect of God, holy and beloved, bowels of mercies, kindness, humbleness of mind, meekness, longsuffering; Forbearing one another, and forgiving one another, if any man have a quarrel against any: even as Christ forgave you, so also do ye.” That is how we have to move. The elect of God forbear and forgive one another.

Offenses are going to come in the congregation: a brother says something, a sister says something, and somebody gets offended. We all have to have mercy on one another, because we are all sick. This is a hospital. If a brother coughs on you, you forgive the brother, because everybody in here is sick.

This is how the bitter leaven gets purged. It came up in one congregation where a brother was bitter with his wife and it destroyed a household, and the same spirit showed up elsewhere. Left unchecked, it can destroy a congregation, so we put off the bitterness and put on mercy and forgiveness, as Christ forgave us.

thread.text: Be ye therefore followers of God, as dear children;

precepts.label: Ephesians 4:17-20
precepts.why:
“Be ye therefore followers of God, as dear children; And walk in love”. “But fornication, and all uncleanness, or covetousness, let it not be once named among you, as becometh saints”. Why did Paul write to the Ephesians that way? Because that is what they used to be caught up in. Ephesus was a tough pagan environment. The worship of Diana, Artemis, involved all manner of lewd behaviour: they filled the great theatre, they had orgies, they got drunk, witchcraft, idolatry. Diana is the queen of heaven, the same as Ashtaroth, and the same as the Yoruba goddess, and our people were caught up in it in ancient times and today.

Chapter 4 shows it: “This I say therefore, and testify in the Lord, that ye henceforth walk not as other Gentiles walk, in the vanity of their mind, Having the understanding darkened, being alienated from the life of God through the ignorance that is in them, because of the blindness of their heart”.

“Who being past feeling have given themselves over unto lasciviousness, to work all uncleanness with greediness. But ye have not so learned Christ”. Paul wrote in that form because he knew the lifestyle they came from, living as the Gentiles.

They were once “Gentiles in the flesh” and “aliens from the commonwealth of Israel”, but now made nigh by the blood of Christ, “fellowcitizens with the saints, and of the household of God”: the northern kingdom, the so-called Argentinians, Colombians, Brazilians, Venezuelans, Puerto Ricans and Mexicans, the Israelites according to the Bible. So our people need to wake up and repent from the idolatry, the fornication and the lasciviousness, and flee from idolatry, or receive the same judgment coming on America.

precepts.label: Genesis 49:10
precepts.why:
Paul beseeches the brethren “by the coming of our Lord Jesus Christ, and by our gathering together unto him.” That “him” is Christ, and Genesis 49:10 shows why: “unto him shall the gathering of the people be.” He is the only one who can gather all twelve tribes together. When people on earth say they are the ones Christ is using to gather the twelve tribes, don't listen to that.

Jacob's blessing lays it out. “The sceptre shall not depart from Judah”: the sceptre is the kingship. “nor a lawgiver from between his feet”: between the feet means the loins, the seed. The lawgiver comes out of Judah's loins, which shows there is no immaculate conception. “until Shiloh come”: until Christ comes.

That is why Paul tells them “be not soon shaken in mind, or be troubled.” In his time many were running around saying the resurrection had come and gone already. Paul reminds them not to let anyone deceive them; Christ had not returned, and the gathering belongs to him alone, when he comes.

precepts.label: Luke 21:24
precepts.why:
Paul says “that day shall not come, except there come a falling away first, and that man of sin be revealed, the son of perdition.” The falling away is not people leaving Christianity to join Islam, the way Christians read it. The falling away means the twelve tribes of Israel have to fall and go into captivity, and Luke 21:24 shows it.

“And they shall fall by the edge of the sword”: the Israelites. “and shall be led away captive into all nations”: slavery. “and Jerusalem shall be trodden down of the Gentiles”: Jerusalem taken over by other nations, in particular the Edomite nations, “until the times of the Gentiles be fulfilled”, until that time of rulership is over.

So two things have to happen before Christ returns: all twelve tribes must go into captivity, which is where we are now, and the man of sin must be revealed, the son of perdition. Perdition means eternal damnation, spiritual ruin and hell; it comes from the Latin perdere, to destroy or to lose. It is the fate of the wicked, the absolute loss of one's soul, the final loss of salvation and unending punishment.

They rise “to seduce, if it were possible, even the elect.” That lets us know there will be a seducing spirit in the last days to get us back into Christianity, back into colonialism, back into that damnable slave religion called Christianity. The seducing spirit that Mark, Matthew and Paul to Timothy all address is in these days.

Revelation names the three unclean spirits like frogs: out of the mouth of the dragon, politics; out of the mouth of the beast, the United States and its financial system; “and out of the mouth of the false prophet”, religion, which is Christianity. “For they are the spirits of devils, working miracles”, gathering the kings of the earth to the battle of that great day. So do not tell us the Bible is not true. If you want to play games and go back into Christianity, go; there are no bars on the door.

precepts.why:
Paul says in a great house there are vessels “of gold and of silver” and also “of wood and of earth”, and “If a man therefore purge himself from these, he shall be a vessel unto honour.” The next chapter names who those vessels of dishonour are: “This know also, that in the last days perilous times shall come. For men shall be lovers of their own selves, covetous, boasters, proud, blasphemers, disobedient to parents, unthankful, unholy, Without natural affection, trucebreakers, false accusers, incontinent, fierce, despisers of those that are good, Traitors, heady, highminded, lovers of pleasures more than lovers of God.”

“Having a form of godliness, but denying the power thereof.” Why does it say a form of godliness? That is the fringes everybody wears and the border of blue, walking around with your Bible, saying Most High, in Christ, blessed heartily. But you are not keeping the laws in your heart. You are really not keeping the commandments.

The great house is the nation of Israel, the real nation of Israel. There are brothers and sisters of gold and silver, applying what we read in 1 Peter 2:1-2. And there are brothers and sisters with fringes and a border of blue who are no damn good. They have not changed their lives; they are the same as they were two, three years ago. Not the new people who just came in, but people who have been with us for years and are still grimy: still that secret adulterer, that liar, complainer, murmurer. You are that wood and that earth. In every IUIC school there are men and women of honour and of dishonour, and the captains must be able to identify which is which. If you can’t do that, there is a problem.

“from such turn away.” That is what he said in the chapter before: purge yourself from these. Purge means cut them off, cut them loose. When you purge a plant you are pruning it, taking away the bad elements. Likewise with us: the bad elements among us, you have to cut off. You know which brothers always get you in trouble. Rolling with grimy brothers, you can almost get arrested many a time; cut them off, say I’m not rolling with y’all no more, and hang out with leadership. That is how you become a vessel “sanctified, and meet for the master’s use, and prepared unto every good work.”

precepts.label: Hebrews 7:14
precepts.why:
“Forasmuch then as the children are partakers of flesh and blood, he also himself likewise took part of the same.” The children are the disciples, us, and Christ took part of the same flesh and blood. “For verily he took not on him the nature of angels; but he took on him the seed of Abraham”, which is flesh and blood. “Wherefore in all things it behoved him to be made like unto his brethren.” In all things, not some things. How is a man made like his brethren in all things? By having a father and a mother.

Then Hebrews 7: “For it is evident that our Lord sprang out of Juda; of which tribe Moses spake nothing concerning priesthood.” He sprang out of Judah based on his father. The tribe comes from the father, as every Israelite’s does.

The fathers show the same. God told David, “I will set up thy seed after thee, which shall proceed out of thy bowels.” David knew “that of the fruit of his loins, according to the flesh, he would raise up Christ to sit on his throne.” And Paul says Christ “was made of the seed of David according to the flesh.” According to the flesh: made flesh and blood like his brethren.

That is why Matthew says “When as his mother Mary was espoused to Joseph, before they came together, she was found with child of the Holy Ghost.” Coming together was the customary wedding feast, as when Laban “made a feast” and Jacob went in unto his wife. Joseph and Mary were already espoused, and betrothal is marriage, so there was no fornication; they lay together before the feast. Child of the Holy Ghost means child of prophecy, the prophecy made to David. Joseph, a just man, was “not willing to make her a publick example”, which means stoned to death, and “was minded to put her away privily”: to hide her, because the child was his. Why would a just man hide a woman for something he did not do? And the angel called him “Joseph, thou son of David.” So our Lord sprang out of Judah through his father, made like his brethren in all things.

precepts.label: Proverbs 29:1
precepts.why:
Hebrews warns “lest any root of bitterness springing up trouble you”. Where does that root come from? Proverbs answers: “He, that being often reproved hardeneth his neck”. He that is often corrected hardens his neck, meaning his mind. You can't tell that brother nothing: I'm a man, you a man, I do what I want. Well, do what you want and burn by yourself.

That is the mindset of a lot of our brothers and sisters. They never took the scripture serious. Leadership corrects them, corrects them, corrects them, to the point where the correction is null and void, because they are not going to apply anything. After a while the Lord says, this spirit is rebellious as hell; he always hardens his mind and doesn't give a damn what you're saying.

You end up hardening your heart from always having correction done to you, until at the end of the day bitterness is formed, and then you're out the door with your wife and your children.

So the question for every brother and sister: are you one of the many that shall be offended when correction comes, when the men are told to get their homes in order and the women to be that pillar of rest and not stress? Or will you get in check with the Lord? The bitterness of Hebrews 12 grows out of a neck hardened against reproof.

precepts.label: Psalms 109:6-9
precepts.why:
Hebrews says “Lest there be any fornicator, or profane person, as Esau”. Paul is comparing the wicked of our people to Esau, who was wicked and estranged from the womb and went to the Canaanitish women when he wanted to get married. The bitter among us become compared to Edom, and Satan becomes their daddy. Psalms shows it: “Set thou a wicked man over him: and let Satan stand at his right hand.” That wicked man is Satan, the daddy of Esau and of the wicked of our people.

“When he shall be judged, let him be condemned: and let his prayer become sin.” Why does his prayer become sin? Because Christ said if you have an ought with your brother, go to him; leave your gift at the altar. You can't come to the Lord while the matter between you and your brother and your sister is not dealt with right. In 2018 there were extortioners speaking against leadership. You are not supposed to rise up against the hoary head; you are supposed to honor, and not revile the gods, your leaders. There was a lot of disrespect and dishonor.

“Let his days be few; and let another take his office. Let his children be fatherless, and his wife a widow.” That is what happens when Satan becomes your daddy. Repent.

So the profane spirit of Hebrews 12, the bitter brother or sister who turns on leadership, carries this lot. We are trying to encourage our people not to be worldly, not to keep the customs of Edom and the I-do-me, but to come back home to your people.

precepts.label: 1 John 3:8-10
precepts.why:
Hebrews warns of the “root of bitterness springing up”, and John shows what spirit jumps on you when you move that way. “He that committeth sin is of the devil; for the devil sinneth from the beginning.” That is the history being drawn out from Cain to Esau: the devil sinned from the beginning, and the same spirit runs down through his children.

“For this purpose the Son of God was manifested, that he might destroy the works of the devil.” The purpose of Christ is to destroy the works of the devil. So why do we move in the spirit of the devil and think that we are moving in the spirit of Christ?

“In this the children of God are manifest, and the children of the devil: whosoever doeth not righteousness is not of God.” This is the manifestation of the children of God. If you don't do righteousness, you are not of God. The scripture tells us how to deal uprightly with our brother and sister: if there is an offense, go by Matthew 18:15. You don't sow discord and murmur in the midst of the congregation and spread that spirit through our brothers and sisters.

“neither he that loveth not his brother.” When you don't love your brother, you are not moving in the spirit of Christ and you are not counted a child of God. You are the son and daughter of Cain, of Esau. We have to be mindful of this spirit and purge that leaven, that bitter spirit, out of us.

precepts.label: Romans 8:6-7
precepts.why:
Esau was a man of the field and a profane person: his religion is sin. Paul gives the name for that mind: “For to be carnally minded is death.” To be carnally minded is to be Edomite minded, the profane mind. It is death, and that is why he is called the son of perdition.

“but to be spiritually minded is life and peace.” When you are spiritually minded, you say, I have to gain my brother. That does not mean we always have to be buddy-buddy, but the scripture says instead of a friend become not an enemy. Brothers turn a brother into an enemy like a rival team in sports, stay pumped up against him and hold on to that feeling, waiting to get back at him. That is the carnal mind. Stay in the spirit.

“Because the carnal mind is enmity against God: for it is not subject to the law of God.” The Edomite mind, the mind of the spirit of Cain, goes against God and is not subject to his law.

So there are the children of God and the children of the devil, with no in between: either the godly mind or the Edomite mind. The bitter spirit that holds a grudge against a brother is the carnal mind of Esau, and it leads to the same death and rejection he found.

precepts.label: Psalms 50:16-17
precepts.why:
This is the Edomite mindset, the carnal mind at war with God. “But unto the wicked God saith, What hast thou to do to declare my statutes, or that thou shouldest take my covenant in thy mouth?” Unto the wicked, the white man, God says: hold on, you are carnally minded. Why are you out there talking about in God we trust? Why are you swearing in on the Bible when you do nothing according to the scriptures?

“Seeing thou hatest instruction, and castest my words behind thee.” He talks about in God we trust while he has transgenders out there, putting two men together. They don't do anything the scriptures say. They cast the word behind their back, because the carnal mind is at war with God.

This is the battle of the spirit and the flesh, and that inner battle is within us too. It is the same profane spirit Hebrews names in Esau, whose religion is sin and who despised what was sacred. So we have to make sure we stand in the spirit, and not take God's covenant in our mouth while we cast his words behind us, as a brother does when he holds on to a bitter spirit.
