precepts.label: Genesis 26:34-35
precepts.why:
Hebrews calls Esau a “fornicator, or profane person”, and brothers often ask what that means. The scriptures explain it, beginning with his marriages: “Esau was forty years old when he took to wife Judith the daughter of Beeri the Hittite, and Bashemath the daughter of Elon the Hittite: Which were a grief of mind unto Isaac and to Rebekah.” His parents did not like his choice of those Hittite women.

Some unlearned Israelites use these two verses to say Esau was black, because his children were mixed with the Hittites. No. God kept that line the way it is. Even today, no matter how black you are, if you marry a white woman you can tell the child is a hybrid: high yellow, sometimes yellow hair, green eyes. Look at Drake as a boy with his family: his hair is like his father's, but his complexion is closer to his mother's.

So you mean back then God could not maintain that same look, that lighter red complexion, in Esau's line? No, God don't have that power? Shut up, Negro. Be quiet. These hybrid children look more like Esau. Mixing with the Hittites did not make Esau black; it is part of what made him a fornicator.

precepts.label: Genesis 28:8-9
precepts.why:
After the Hittite wives, Esau went further: “Esau seeing that the daughters of Canaan pleased not Isaac his father; Then went Esau unto Ishmael, and took unto the wives which he had Mahalath the daughter of Ishmael Abraham’s son, the sister of Nebajoth, to be his wife.”

Esau saw that Isaac was pissed off that he married the daughters of Canaan, and instead of turning back to his own kindred, he went to Ishmael. So now he married Arab kids too. That is what Esau was doing: taking wives outside his father's tribe, one after another.

That is the fornication Hebrews 12:16 names. Esau married the Hittites and the Ishmaelites, strange women, and he was profane because for “one morsel of meat” he sold his birthright; it meant a lot, and he did not care about it.

precepts.label: Tobit 4:12
precepts.why:
Tobit 4:12 shows why Esau is called a fornicator: “Beware of all whoredom, my son, and chiefly take a wife of the seed of thy fathers, and take not a strange woman to wife, which is not of thy father’s tribe.” Whoredom falls under fornication. Esau married Hittite women and Ishmaelite women, strange women not of his father's tribe.

Ishmael was the beginning of another race; Genesis is the beginning of races. Tobit goes on: “for we are the children of the prophets, Noe, Abraham, Isaac, and Jacob: remember, my son, that our fathers from the beginning, even that they all married wives of their own kindred, and were blessed in their children, and their seed shall inherit the land.”

So the fathers married within their own kindred and were blessed in their children; Esau did not. Then there is the profaneness. Hebrews says he sold his birthright “for one morsel of meat”, and that shows what was in the pottage. When Esau came in from the field faint and said, “Feed me, I pray thee, with that same red pottage”, he wanted it as it was, raw, red and bloody. “therefore was his name called Edom”, which means red. He said, “Behold, I am at the point to die: and what profit shall this birthright do to me?” and “thus Esau despised his birthright.” And there are brothers today lusting after these same people and having children with them.

That is why, “when he would have inherited the blessing, he was rejected”: rejected by God, “for he found no place of repentance, though he sought it carefully with tears.”

precepts.label: Ephesians 2:21-22
precepts.why:
Christ's body was the temple, and his temple today is us. Peter says “Ye also, as lively stones, are built up a spiritual house”, and Paul shows how that house grows: “In whom all the building fitly framed together groweth unto an holy temple in the Lord”. All the building is you and me. See that word growing: Peter just explained how we grow, by laying aside all malice, all guile, all hypocrisies, all evil speakings, and desiring the sincere milk of the word.

You know what fitly framed together means? Stones have to come together. Brothers, we must merge together. Whatever your position is, play that position. Don't try to change positions through deceit. A brother was demoted in New York for lying over a simple thing; when we ask, most of the time we already know the answer, and when the witnesses are called, the liar is put on front street and found not worthy of his rank. A stone full of guile does not fit in the frame.

“In whom ye also are builded together for an habitation of God through the Spirit.” Wherever our congregation is, that is a spiritual house, the real temple, and God dwells in it through the Spirit. That is why Zerubbabel is our example: he got to his position not only for his fighting skills but because he was of noble character, understanding God's truth. We should not be deceitful, envious, hateful or filled with guile toward one another, but lively stones with zeal, passion and fire, built together into the house where God lives.

precepts.label: 1 Corinthians 3:16-17
precepts.why:
“Know ye not that ye are the temple of God, and that the Spirit of God dwelleth in you?” We are the temple, the spiritual house Peter speaks of. “If any man defile the temple of God, him shall God destroy; for the temple of God is holy, which temple ye are.” That is why we have to change the way we conduct ourselves. Our communications must change. The malice, guile, hypocrisies, envies and evil speakings of 1 Peter 2:1 defile the temple.

Paul goes on in 2 Timothy: “Let every one that nameth the name of Christ depart from iniquity.” “But in a great house there are not only vessels of gold and of silver, but also of wood and of earth; and some to honour, and some to dishonour.” The great house is the nation of Israel, the real nation. There are brothers and sisters who are gold and silver, applying 1 Peter 2:1-2. And there are those of wood and earth, meaning no good: fringes and a border of blue, but they have not changed their lives in two or three years. Not the new people, but those who have been with us for years and are still grimy, still that secret adulterer, still that liar, complainer, murmurer.

The captains must be able to identify in their school who is honourable and who is dishonourable. “If a man therefore purge himself from these, he shall be a vessel unto honour, sanctified, and meet for the master’s use, and prepared unto every good work.” Purge means cut them off, like pruning a plant and taking away the bad elements. I knew which brothers always got me in trouble; I almost got arrested many a time with those grimy brothers, and I had to cut them off and hang out with leadership. Keep the temple holy.

precepts.label: Acts 17:10-11
precepts.why:
God “delivered just Lot, vexed with the filthy conversation of the wicked”. Examine yourself: are you vexed with the filthy conversation of this world? Or are you up late scrolling, looking at booties, two hours in the middle of the night on your phone? Those two hours you could have read the Bible. If you can't sleep, pick up the Bible; half of one chapter and the demon will put you to sleep. In time the Most High will wake up your spirit, and you will read one, two, three, four chapters.

“For that righteous man dwelling among them, in seeing and hearing, vexed his righteous soul from day to day”. Every day you wake up you should be vexed with the filthy conversation of this world. But to be vexed, you have to be in this Bible. It is by having the word of God in you that sin starts becoming repulsive. If you are not reading and not studying, the sins of the world will be normal to you, just like everybody else. The Lord saved a remnant, and that is why we did not become as Sodom and Gomorrha. What is that remnant doing? Studying day and night.

Paul and Silas were sent by night unto Berea and went into the synagogue, and “These were more noble than those in Thessalonica, in that they received the word with all readiness of mind, and searched the scriptures daily, whether those things were so.” If you are searching the scriptures daily, you will be vexed with the filthy conversation of this world. If you are not, whose words are going to be in your ears? The TV, the street, your phone: the ways of this world.

God turned Sodom and Gomorrha into ashes, “making them an ensample unto those that after should live ungodly”. America read the example and legalized gay marriage anyway, a habitual line stepper pushing the envelope until his sin reached the heavens. Only the one searching the scriptures daily will be vexed like Lot and delivered like Lot.

thread.label: 2 Peter 3:3-11
thread.text: Knowing this first, that there shall come in the last days scoffers, walking after their own lusts,

classes.title: Drowning in Sin & Perdition

precepts.label: Job 1:22
precepts.why:
Peter says “there shall come in the last days scoffers, walking after their own lusts, And saying, Where is the promise of his coming?” A scoffer mocks and ridicules; he doesn't just disagree, he expresses insolent doubt and derision, openly opposing God and divine truth, arrogant, close-minded and fueled by pride. Of all the reasons people scoff at the Bible, one stands out: the problem of evil and suffering, why God would permit harm.

An ex-pastor turned atheist, who preached in the streets and the prisons for fifteen years, now says the Bible is fiction, that black people are not Israelites, that even if we were he would hate that God, and asks what Jesus did about slavery, Jim Crow and the Trail of Tears. Going through his page, the reason showed itself: he has a child in remission from stage four brain cancer. That's a lot of trauma. Maybe they tried the holy water and the laying on of hands and nothing worked.

A lot of times when bad things happen, people turn around and blame God: God, why did you do this to me? That is why a lot of people turn atheist. One sister had a miscarriage and started blaming God. But we have to do what Job did. Job lost his children, his wealth and his health, and “In all this Job sinned not, nor charged God foolishly.” He didn't charge God foolishly. That's it. We cannot charge God foolishly, knowing that he has his reasons.

And as for the cures for cancer being hidden: after the Epstein files dropped we saw how much the pharmaceutical companies were holding back. They already have patents on things and hold them back because there is more money in the treatment than the cure. The scoffer blames God for what the wicked have done, and he is willingly ignorant, like the scoffers in the days of Noah, whom God put to death.

thread.label: 2 Peter 3:8
thread.text: But, beloved, be not ignorant of this one thing, that one day is with the Lord as a thousand years, and a thousand years as one day.

classes.title: The Pride Of Thine Heart

precepts.label: Baruch 4:25
precepts.why:
Peter says “that one day is with the Lord as a thousand years, and a thousand years as one day.” David says our days are seventy, eighty years. Do the math: if a thousand years is one day to God, eighty years is 0.08 of a day, about an hour and fifty-five minutes. An entire human lifetime is less than two hours to God, and it may be even less than that; the concept of time does not apply to the Ancient of days. Eighty years and you come back and God says, you just left, why you back already?

That is why the scriptures say things like Baruch: “My children, suffer patiently the wrath that is come upon you from God: for thine enemy hath persecuted thee”. It is happening right now. We are going through it, and it seems like forever, because down here it takes forever to become an adult, to get your license, to turn 21. Lord, come save us; they are doing their worst.

Then, “but shortly thou shalt see his destruction, and shalt tread upon his neck.” Shortly: in less than a few minutes of God's time your life is over, and in an hour or so you see the destruction of your enemy and have a lifetime of God time, eternal. So suffer patiently. What seems long to us is short to him.

precepts.label: Isaiah 54:7-8
precepts.why:
“For a small moment have I forsaken thee; but with great mercies will I gather thee.” A small moment. That is why God says small moment: it is not even two hours to him, not even a day to him. If a thousand years is as one day with the Lord, our whole captivity is a moment in his eyes.

“In a little wrath I hid my face from thee for a moment; but with everlasting kindness will I have mercy on thee, saith the Lord thy Redeemer.” For a moment. Start thinking like that: I'm only here for a short while.

And since it is only a moment, Peter gives the wisdom Christ put in his mouth: “Humble yourselves therefore under the mighty hand of God, that he may exalt you in due time”. The real exaltation we want is when we go back to him: a crown from God Almighty, and you can't get any higher than that. “Casting all your care upon him; for he careth for you.” He knows you only have a short amount of time here.

Right after that comes “your adversary the devil, as a roaring lion, walketh about, seeking whom he may devour”, because Satan is looking for the prideful, the ones who think they know more than God in the little time they have been here. We stress over three to five business days and get mad when Amazon doesn't deliver in two. God's small moment calls for humility, not pride.

precepts.label: Wisdom of Solomon 3:5
precepts.why:
We feel what we are going through. We complain, we cry, we fast, we do what we can to make it through. But look what God calls it: “And having been a little chastised, they shall be greatly rewarded”. A little chastised. We are not even yet at the point of being persecuted and put to death, and he calls this a little chastising.

That fits with 2 Peter 3:8: if one day with the Lord is as a thousand years, a whole lifetime of suffering is a little chastising, less than two hours in his eyes, and the reward that follows is eternal.

Then, “for God proved them, and found them worthy for himself.” The chastising is the proving. He tries us to find us worthy unto himself. So we have to endure to the end, people. We have to endure to the end, humbling ourselves under his mighty hand, and when the short moment is over, those found worthy will be greatly rewarded.

thread.label: 1 John 2:15-17
thread.text: Love not the world, neither the things that are in the world. If any man love the world, the love of the Father is not in him.

classes.title: Eleutherophobia the Fear of Freedom

precepts.label: Sirach 10:12-13
precepts.why:
John says “all that is in the world, the lust of the flesh, and the lust of the eyes, and the pride of life, is not of the Father, but is of the world.” The lust of the flesh: in America everything is accessible; order it and it's there in twenty minutes. The lust of the eyes: social media, looking at the big butt, keeping up with the Joneses, twerking, the competition of niggardom: I can jump on a car better than she can, I can roll a blunt this big, I can rap about nothing and can't say my ABCs. Our people love the world for those things but fail to love God.

And what is the pride of life? Sirach answers: “The beginning of pride is when one departeth from God, and his heart is turned away from his Maker.” That is the pride of life we just read in 1 John. “And the sixth angel poured out his vial upon the great river Euphrates; and the water thereof was dried up”. The Euphrates runs from Iraq up through Syria to Turkey, and it is drying up right now, from severe droughts, with dams along it; whoever controls the water controls the agriculture. So don't tell us the Bible isn't true. We are in these days, the time is now. You won't read this in the Quran, the Gilgamesh epic or the Egyptian Book of the Dead; you only read it in the Bible.

Why is it dried up? So “that the way of the kings of the east might be prepared.” Ezra shows who the kings of the east are: “Behold an horrible vision, and the appearance thereof from the east: Where the nations of the dragons of Arabia shall come out with many chariots, and the multitude of them shall be carried as the wind upon earth, that all they which hear them may fear and tremble.” The dragons of Arabia are the Arabs.

“Also the Carmanians raging in wrath shall go forth as the wild boars of the wood, and with great power shall they come, and join battle with them, and shall waste a portion of the land of the Assyrians.” The Carmanians are Iran, the Iranians. And the land of the Assyrians here is Israel: they are going to waste a portion of the land of Israel.

Then come the three unclean spirits out of the mouth of the dragon, the beast and the false prophet: politics with NATO, the financial system of the United States, and Christianity. “For they are the spirits of devils, working miracles, which go forth unto the kings of the earth and of the whole world, to gather them to the battle of that great day of God Almighty.” Those three spirits, all coming from the white man, are leading to war on top of war like we have never seen, and the way is being prepared for the kings of the east.

precepts.label: Revelation 13:11
precepts.why:
The three unclean spirits like frogs come “out of the mouth of the dragon, and out of the mouth of the beast, and out of the mouth of the false prophet.” Those three unclean spirits are politics, religion and finance. To see the first of them, go to the beast of Revelation 13.

John says, “I beheld another beast coming up out of the earth; and he had two horns like a lamb, and he spake as a dragon.” Those two horns like a lamb are the two political parties, the Democrats and the Republicans: two political systems that look gentle like a lamb. But he speaks as a dragon.

That is the politics, the frog that comes out of the mouth of the dragon. And what comes out of a mouth? Communication, and that communication is propaganda, persuasion and lies. These are “the spirits of devils”, and they do not stay at home: they “go forth unto the kings of the earth and of the whole world”, gathering them “to the battle of that great day of God Almighty.”

precepts.label: Revelation 13:16-17
precepts.why:
The second frog comes “out of the mouth of the beast.” Go back to Revelation 13: “he causeth all, both small and great, rich and poor, free and bond, to receive a mark in their right hand, or in their foreheads: And that no man might buy or sell, save he that had the mark, or the name of the beast, or the number of his name.”

That no man might buy or sell: that is the finance, one of the three unclean spirits like frogs, alongside the politics and the religion.

It is coming to a time where, if you are not in cahoots with, in support of, or in allegiance with what America pushes, you will not be able to buy or sell. On a large scale that is trade between nations, but it is also the regular buying and selling of everyday life. That is why they are trying to do away with the currency as it is now and bring everything into a digital system: to monitor God's people who speak up against this society.

The third frog, out of the mouth of the false prophet, is Christianity, their religion and their religious systems. Politics, finance and religion together are the spirits of devils working miracles, going out to the kings of the whole world, not only here at home.

precepts.label: Deuteronomy 28:48
precepts.why:
Babylon's merchandise runs from “gold, and silver, and precious stones” down to “slaves, and souls of men.” The tin, the copper, the iron, the rubber, the bauxite, the slaves and the cheap labor have all been taken out of our countries. These countries are not underdeveloped; they are overexploited. They all should be rich countries, world powers, with the blessings the Lord gave us in those places. It was done in Latin America and in Africa, especially the west coast where we are dispersed, and the slave routes and trade routes were the commerce they made of us.

The way they keep that dominance today is economic, backed by the threat of military power, and it follows a pattern, as with Noriega and now Maduro. First they criminalize the leader with drug, terror and corruption narratives, framing mischief by a law. Then they declare the regime illegitimate. Then they apply sanctions and economic siege. Then they isolate the country diplomatically and militarily, remove or extract the leadership, and install or manage a transition authority.

The sanctions are the modern face of Deuteronomy 28:48, for those who say the curses were only for back then or only for the time of the conquistadors: “Therefore shalt thou serve thine enemies which the Lord shall send against thee, in hunger, and in thirst, and in nakedness, and in want of all things”. Want of all things because of sanctions and their economic might. If you try to nationalize your resources or do things outside of their money, even though you have your own resources you are overexploited to the point that you cannot do it on your own. There is no might in your hand.

“and he shall put a yoke of iron upon thy neck, until he have destroyed thee.” A lot of times we did this willingly. It is the same pattern we followed with Assyria and Egypt: when the United States became a world power we leaned on them, and found out really quick that they do not keep their word on anything. It is history repeating itself, the doctrine of the scripture executed over and over again.

precepts.label: Revelation 2:9
precepts.why:
“I know thy works, and tribulation, and poverty, (but thou art rich).” First and foremost, the riches are the promise of the kingdom of heaven. Unto us pertain the promises, the law, the adoption of sons, all of it; we are the ones Christ died for. That is the true riches.

But Revelation 18 gives it a new spin. Babylon trades in gold, silver, precious stones, fine wood, iron and marble, and these come out of our lands. So-called third world countries are rich with resources; it is the people who are poor, because they are overexploited. What a distinction. The countries of Israel are not underdeveloped, and the poverty of our people sits on top of the riches of our lands.

“and I know the blasphemy of them which say they are Jews, and are not, but are the synagogue of Satan.” Those who say they are Jews and are not are part of the same machine working to oppress our people, and it is the same playbook of sanctions, isolation and regime change that runs through the whole system.

So Revelation 2:9 stands beside Revelation 18:12: the merchants of Babylon grow rich off the goods of the lands where Israel is scattered, while Israel lives in tribulation and poverty, though rich in the promises and in the land itself.

precepts.label: Revelation 22:8-9
precepts.why:
John says it twice. In Revelation 19 he fell at the angel's feet, and here again: “I John saw these things, and heard them. And when I had heard and seen, I fell down to worship before the feet of the angel which shewed me these things.”

And the angel says the same thing again: “See thou do it not: for I am thy fellowservant, and of thy brethren the prophets, and of them which keep the sayings of this book: worship God.” He will not take worship, because he is not God. He is a fellowservant, one of the brethren.

That is who the angels are: our brothers. They are not demons. They ate with Lot because they have mouths just like us, and they were going to lie down because they look like us. Esau calls them humanoids, and to Esau they are going to be some demons, but those are our brothers. The angels have tribes too, and in Revelation 21, do not be surprised if the angels standing at the twelve gates are each standing at the gate of their own tribe.

precepts.label: Tobit 5:12-14
precepts.why:
Here Raphael, before he makes himself known, presents himself to Tobit another way: “I am Azarias, the son of Ananias the great, and of thy brethren.” An angel of God naming himself as one of the brethren, just as the angel told John, “I am thy fellowservant, and of thy brethren.”

Tobit answers, “Thou art welcome, brother; be not now angry with me, because I have enquired to know thy tribe and thy family; for thou art my brother, of an honest and good stock.” Tobit asks after his tribe and his family, and receives him as a brother.

He knows his people: “I know Ananias and Jonathas, sons of that great Samaias, as we went together to Jerusalem to worship, and offered the firstborn, and the tenths of the fruits; and they were not seduced with the error of our brethren: my brother, thou art of a good stock.”

So the angel who walked with Tobit's son was taken for an Israelite brother, of a tribe and a family. That is how close the angels are to us: they look like us, they have tribes too, and they are our brethren.

precepts.label: Tobit 12:15
precepts.why:
Now Raphael makes himself known: “I am Raphael, one of the seven holy angels, which present the prayers of the saints, and which go in and out before the glory of the Holy One.” The one Tobit called brother, Azarias of his brethren, was the angel all along.

Why do the angels present the prayers of the saints? Because they minister unto us. They are ministering spirits working on our behalf, because those are our brothers.

They are not demonic spirits sent here to oppose the people that inhabit this place called the United Snakes of America. That is untrue. That is popular persuasion; that is lies. The world is being taught to call what comes out of the heavens demons and fallen angels, so that it will gather to fight against Christ and his army. But the angels are our brethren, fellowservants who keep the testimony of Jesus, and we worship God alone.

precepts.why:
The armies in heaven follow Christ “upon white horses, clothed in fine linen, white and clean.” That fine linen, white and clean, is the immortal body. To prove it, go to Isaiah, speaking to Babylon: “Thy nakedness shall be uncovered, yea, thy shame shall be seen: I will take vengeance, and I will not meet thee as a man.”

Christ said he is going to take vengeance, and he will not meet Babylon as a man. Christ is coming back with that immortal body. You will not be able to nail him back to the cross like you did in Jerusalem.

That is what the white horse and the fine linen, white and clean, make reference to. And he comes to make war, because God is a man of war: “in righteousness he doth judge and make war.” His vesture is dipped in blood, because there is going to be a lot of bloodshed, a lot of killing. On his head are many crowns, because he is going to take everyone's crowns and be the one King, “KING OF KINGS, AND LORD OF LORDS.”

precepts.label: Wisdom of Solomon 5:1-6
precepts.why:
Revelation says the beast and the kings of the earth and their armies were gathered together to make war against him that sits on the horse. Wisdom shows what happens when they see him: “Then shall the righteous man stand in great boldness before the face of such as have afflicted him, and made no account of his labours.” That is us, the Israelites, standing before Esau and the nations, who made no account of our labours here.

“When they see it, they shall be troubled with terrible fear, and shall be amazed at the strangeness of his salvation, so far beyond all that they looked for.” The strangeness of his salvation is the chariots, us being taken up. That is going to be strange and foreign to them. They will no longer talk about the deliverance out of Egypt, but about the new deliverance from the land of the north. A black God, a black Christ, coming to redeem his black people: that is going to be the new talk of the town.

“And they repenting and groaning for anguish of spirit shall say within themselves, This was he, whom we had sometimes in derision, and a proverb of reproach.” Christ is going to put it in their mind: these are the people you afflicted, raped, robbed, murdered and enslaved. These are my people.

“We fools accounted his life madness, and his end to be without honour: How is he numbered among the children of God, and his lot is among the saints! Therefore have we erred from the way of truth.”

precepts.label: 2 Esdras 13:1-11
precepts.why:
Revelation says the armies were gathered together to make war against him that sat on the horse and against his army. Ezra saw that same war. “there arose a wind from the sea”, and “that man waxed strong with the thousands of heaven: and when he turned his countenance to look, all the things trembled.” The man that came out of the sea is Christ, with the thousands of heaven, the armies that follow him.

And “whensoever the voice went out of his mouth, all they burned that heard his voice, like as the earth faileth when it feeleth the fire.” He speaks the laws out of his mouth, and the people just disintegrate, because they are guilty of that law. That is the sharp sword out of his mouth in Revelation, the laws of God.

Then “there was gathered together a multitude of men, out of number, from the four winds of the heaven, to subdue the man that came out of the sea”. They will have one consent, because the Most High is going to harden them like he did Pharaoh. And the popular persuasion is already laying the groundwork: let's all come together and fight the demons coming from space.

After this, “all they which were gathered together to subdue him were sore afraid, and yet durst fight.” Scared to death, but the Most High moves them. As Romans 9 shows, he built them up, just like ancient Egypt: Babylon the Great, this white man, this Edomite, built up just to be destroyed, made to fight against him.

And “he neither lifted up his hand, nor held sword, nor any instrument of war”, but sent out of his mouth “a blast of fire”, “a flaming breath”, and “sparks and tempests”, and “burned them up every one, so that upon a sudden of an innumerable multitude nothing was to be perceived, but only dust and smell of smoke.” Ashes to ashes, and dust to dust.

precepts.label: Hosea 1:10
precepts.why:
“Afterward saw I the same man come down from the mountain, and call unto him another peaceable Multitude.” The same man is Jesus the Christ, the black Messiah of Revelation 1, with feet like burnt brass and hair like wool. And the angel explains it: “he gathered another peaceable multitude unto him”, those are the ten tribes, the northern kingdom. That is who Christ gathers in these last days, through the work the prophets are doing in the worldwide blitzes, in Puerto Rico, Ecuador, Mexico, Chile.

The historians knew who that peaceable multitude was. Columbus gave the peaceable multitude of the islands the name Indios, because he took their home to be the Indies, but perhaps also because he thought of them as living in God, en Dios. Columbus was reading the book of Esdras. The scriptures call them a peaceable multitude; the world called them noble savages.

The historian Duran found more confirmation in Hosea: “Yet the number of the children of Israel shall be as the sand of the sea, which cannot be measured nor numbered.” Surely, he argued, that promise was fulfilled by the multitudes the Spanish found in the new world. Remember Israel blessed Ephraim and Manasseh to be a multitude of nations; that is what the Spaniards found.

Duran also noted that the Indians of Mexico had traditions of long journeys like the one from Assyria to Arzareth, flights like the Exodus from Egypt, earthquakes that swallowed evil men, manna falling from heaven, and an old man who began the tale of his people’s origins with the words in the beginning, like Genesis. Why would so-called Indians be quoting the Bible unless they were Israelites? We had books, we carried the Bible with us, and they stole our records.

So the peaceable multitude Christ calls is the ten tribes scattered on this side of the world, and Hosea’s promise stands over them: “in the place where it was said unto them, Ye are not my people, there it shall be said unto them, Ye are the sons of the living God.”

That was the Assyrian captivity, 722 BC; the northern kingdom was forcefully displaced into Assyria. Then Esdras says, “But they took this counsel among themselves, that they would leave the multitude of the heathen”. That is a jump in history, into the Persian captivity, when Cyrus the Persian gave us freedom.

For our people who don't know that history, Ezra 1 shows it: “Now in the first year of Cyrus king of Persia, that the word of the Lord by the mouth of Jeremiah might be fulfilled, the Lord stirred up the spirit of Cyrus king of Persia”. The Most High moved the king of Persia in 539 BC. Cyrus proclaimed, “The Lord God of heaven hath given me all the kingdoms of the earth; and he hath charged me to build him an house at Jerusalem, which is in Judah.”

“Who is there among you of all his people? his God be with him, and let him go up to Jerusalem”. His people: not Persians, but Israelites, God's people. “And whosoever remaineth in any place where he sojourneth, let the men of his place help him with silver, and with gold, and with goods, and with beasts”. Whether we were in Assyria or in Persia, wherever we were scattered and displaced, we were given freedom to go back to Israel and build the house of God.

That is what 2 Esdras 13 is recording. The ten tribes were given that freedom, but they took counsel to go instead “into a further country, where never mankind dwelt, That they might there keep their statutes, which they never kept in their own land.” The northern kingdom wanted a fresh start, tired of captivity after captivity: Assyrian, Babylonian, Persian. So they went into Arsareth, the land Columbus identified as America. Our land is Israel; we were not always in the islands.

precepts.label: Revelation 18:9-10
precepts.why:
Ezra saw the clouds and the horrible star, the missiles, and then “they shall go stedfastly unto Babylon, and make her afraid.” Babylon is America. They talk about making America great again; God says he is going to make her afraid again. “They shall come to her, and besiege her”: it will not be a one-on-one fight. The nations, NATO among them, will besiege America and pour out all their wrath upon her. “Then shall the dust and smoke go up unto the heaven, and all they that be about her shall bewail her.”

Revelation tells the same thing: “And the kings of the earth, who have committed fornication and lived deliciously with her, shall bewail her, and lament for her, when they shall see the smoke of her burning, Standing afar off for the fear of her torment, saying, Alas, alas, that great city Babylon, that mighty city! for in one hour is thy judgment come.”

The smoke that goes up unto heaven in Ezra is the smoke of her burning in Revelation. The ones about her that bewail her are the kings of the earth who lived deliciously with her, standing afar off in fear. Her judgment comes in one hour.

Then “they that remain under her shall do service unto them that have put her in fear”: prisoners of war. And the party is not over. After the fall of Babylon, the Lord bends Judah for him, fills the bow with Ephraim, and raises up the sons of Zion against the sons of Greece.

thread.label: 2 Esdras 16:68
thread.text: For, behold, the burning wrath of a great multitude is kindled over you, and they shall take away certain of you, and feed you, being idle, with things offered unto idols.

classes.title: Christ: the Enemy of Christianity

precepts.label: Isaiah 19:20
precepts.why:
“For, behold, the burning wrath of a great multitude is kindled over you”. Who is this great multitude that is over us? It is law enforcement, their military, set over the believing Israelites. Isaiah proves it.

“In that day shall there be an altar to the Lord in the midst of the land of Egypt, and a pillar at the border thereof”. This Egypt is a spiritual Egypt: America. An altar is used for sacrifice, so there is going to be a lot of death. “And it shall be for a sign and for a witness unto the Lord of hosts in the land of Egypt: for they shall cry unto the Lord because of the oppressors”.

Why would we cry unto the Lord? Because of the oppressors, with an s on it: more than one. That is the great multitude whose burning wrath is kindled over us. That is Jacob's trouble, and we have not gotten to that part yet.

So the great multitude of 2 Esdras 16 is the oppressors of Isaiah 19, the power of spiritual Egypt that will be over our people in this land, and it is because of them that Israel will cry unto the Lord.

precepts.label: Joel 2:17
precepts.why:
Joel shows the same cry. “Blow the trumpet in Zion, sanctify a fast, call a solemn assembly”, and “Let the priests, the ministers of the Lord, weep between the porch and the altar, and let them say, Spare thy people, O Lord, and give not thine heritage to reproach, that the heathen should rule over them: wherefore should they say among the people, Where is their God?”

Why will we cry, Spare thy people? We just read it in Isaiah 19: because of the oppressors. They will say, we killed you, where is your God? We cut your throat, we ended your bank account, where is your God?

“Then will the Lord be jealous for his land, and pity his people.” He pities his people because we are not in the land. But he promises not to leave us alone: “Behold, I will send you corn, and wine, and oil”, “and I will no more make you a reproach among the heathen”.

“But I will remove far off from you the northern army”. That is the name the Bible gives to the power that is going to be on us: the oppressors of Isaiah 19, the great multitude of 2 Esdras 16, is the northern army. He will drive him into a land barren and desolate, with his face toward the east sea, the Dead Sea, and his hinder part toward the utmost sea, the Mediterranean, “and his stink shall come up”. The white man shall meet death when he goes to that land, because he has done evil things.

precepts.label: Sirach 33:27
precepts.why:
The great multitude “shall take away certain of you, and feed you, being idle, with things offered unto idols.” Spell that word: i-d-l-e. “Send him to labour, that he be not idle; for idleness teacheth much evil.”

Idle means a person avoiding work: lazy, indolent, slothful, shiftless, inactive, sluggish, lethargic; without purpose or effect. Those words fit some of you in here, men and women. Not the new people who just came, but those who have been with us two years or more. What are you doing? Do you have an office? Is there something you are doing here in Israel? If not, you are idle, and idleness teaches much evil.

And what will the idle be fed? Things offered unto idols, i-d-o-l: an image or representation of a god used as an object of worship. Look at the images of the Roman Catholic Church; those are idols. One word: Christianity.

So the ones the multitude takes away and feeds with idolatry are the ones with no purpose in here. Because you were idle, you will be seduced and given Christianity, that idolatrous religion. Stay busy in the work of the Most High.

thread.text: And when one of the Ninevites went and complained of me to the king, that I buried them, and hid myself; understanding that I was sought for to be put to death, I withdrew myself for fear.

classes.title: The Nativity: the Bloodline, Birthright, & the Messiah

precepts.label: Revelation 13:17
precepts.why:
Tobit had a decent job in captivity, over the king’s accounts, and while he was well off he did good: “I gave many alms to my brethren, and gave my bread to the hungry, And my clothes to the naked”. When Sennacherib came back from Judea, where an angel killed 185,000 of his men, he came back mad and took it out on Ephraim, throwing them off the walls. Tobit would sneak and bury them: “I buried them privily”. He was not supposed to; the king wanted to see those bodies, “but the bodies were not found, when they were sought for of the king.”

Then he got ratted out: “when one of the Ninevites went and complained of me to the king, that I buried them”, he knew he “was sought for to be put to death” and became a fugitive. “Then all my goods were forcibly taken away, neither was there any thing left me, beside my wife Anna and my son Tobias.” Everything he had, they took from him.

That is what Revelation 13 means when it says no man should buy or sell. All the positions and things you have here: the time is going to come when you go against this system, teach against it, and do not support the beast, and everything you have they will take from you. Tobit is the example. They took his possessions, and most likely his wife and child were taken too, imprisoned, because he was considered an enemy of the state. That is the consequence for serving God, and the time is coming when you will have to make the choice to serve God.

But the Lord spared his son and wife. Within fifty-five days Sennacherib’s own sons killed him, and Sarchedonus set Tobit’s nephew Achiacharus over the accounts. “And Achiacharus intreating for me, I returned to Nineve.” His nephew was cupbearer, “keeper of the signet, and steward, and overseer of the accounts”, next unto the king, and he spoke for his uncle. Then “my wife Anna was restored unto me, with my son Tobias, in the feast of Pentecost”: he was keeping the feasts in captivity, not in Jerusalem.

Tobit stayed faithful, and he was not alone out there being righteous. He looked out for his people with the status he had, fed the hungry and gave alms to those keeping the commandments in captivity, and when it came back around his nephew did the same for him. The Lord looked out for him as he looked out for his own people.

precepts.label: Psalms 96:4-5
precepts.why:
Wisdom tells the kings of the earth that “the desire of wisdom bringeth to a kingdom”, and to “honour wisdom, that ye may reign for evermore.” David shows why the kingdoms of the nations never did: “For the Lord is great, and greatly to be praised: he is to be feared above all gods. For all the gods of the nations are idols”.

They are all idols. All kingdoms fall because they do not walk after the wisdom of God. Name a kingdom that has kept the commandments of God. They don't. They fall because they serve idol gods, and pride destroys them, as it destroyed Herod, who gave not God the glory and was eaten of worms. Assyrian, Babylon, Greek, Rome, America: nobody is exempt from pride and God destroying them.

It is no different with Babylon the Great. This Edomite has the most gods of all: he has all the idol gods of every kingdom wrapped up in one, in different forms. That is why Obadiah follows, “concerning Edom”, the white man, the Caucasian, his biblical name: “thou art greatly despised”, and “The pride of thine heart hath deceived thee”. None of the kings before him, Assyrians, Babylonians, Persians, Greeks or Romans, was more prideful than Esau.

The same judgment is on us. The power God gave was given to us by God too, and for our pride as a nation we have been destroyed. The only way our kingdom will last for ever is when we walk in wisdom and humility toward God. Outside of that, the kingdom comes down, the same as it did with all the nations before us.

precepts.label: 1 Corinthians 2:6
precepts.why:
Wisdom is “loving the thing that is good quick, which cannot be letted, ready to do good”. That wisdom will properly guide us in everything we seek to move in, every endeavour, everything we seek to make happen. But not just any kind of wisdom: God’s wisdom. Paul makes that clear.

“Howbeit we speak wisdom among them that are perfect”. We speak wisdom among these people out here who think they have some real wisdom. “Yet not the wisdom of this world”: we do not speak their wisdom. We speak God’s wisdom, God’s commandments; that is how we speak.

“Nor of the princes of this world, that come to nought”. The wisdom of the princes of this world is not God’s wisdom, and it comes to nothing. The Lord is going to bring all that wisdom down, and it is our wisdom that is going to be raised up in authority in this society.

That is the difference between God’s wisdom and what we learned under Christianity, clapping with a Bible while learning nothing about ourselves, our condition, our deliverance or our salvation, and still having white supremacy on the mind. The wisdom of this world taught us to look at ourselves as nothing, and everything behind that was destroyed. God’s wisdom is “the breath of the power of God, and a pure influence flowing from the glory of the Almighty: therefore can no defiled thing fall into her.” That breath has to come in, as in Ezekiel 37 when “the breath came into them, and they lived, and stood up upon their feet, an exceeding great army”, and undo all that damage.

precepts.label: Ezekiel 35:5
precepts.why:
Wisdom says the Lord gave the ungodly “place of repentance, not being ignorant that they were a naughty generation, and that their malice was bred in them”. Their malice is their hatred for us, shown in all the sins they have committed against us, and it is still going on: innocent blood shed again in Springfield, Illinois, a woman who called the police for help and ended up murdered in her own house. How do you call the police for help and they kill you?

Ezekiel names that malice: “Because thou hast had a perpetual hatred, and hast shed the blood of the children of Israel by the force of the sword in the time of their calamity, in the time that their iniquity had an end”. While we are here struggling and suffering, they are still killing us.

That is why the Lord executes judgment on them “by little and little”: a flood here, a fire there, an earthquake here, a war there. He is not ignorant of what they are; he created them, so he knows their pedigree. “Their cogitation would never be changed”: their way of thinking, the hatred they have for us, cannot change. That is why the cop shot the man and said he did not even know why he shot him. It is in them.

It was there from the beginning: “And Esau hated Jacob because of the blessing wherewith his father blessed him: and Esau said in his heart, The days of mourning for my father are at hand; then will I slay my brother Jacob.” He made up his mind from young to kill Jacob, and that thought has continued from generation to generation. It started with Cain and Abel, for Esau is Cain regenerated. That is the perpetual hatred.

“For it was a cursed seed from the beginning; neither didst thou for fear of any man give them pardon”. There is no pardon and no grace for Esau. His neck is on the chopping block, and the judgment coming to America will not change however much they jump, yell and shout. This land is Esau’s kingdom and we are just living in it, so do not set your affection on it.

precepts.why:
“For the worshipping of idols not to be named is the beginning, the cause, and the end, of all evil.” Understand that idolatry is not only bowing to a statue. Idolatry is going into your stubbornness, your bullheadedness, and your disdain for God’s commandments. Setting your own will above the commandments is the beginning, the cause and the end of all evil.

So Paul gives the answer to it: “Wherefore, my dearly beloved, flee from idolatry.” Do what? Flee from idolatry. Do not stand there and bargain with it; run from it.

This comes as the Lord promises to gather his people: “I will save my people from the east country, and from the west country”, and bring them to dwell in the midst of Jerusalem, “and they shall be my people, and I will be their God, in truth and in righteousness.” The twelve tribes scattered over here until the time of restoration have to flee their idols, their stubbornness and their disdain for the law, to be that people.

precepts.label: Sirach 30:12
precepts.why:
The Lord clothed us and named us, yet even in 2026 our people are still worshiping the devil, giving gifts to the sea goddess. And we wonder why America is going down there stealing presidents, starving people out and destabilizing countries. “A stubborn heart shall fare evil at the last; and he that loveth danger shall perish therein.” We have to prophesy against the idolatry and come up out of this foolishness: Christmas, Valentine’s Day, which a lot of our people celebrated. That has nothing to do with us. God did not give that to us.

Sirach shows where stubbornness is dealt with: “Bow down his neck while he is young, and beat him on the sides while he is a child, lest he wax stubborn, and be disobedient unto thee, and so bring sorrow to thine heart.”

That is why we teach God’s laws the way we do. We are not going to the left or to the right with any of you. We are not playing games, because we know why we got over here. We know how we got here: through stubbornness. So if we want to be delivered, we have to wake up.

Judges shows how Israel gets down: “when the judge was dead, that they returned, and corrupted themselves more than their fathers, in following other gods to serve them”, and “they ceased not from their own doings, nor from their stubborn way.” When there is no leader in place, when the officer, the captain, the deacon or the bishop isn’t there, they go back to their lonesome. If you cannot uphold righteousness when nobody is looking, that is your future: damnation, judgment, destruction. A stubborn heart shall fare evil at the last.

classes.title: The Pride Of Thine Heart

precepts.label: Psalms 100:3
precepts.why:
“Pride was not made for men, nor furious anger for them that are born of a woman.” Pride, arrogance, disdain, the inability to admit fault, the inflated ego: God said it wasn't made for you. You are nothing but dust that shall return to where it came from. And anger doesn't get you anywhere either; it holds you back and stunts your growth.

Why wasn't pride made for us? “Know ye that the Lord he is God: it is he that hath made us, and not we ourselves”. You didn't put one finger on your hand. You didn't put the knee bone with the hip bone and the leg bone. All of that belongs to God, the Creator, from way back when he said, Let us make man in our image.

He didn't consult you: where should I put the knee? How high up on the leg should it go? What should the arch of the foot look like? What skin tone should I give them? What should I make their hair like? None of us were included in that conversation.

So pride has no ground to stand on. The one who did not make himself cannot be proud before the one who made him. That is why the beginning of pride is turning away from your Maker.

precepts.label: Ecclesiastes 11:5
precepts.why:
“As thou knowest not what is the way of the spirit”: you don't know how the spirit was even made, and the body doesn't function without a spirit in it. We say someone is soulless, and it may be jacked up and crooked like the Esau in them, but that body isn't walking around with nothing in it. This is not a movie where they clone you and you come back with no soul, or a vampire who lives forever and can't see his reflection. There is a spirit in all of us, and the Most High made that.

“nor how the bones do grow in the womb of her that is with child”. Science tries to explain it the best way it can, by the mitochondria and this and that, but they don't know what God did to make it. Science is God giving man some sense of his mastery, and man takes it and says, I can do better than God: let me put this rod on you as a woman, let me cut yours off. That's why the Bible warns us to beware of science that opposes God.

“even so thou knowest not the works of God who maketh all.” So why is earth and ashes proud? Man does not even know how he himself was made; pride was not made for men.

precepts.label: Ecclesiastes 12:7
precepts.why:
Solomon mentions that spirit again: “Then shall the dust return to the earth as it was: and the spirit shall return unto God who gave it.”

The body goes back to the dust it came from, and the spirit goes back to God who made it. All of this, the dust and the spirit, belongs to the Most High God. That is why pride is not made for us.

Sirach asks, “Why is earth and ashes proud?” and says that when a man is dead “he shall inherit creeping things, beasts, and worms.” The man who is today a king tomorrow shall die. Neither the body nor the spirit is ours to boast in: one returns to the earth, the other to its Maker. So the beginning of pride, departing from God and turning the heart away from the Maker, is turning away from the very one the spirit must return to.

precepts.label: 1 Corinthians 6:20
precepts.why:
“For ye are bought with a price: therefore glorify God in your body, and in your spirit, which are God’s.” That is who your body belongs to.

This isn't something the young ones usually fight with. It's us, as we get older, who start smelling ourselves: I'm going to do this, this is what I want to do. We forget that at the end of the day we are still the children of the Most High God. You don't get to tell him what you are going to do with that body. The way parents look at their son and say, you'll always be my baby, even at forty-seven with gray hair: apply that to your life with God.

You have to keep these commandments, because he is still your Father and that is what he said to do. And that is the beginning of pride in Sirach 10: “when one departeth from God, and his heart is turned away from his Maker.” As we get older we start thinking we can decide whether to serve God or obey our Father, and that is pride. Pride is the beginning of sin; don't tell yourself you have a good heart while you depart from his commandments. Pride is hateful before God, and what he hates has an expiration date.

precepts.label: 2 Maccabees 6:1-2
precepts.why:
The book of Sirach was written by Jesus the son of Sirach, a wise man, around 200 to 175 BC. That is the Greek time period, and the book was written to help fight against Greek influence in the time it was written. So when Sirach speaks of “They that sit upon the mountain of Samaria”, the question is who, during the time of the Greeks, sat upon the mountain of Samaria. Second Maccabees answers it.

“Not long after this the king sent an old man of Athens to compel the Jews to depart from the laws of their fathers, and not to live after the laws of God”. That is the Greek king commanding Judah to depart from the laws of our God and serve the Greek laws and the Greek fashions instead. This is called assimilation, integration, Hellenization: we became Greeks, Greek citizens, like African Americans today. Same thing.

“And to pollute also the temple in Jerusalem, and to call it the temple of Jupiter Olympius”. The Greeks polluted the temple in Jerusalem, in Judah, and called it the temple of Zeus, for Jupiter is Zeus. “And that in Garizim, of Jupiter the Defender of strangers, as they did desire that dwelt in the place.” Garizim is a mount in Samaria. The Greeks built and sat upon Mount Garizim.

So who sat upon the mount in Samaria at this time? The Greeks. Other translations of Sirach 50:26 call them Edomites, verbatim: Edomites that sat upon Samaria. Then Sirach is telling you the Greeks were Edomites.

The rest of the verse follows: “they that dwell among the Philistines” are the Hamites, and “that foolish people that dwell in Sichem” is the northern kingdom, the silly nation that loved the heathen, the not a people of Deuteronomy 32. It is always them trying to take our land. This is war.

thread.text: Now Judas had heard of the the Romans, that they were mighty and valiant men, and such as would lovingly accept all that joined themselves unto them, and make a league of amity with all that came unto them;

classes.title: Raising Cain: The Son of Perdition, Merchants, and Captive Nations

precepts.label: Hosea 8:4
precepts.why:
Judas heard of the Romans, “that they were mighty and valiant men”, and that “by their policy and patience they had conquered all the place”. With their friends they “kept amity”, but whom they would help to a kingdom, those reigned, and whom they would, they displaced. Hosea shows Israel doing the very thing: “They have set up kings, but not by me: they have made princes, and I knew it not”.

Ephraim, the northern kingdom, did the same with Assyria and with Egypt. We were always trying to go to other countries to get leverage, never realizing that all we had to do was return to God, reunite with the southern kingdom, keep God's commandments the way they were given, and be one people.

Those same tendencies are here to this day. When the United States became a world power it did what Rome did. Rome trained proxy rulers, like Herod, an Edomite set as ruler over us in Israel; America trains proxy militaries and governments through the School of the Americas, renamed the Western Hemisphere Institute for Security Cooperation, and removes the leaders who resist. That is how they made princes: they trained the Jasons, the ungodly wretches who turned against their own people, the dictators of the northern kingdom countries of Latin America.

Then: “of their silver and their gold have they made them idols, that they may be cut off.” They traded their resources and leveraged what they had to put these people in front of them. Whom they would help, they helped; whom they would weaken, they weakened; whom they would remove, they removed. That sums up the School of the Americas, and the 56 interventions in Latin America: the spirit of Cain coming through Esau, from Rome to America.

thread.label: 1 Maccabees 8:13
thread.text: Also that, whom they would help to a kingdom, those reign; and whom again they would, they displace: finally, that they were greatly exalted:

classes.title: Zionism in the Face of Syria & Hezbollah

precepts.label: 1 Maccabees 8:24-29
precepts.why:
Rome was such “that, whom they would help to a kingdom, those reign; and whom again they would, they displace”: this is where America got the idea of the coup, of destabilizing countries. Judas Maccabeus was catching so much hell from the Greeks that he went to Rome for help, and these are the articles Rome gave him.

“If there come first any war upon the Romans or any of their confederates throughout all their dominion, The people of the Jews shall help them, as the time shall be appointed, with all their heart: Neither shall they give any thing unto them that make war upon them, or aid them with victuals, weapons, money, or ships, as it hath seemed good unto the Romans”. No food, no weapons, no money, no ships to the other side. Today that is called a sanction. That is why they cut Cuba off and forbid all countries to help Cuba; that is why America told the Caribbean, get rid of the Cuban doctors or we cut off your food supply, and the Caribbean said, we need you, but you have to go.

“In the same manner also, if war come first upon the nation of the Jews, the Romans shall help them with all their heart”: America will help you with all their heart, as long as you are theirs. “According to these articles did the Romans make a covenant with the people of the Jews.” It is the same today: America makes articles with countries, and this is where they got it from.

So when you hear about rebel forces, ask where the money and weapons come from: America, Britain, France or Israel, always one of these European powers. The new president of Syria was an al-Qaeda rebel commander with a $10 million bounty on his head, cleaned up and given a haircut. Out of a country of millions, two or three hundred disgruntled people are given money and promises to overthrow the government. Whom they would, they displace.

precepts.label: Romans 9:6
precepts.why:
“Then came ungodly persons, who hated their own people, went unto the king, and told him that Jonathan besieged the tower”. You have to hate your own people to betray them. That is the young man in the red MAGA hat who said he would deport his own parents for not having Esau's paperwork. That paperwork means nothing; the earth belongs to us, and our paperwork is the Bible.

How can one of our own do that? Paul answers: “Not as though the word of God hath taken none effect. For they are not all Israel, which are of Israel”. The word of God is not going to fail; it has not failed. But they are not all Israel which are of Israel.

Just because somebody looks like you, speaks the same language as you and eats the same foods as you does not mean they are of your people. We have to be aware of this.

Esau in his witchcraft tells our young men, join the military, you will explore and experience the world, your family will be good, we will give you college tuition. What he does not tell you is that you have to go to the countries of your people and oppress them and kill them. Poor whites and mainly poor blacks and Latinos go out in Esau's military and kill people who look just like them: in Panama, Venezuela, the Dominican Republic, Nicaragua, Libya, Iraq. They are going to rat us out; our own people who hate us will betray us, as they did Jonathan.

precepts.label: Matthew 24:12
precepts.why:
Christ said it would come to this: “And because iniquity shall abound, the love of many shall wax cold.” Because sin shall abound, the love of many shall wax cold: emotionless, no empathy, no feelings for your people, not even for your parents. That is what we are seeing in the ungodly persons who hate their own people and go to the king to betray them.

If they are doing that now, imagine when we are making noise. They are already passing laws and putting a media blackout on us. It is going to get to such a level that they will want to put us to death, thinking they are doing good and saving the people.

But it is only betrayal, and their salvation in Esau's kingdom is only for a moment. There is a judgment for betraying your people. Look at Judas, the main betrayer: he betrayed Christ for thirty pieces of silver, and he killed himself, because he knew what he did was evil. The red MAGA hat gives you no superpowers. It does not hide your brown skin or your black skin; it just makes you look more and more like a clown, like a traitor.

classes.title: The Pride Of Thine Heart

precepts.label: Acts 12:21-23
precepts.why:
Cyrus the Persian humbled himself and let all Israel go, and God said, you can rule. But the Greek Antiochus “had spoken proudly”, saying “he would come to Jerusalem and make it a common burying place of the Jews.” As soon as he spoke those proud words, “a pain of the bowels that was remediless came upon him, and sore torments of the inner parts”, and that most justly, because he had tormented other men’s bowels. He fell from his chariot, rotted until he could not abide his own smell, and finally said “It is meet to be subject unto God, and that a man that is mortal should not proudly think of himself if he were God.”

It did not stop with the Greeks. Now we come down to the Romans, because that is what Herod was: “And upon a set day Herod, arrayed in royal apparel, sat upon his throne, and made an oration unto them. And the people gave a shout, saying, It is the voice of a god, and not of a man.”

Black folk always think the white man is God, and God always has to remind you who he is. “And immediately the angel of the Lord smote him, because he gave not God the glory: and he was eaten of worms, and gave up the ghost.” Antiochus rotted with worms rising out of his body; Herod was eaten of worms. The same judgment for the same pride.

Pride destroyed them. All kingdoms fall because of pride, and nobody is exempt: Assyria, Babylon, Greece, Rome, America. That is the judgment for it. So check yourself before you wreck yourself: a man that is mortal must not think of himself as if he were God.
